1125.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Nothing happens outside you, (O God). Making (all things), you watch over them, and you yourself know their state. What can one say? Nothing can be said. Whatever there is, all is your will. Whatever is to be done rests with you; before whom (else) should a prayer be made? (Our) speaking and hearing is your word (of praise) alone. You yourself know (all), O Lord of every wonder. (God) himself does, causes to be done, and knows; O Nanak, setting up and pulling down, he watches over (all). ॥4॥
Chaupade (chau, four; pad, stanza): hymns of four stanzas.
1125.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Through the Guru's Shabad (the Word) countless sages have crossed over; Indra and his like, Brahma and his like, have crossed over. Sanak, Sanandan and countless ascetics have reached the far shore by the Guru's grace. Without the Shabad, how can the world-ocean be crossed? Without the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) the world is gripped by disease; in double-mindedness one drowns and drowns, and dies. The Guru is the Divine; the Guru is the unseen, the unfathomable (Lord); in the Guru's service lies the understanding of the three worlds. The Guru, the Giver, himself bestowed the gift, and the unseen, unfathomable (Lord) was found. The mind is king: the mind has been won over by the mind itself, and desire has merged in the mind. The mind is the yogi (joined to God); the mind, going to ruin, is the one separated (from him); the mind, when it understands, sings (his) praises. Those who through the Guru have subdued the mind and reflected on the Shabad are rare in the world. O Nanak, the Master pervades and fills (all); through the true Shabad comes deliverance. ॥4॥
Sanak and his brothers: Sanak, Sanandan, Sanatan and Sanat Kumar, in the Puranas the four sons of Brahma, sages held to remain children for ever.
1125.3: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). There is no sight in the eyes, the body is wasted; old age has conquered (you), and death (stands) over (your) head. Beauty, colour and gladness do not last; how will the net of Jam (the messenger of Death) let (you) go? O mortal, repeat (the Name of) the Lord: (your) life is slipping away. Without the true Shabad you will never be released; (your) life has been in vain. In the body are lust, anger, ego and possessiveness; (their) pain is hard and very heavy. Through the Guru, repeat (the Name of) Ram (the Lord), and savour (its) taste with the tongue; in this way, swim, and cross over. The ears are deaf, the intellect has grown shallow, (yet you) have not understood the Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) of the Shabad. The manmukh (the self-willed) has gambled away the treasure of (human) life; without the Guru the blind one has not seen. He who stays unattached, free of hope among hopes, a renunciant in the meditation of Sahaj, Nanak humbly prays: (that one) is released through the Guru, his loving attention fixed on the Name of Ram. ॥4॥
1126.1: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (In old age) the gait is clumsy, the feet and hands give way, the skin of the body has withered; the eyes are misted, the ears have gone deaf; (yet) the manmukh has not known the Naam. O blind one, what have you gained by coming into the world? Ram is not in (your) heart, nor the Guru's service; you are leaving, having lost (even your) capital. The tongue is not dyed in the Lord's love; whenever it speaks, (its words are) insipid. Caught up in slandering the Sants (saints), (such people) have become beasts; they never become good. Only a rare one has tasted the Amrit (the nectar that gives spiritual life), (one whom the Lord) has brought into union with the True Guru. As long as the secret of the Shabad has not come (to one), so long does death torment (him). He who never knows another's door or house, (only) the one door of the True One, by the Guru's grace he has attained the supreme state: so Nanak says, having reflected. ॥4॥
1126.2: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). All night you sleep, a noose around your neck; the day you have wasted in entanglements. Not for an instant, a moment, a little while have you known God, who created this world. O mind, how will you escape (this) heavy pain? What did you bring, and what will you take away? Repeat (the Name of) Ram: (that alone) does good. The manmukh's (heart-)lotus is upside down, (his) understanding shallow; because of the blind mind, worldly affairs (ride) on his head. Death and birth hang ever over your head; without the Name the noose is around (your) neck. The gait totters, and the eyes too are blind; (yet) attention to the Shabad has not pleased (you). (Reading) the Shastras and the Vedas, (one) is still in Maya (the world's illusion and lure) of the three qualities; the blind one toils only at worldly affairs. You have lost the capital: where will you find profit, O evil-minded one, empty of wisdom? Those who, reflecting on the Shabad, have tasted the delight of Ram, O Nanak, are content in the True One. ॥4॥
The three qualities (gunas) of Maya: rajas, sattva and tamas, under which all deeds are done.
1126.3: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (He who) stays with the Guru day and night, (keeps) Ram on (his) tongue, and is dyed in (his) love, who knows no other, recognises the Shabad, and has known and recognised (the Lord) within — such a servant is pleasing to my mind, who, subduing his self, is dyed in the Infinite and does the work (the Guru gives him). Within and without is the Being, Niranjan, free of the stain of Maya; to that primal Being, (my) salutation. Within each and every heart, and in all without a break, the One whose form is true is pervading. Those dyed in the True One have the true Amrit on (their) tongue, and not a mustard seed's worth of the filth of falsehood. They have tasted the pure Naam, the delight of Amrit; dyed in the Shabad, they have won honour. The virtuous, meeting the virtuous, earns the profit; through the Guru, in the Naam, (he finds) glory. All sorrows are erased through the Guru's service; O Nanak, the Naam (becomes his) companion. ॥4॥
1127.1: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). To hold the Naam in the heart is all wealth and support; it is obtained by the Guru's grace. Through this undying treasure one is fulfilled, and in the meditation of Sahaj one is attuned (to the Lord) in love. O mind, one should fix one's thought on the devotion of Ram. Through the Guru, repeat the Name of Ram in the heart: (so) one reaches (one's true) home in Sahaj. Doubt, separation (from God) and fear are never shed; coming and going (in births), (one) does not understand. Without the Lord's Name no one finds liberation; (such people) drown and die without water. Busy with worldly affairs, you will lose all honour, O fool, and (your) doubt will not be erased. Without the Guru's Shabad there is never liberation, O blind one; (there is only) the sprawl of worldly affairs. (He whose) mind is at one with the Stainless One, who has no lineage, (his) mind has died through the mind itself; within and without he has known the One alone; O Nanak, (for him) there is no other, no second. ॥4॥
1127.2: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). With sacrifices, fire offerings, charity, austerities and worship, the body (still) suffers and ever endures pain; without the Name of Ram (no one) finds liberation; through the Guru one obtains liberation in the Naam. Without the Name of Ram, birth in the world is in vain. (One) eats poison and speaks words of poison; without the Name (he) dies fruitless and wanders (in births). (The pandit) expounds books, their recitation and grammar, and performs the sandhya rites at the three times of day; (but) O mortal, where is liberation without the Guru's Shabad? Without the Name of Ram (he) dies entangled. (Taking up) the staff and water-pot, the topknot, the sacred thread and the loincloth, (one) journeys to places of pilgrimage and wanders far and wide; (but) without the Name of Ram peace does not come; he who repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har, crosses over. (One) makes a crown of matted hair, smears ashes on the body, and leaving off clothes goes naked; (but) without the Name of Ram there is no fulfilment; for one bound by his past deeds, (all this) is but a garb. However many beings and creatures dwell in water, on land and in the sky, you, (O God), are everywhere, in every being. By the Guru's grace, save your servant: Nanak has drunk the Lord's delight, savouring it. ॥5॥
1127.3: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Let no one take pride in (high) caste. He who knows Brahm (God) is a Brahmin. Do not take pride in caste, you foolish, ignorant one: from this pride many evils spring. Everyone speaks of the four varnas (castes); (yet) all creation has come from the (one) seed of Brahm. The whole world is one clay; the Potter shapes (from it) vessels of many kinds. The five elements join to make the form of the body; who can reckon (them) less (in one) or more (in another)? Says Nanak, this soul is bound by (its) deeds; without meeting the True Guru, (it) is not set free. ॥5॥
Brahmin, Khatri (Kshatriya), Vaish and Shudra are the four varnas.
1128.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Yogis, householders, pandits and the wearers of (religious) garbs: these are asleep, (each) in his own pride. Drunk with the wine of Maya, (the soul) lies asleep; (he who) stays awake is robbed by no one. He alone is awake who meets the True Guru; he brings the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) under (his) control. He alone is awake who reflects on the Essence; he dies (to himself) and does not kill others. He alone is awake who knows the One; he leaves prakriti (the world of Maya) and recognises the Essence. Whoever of the four varnas is awake is released from Jam, from death. Says Nanak, that servant is awake in whose eyes is the collyrium of (divine) wisdom. ॥6॥
1128.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). He whom (God) keeps in his refuge clings to the True One and obtains the true fruit. O people, to whom (else) do you cry out? By (his) Hukam (God's will and command) (all) came to be; by (his) Hukam (all) takes its course. This (visible) form (of the world) is upheld by you, (O God); in an instant it perishes, and (you) take no time to make (it). (He to whom God) in his grace has shown (the world as) a play has attained the supreme state by the Guru's grace. Says Nanak, he (alone) kills and brings back to life; understand (it) so, and let no one stray in doubt. ॥4॥
1128.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). I am the bride; the Creator is my Husband; as he makes me do, so is the adornment I put on. When it pleases him, he takes his delight (in me); (my) body and mind are for the True Master (alone). What praise or slander can anyone offer, when he, the One, is himself at work (in all)? By the Guru's grace, (I feel) the pull of love; I shall meet the Merciful One, sounding the five Shabads (sounds). Says Nanak, what can anyone do (against one) whom he himself unites (with himself)? ॥4॥
The five Shabads (sounds): the music of the five kinds of instrument (strings, metal, wind, skin drums and pots), an image of full joy.
1128.4: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). He alone is a muni (a silent sage) who kills the double-mindedness of the mind, and, having killed double-mindedness, reflects on Brahm. Let someone search out this mind, O brother: searching the mind, the Naam, the nine treasures, is found. Making attachment the root, the Creator brought forth the world; attaching (it) to possessiveness, he led (it) astray in doubt. From this mind (come) all bodies and breath; through the mind's reflection, understanding the Hukam, (one) merges (in God). (When God's) grace comes, the Guru shows mercy; (then) this mind awakens, and the double-mindedness of this mind dies. The mind's (true) nature is (that of) the ever-detached One, who dwells in all, beyond (Maya), without attachment. Says Nanak, he who knows this secret (becomes one with) the primal Being, the Stainless, the Divine. ॥6॥
1129.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Name of Ram is the deliverance of the world; it carries (one) over the world-ocean to the far shore. By the Guru's grace, cherish the Lord's Name (in your heart); it keeps faith with you for ever. The foolish manmukhs do not keep the Naam in mind; without the Name, how will they reach the far shore? The Giver himself bestows the gift; all praise to the One who gives. (On whom God) casts his glance of grace, (him) he unites with the True Guru; O Nanak, (and) he makes the Naam dwell in (his) heart. ॥4॥
1129.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). As many as there are in the worlds, all have been saved through the Naam alone — those who receive it through the Guru. (On whom) the dear Lord bestows his grace, (him) he gives, through the Guru, the glory of the Naam. Those who hold the Name of Ram in love and affection are saved themselves, and (each) becomes the saviour of all (his) families. Without the Name the manmukhs go to the city of Jam; they are in torment and suffer blows. (When) he, the Creator, himself gives, O Nanak, (then) the Naam is received. ॥4॥
1129.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Love of Govind carried Sanak and his brothers across; through the Shabad they reflected on the Name of Ram. O dear Lord, bestow your grace (on me), (that) through the Guru love for the Naam alone may take hold (of me). When there is love within, and true devotion, (then) union (with God) comes through the perfect Guru. (Such a one) dwells in his own home, in Sahaj and in love; through the Guru, the Naam comes to dwell in the mind. The Seer himself watches over (all); O Nanak, keep the Naam enshrined in (your) heart. ॥4॥
1129.4: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In Kalyug, enshrine the Name of Ram in (your) heart; without the Name, (one) only puts ashes on (one's own) forehead. The Name of Ram is hard to obtain, O brother; it comes to dwell in the mind by the Guru's grace. The servants who seek that Name of Ram receive it from the perfect Guru. The servants who accept the Lord's will are approved; through the Guru's Shabad (they bear) the mark of the Naam. Serve him who upholds (all) by his power; O Nanak, through the Guru, love the Naam. ॥4॥
Kalyug: in the reckoning of the Puranas, the fourth and darkest of the world's four ages, held to be the present one.
1129.5: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In Kalyug (people) perform many rites; (but) it is not their season, nor are the rites accepted. In Kalyug the Name of Ram is the essence (of all); through the Guru, true love (for it) takes hold. Searching body and mind, he has found (God) in (his own) house, who through the Guru has fixed (his) thought on the Name of Ram. The collyrium of (divine) wisdom comes from the True Guru; (then) the Name of Ram (is seen) pervading the three worlds. In Kalyug (it is the season of) the one dear Lord alone; there is no other season. O Nanak, through the Guru, make the Name of Ram take root in (your) heart. ॥4॥
1130.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The manmukhs are gripped by the disease of double-mindedness; they burn greatly in craving. Dying again and again they are born, and find no resting place; (they have) wasted (their) life in vain. O my Beloved, be merciful and grant (me) understanding. The world has been made sick with Haumai (ego); without the Shabad the sickness does not go. Countless sages read the Simritis and the Shastras, (but) without the Shabad (true) awareness is not gained. All who live in the three qualities are gripped by the disease; possessiveness has robbed (them of) awareness. Some God himself has drawn out (of it); God himself has set (them) to the Guru's service. They have found the treasure of the Lord's Name, and peace has come to dwell in (their) minds. The Gurmukhs (those who follow the Guru) live in the fourth state; they have found a dwelling in their own home. The perfect True Guru has shown (them) mercy, and (they) have rid themselves of self from within. Over every head is the command of the One alone, who created Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra (Shiv); O Nanak, the One alone is unmoving and true; he neither dies nor is born. ॥5॥
The Simritis are the Hindu books of conduct and law, the Shastras the books of the six schools of philosophy.
The fourth state (turiya): the spiritual state beyond Maya's three qualities.
1130.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The manmukh, in double-mindedness, is ever sick; the whole world is sick. The Gurmukhs understand (this), and rid themselves of the sickness by reflecting on the Guru's Shabad. O dear Lord, unite (me) with the Sat Sangat (the company of the true). O Nanak, (the Lord) gives glory to him who fixes (his) thought on the Name of Ram. Through possessiveness all are gripped by the disease of death; Jam's rule is over their heads. Jam does not come near the Gurmukh mortals who keep the Lord enshrined in their hearts. Those who have not known the Lord's Name through the Guru, why did they come into the world? They never did the Guru's service; they wasted (their) life in vain. O Nanak, those whom (the Lord) has set to the True Guru's service are perfect and greatly fortunate; whatever they wish, that fruit they obtain; through Gurbani (one) finds peace. ॥4॥
1130.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (The manmukh) is born in pain, dies in pain, and in pain goes about (his) work; he never escapes the womb and the cycle of births; he stays sunk in filth. Cursed, cursed is the manmukh: he has squandered (his) life; he did not serve the perfect Guru, nor was the Lord's Name pleasing (to him). The Guru's Shabad takes away every disease of the one whom the dear Lord joins (to it). Through the Naam, in the Naam alone, glory comes to the one in whose mind (the Lord) makes (it) dwell. When the True Guru is met, then (one) obtains the fruit: true living, the essence of peace. Pure are the servants who cling to the Lord and set (their) love on the Lord's Name. Should I find the dust (of the feet) of those who have meditated on the perfect True Guru, I would put it on (my) forehead. O Nanak, the dust of those who have fixed (their) thought on the Name of Ram is found by perfect fortune. ॥4॥
1131.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The servant who reflects on the Shabad is true; those in whose hearts that True One (dwells) (and who) practise true devotion day and night — then no pain (touches their) body. Everyone talks of the devotee, the devotee; (but) without serving the True Guru, devotion is not found; that God is met by perfect fortune. The manmukhs lose (their) capital and ask for gain; where can any gain or profit come from? Jam, Death, stands ever over (their) heads; in the love of another, (they) have lost (their) honour. In many garbs (people) roam day and night, (but) the disease of Haumai does not go. Reading and reading, they wrangle and dispute; joined to Maya, (they) have lost (their) awareness. Those who serve the True Guru attain the supreme state; through the Naam (they) receive glory. O Nanak, those in whose minds the Naam has come to dwell have won honour at the True One's door. ॥4॥
1131.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The manmukh's hope never leaves (him); in the love of another (he) comes to ruin. Like a river, (his) belly is never filled; the fire of craving burns him away. Those dyed in the delight of Ram are ever in bliss. The Naam is in (their) hearts, double-mindedness has fled from (their) minds; drinking the Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, (they) are satisfied. The Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), who fashioned the creation, himself sets each and every one to (his) task; he who himself made attachment to Maya himself sets (beings) on (the love of) another. If there were a second, something could be said to that one; (O God,) all are merged in you. (He who) through the Guru has reflected on the essence of (divine) wisdom, (God) merges (his) light in the Light. That God is true, true for ever; true is the whole of (his) visible form. O Nanak, the True Guru has given (this) understanding: through the True Name comes deliverance. ॥4॥
1131.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In Kalyug those who have not recognised Ram are ghosts; in Satjug those who reflected (on him) were Param Hans (supreme swans); in Duapar and Treta (too such) humans live; a rare one has subdued Haumai. In Kalyug, glory (comes) through the Name of Ram. In every age the Gurmukh has known the One; without the Name, liberation is not found. The true servant perceives the Naam in (his) heart; through the Guru, he enshrines it in (his) mind. Those who are attuned in love to the Name of Ram have crossed over, and carried across all (their) families too. My God is the giver of virtue; through the Shabad he burns away faults. The servants in whose minds (he) has come to dwell are beautiful; (they) have enshrined the Naam in (their) hearts. (He to whom) the True Guru has shown (the Lord's) home, door and mansion delights in (his) love; whatever (the Guru) says, he accepts as good; O Nanak, he utters the Naam. ॥4॥
Satjug, Treta and Duapar: in the reckoning of the Puranas, the three ages before Kalyug.
1132.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Merge the mind's desire back into the mind, by reflecting on the Guru's Shabad. (He who) gains understanding from the perfect Guru does not die again and again. O my mind, the Name of Ram is (your) support; (he who takes it), by the Guru's grace, has attained the supreme state; (the Lord) is the fulfiller of every wish. The One alone pervades all; without the Guru, this is not understood. (He in whom) my Lord God has been revealed through the Guru sings the Lord's praises night and day. The Lord alone is the giver of peace; elsewhere (people) find no peace. Those who have not served the True Guru, the Giver, go at the last, repenting. (He who), serving the True Guru, has found lasting peace: pain does not rush upon (him) again. O Nanak, (he) has received the Lord's devotion; (his) light merges in the Light. ॥4॥
1132.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Without the Guru the world has gone mad; gone astray, it suffers blows. Dying again and again it is born, ever in pain; it finds no word of (the Lord's) door. O my mind, ever remain in the True Guru's refuge. (so) the Lord's Name feels ever sweet in the heart, and by the Guru's Shabad the world-ocean is crossed. (One) puts on many garbs, (but his) mind wavers; within are lust, anger and pride. Within is thirst and very great hunger; he goes barking from door to door. Those who die through the Guru's Shabad and then live find liberation at (the Lord's) door. Within (them) is calm, and lasting peace, (for they) keep the Lord enshrined in (their) hearts. As it pleases him, so he makes (beings) walk; nothing (else) can be done. O Nanak, through the Guru (one) cherishes the Shabad, (and finds) glory in the Name of Ram. ॥4॥
1132.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Haumai and attachment to Maya have led (the manmukh) astray; he earns pain and eats pain. Within is greed, (like) rabies, a heavy affliction; without discernment he wanders. Cursed is the manmukh's life in the world; not even in a dream has he called the Name of Ram to mind; never does he come to love the Lord. He does the deeds of beasts and does not understand; he practises falsehood and becomes false. If the True Guru is met, (his mind) is turned around; some rare servant searches and finds (the Lord). (He in whose) heart the Name of the Lord, Har Har, ever dwells has found the treasure of virtues; by the Guru's grace he has found the Perfect One, and the pride of (his) mind is ended. The Creator himself does and causes (all) to be done; he himself sets (one) on the path; he himself gives glory through the Guru; O Nanak, (such a one) merges in the Naam. ॥4॥
1133.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Write on my tablet (the Name of) Hari, Govind, Gopal. In the love of another, (people) are caught in Jam's net. The True Guru cherishes and keeps me; the Lord, the giver of peace, is with me. By the Guru's teaching Prahlad utters (the Name of) the Lord; the child does not worry over punishment. His mother counsels (him): O dear Prahlad, son, give up the Name of Ram, and save your life. Prahlad says: Listen, O my mother, I will not give up the Name of Ram; the Guru has made me understand (it). Sanda, Marka and all the rest went and complained: Prahlad has gone astray himself, and has led all the pupils astray. In the assembly of the wicked a plot was settled; (but) the Lord, Raghurai, becomes Prahlad's protector. (Harnakhash) rushed (at him), sword in hand, in great pride: Where is your Lord, who would save you? In an instant a fearsome form came forth, tearing the pillar open; (the Lord) tore Harnakhash apart with his claws, and saved Prahlad. The dear Lord brings the tasks of the Sants to good; he saved twenty-one generations of his servant Prahlad. Through the Guru's Shabad (he) kills the poison of Haumai; O Nanak, through the Name of Ram (he) carries the Sants across. ॥5॥

Prahlad was the son of the demon king Harnakhash (Hiranyakashipu) and held to devotion to God through all his father's torments; in the Puranas, God took the form of Narasimha, the Man-Lion, and killed Harnakhash. Sanda and Marka (Amarka) were Prahlad's teachers.
Raghurai: the king of the line of Raghu, Rama; in Gurbani, a name of the one God.
1133.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (God) himself sets demons upon the Sants, and he himself is (their) protector. (O God,) those who are ever in your refuge have no pain in their minds. In every age (the Lord) has kept (the honour) of his devotees. The demon's son Prahlad knows nothing of the Gayatri or of tarpan; through the Shabad (the Lord) has united him in union with himself. (The devotees) practise devotion at all hours, day and night; through the Shabad (they) have shed double-mindedness. Ever pure are those who are dyed in the True One; that True One dwells in (their) minds. The fools read (the lore of) double-mindedness and do not recognise the Root (of all); they have wasted their life in vain. They slander the Sants; (they) stirred up the wicked demon. Prahlad does not read (the lore of) double-mindedness, does not give up the Lord's Name, and is not frightened by anyone's threats. The dear Lord is the protector of the Sants; the demon's death drew near. (The Lord) himself keeps his own honour, and gives glory to the devotees. O Nanak, (the Lord) tore Harnakhash apart with his claws; the blind (demon) found no word of (the Lord's) door. ॥5॥
The Gayatri: the Rig Veda verse recited at the sandhya prayers; tarpan: offering water to the ancestors and the gods.
1133.3: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (The Lord) in his grace attaches (one) to the feet of the Sants, the Lord's servants; through the Guru's Shabad meditate on the Lord, and let (your) awareness merge (in him). O my mind, meditate on the Name of the Lord, Narayan. (He on whom) the Lord, Har Har, the giver of peace, shows his grace, (him) he carries across the world-ocean through the Guru, by the Lord's Name. Joining the company of the Saadh (the holy one), sing of the Lord; through the Guru's teaching take (the Name of) Ram, the home of all delights. Bathe in the pool of the Amrit wisdom of the Guru, the holy one; (so) all misdeeds and sins are destroyed. (O God,) you yourself are the Creator, and the universe rests on you; unite servant Nanak, the slave of your slaves, (with yourself). ॥4॥
1134.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Utter the Lord's Name; fruitful is that moment (when it is uttered); by the Guru's teaching all pains are dispelled. O my mind, meditate on the Name of the Lord, Narhari. (O God,) in your grace unite (me) with the perfect Guru, (that) in the company of the Sat Sangat (I) may cross the world-ocean. Meditate on the Life of the world, and in (your) mind remember the Lord; (he) dispels your sins, millions upon millions. (He on whose) face the dust (of the feet) of the Saadhs of the Sat Sangat has fallen has bathed at the sixty-eight (tiraths) and in the Sursari (the Ganga). The Lord has shown his grace to me, a fool; the Lord who carries across has carried servant Nanak across. ॥4॥
Narhari (nar, man; hari, lion): Narasimha, the Man-Lion in whose form, in the Puranas, God saved Prahlad; in Gurbani, a name of God.
The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage: the tiraths held most holy in India.
1134.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Doing good deeds is the best (of all things), (and it is) the rosary; turn it in (your) heart, and it will go along with you. Repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Banwali. (O God,) in your grace unite (us) with the Sat Sangat, (where) the noose of Maya, the noose of Jam, is broken. He who has given himself to the toil of service, through the Guru: for him the Shabad is fashioned in the true mint. The Lord is beyond reach, beyond the senses; the Guru has shown (him) the One beyond reach; searching within the city of the body, (he) has found the Lord. We are children, the Lord is the father who cherishes (us); with your glance of grace carry servant Nanak across. ॥4॥
Banwali, Banwari (wearer of the garland of forest flowers, a name of Krishna): in Gurbani, a name of God.
1134.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). All bodies are yours, and you are within them all; there is no one outside you. O my mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, the giver of peace. (O God,) I praise you; you are my Lord God, my father. Wherever I look, there is that Lord God; all is in your power; there is no other at all. He whom it pleases you to protect, O Lord: no one goes near him. (O God,) you fill the water, the land and the sky; you are in all. O servant Nanak, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, ever present, right before (you). ॥4॥
1134.4: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The Lord's Sant, in whose heart is the Name of the Lord, Murari, is the Lord's own image. He on whose forehead (such) destiny is written cherishes the Lord's Name in his heart, through the Guru's teaching. One should repeat (the Name of) Madhusudan, enshrining (him) in the heart. In the city of the body are five restless thieves; the Lord, through the Guru's Shabad, has struck (them) down and driven (them) out. Those whose minds are at one with the Lord: the Lord himself brings their tasks to good. Their dependence on people is ended; the Lord, the Creator, has taken their side. Counsel and planning could be held only if anything were outside the Lord. Whatever (he) does, that alone will be good; meditate night and day on the Name of the Lord, Murari. Whatever the Lord does, he does it himself, by himself alone; he asks no one, and takes no one's counsel. O Nanak, one should ever meditate on that God who in his grace has brought (us) to the True Guru. ॥4॥
Murari (the foe of the demon Mur) and Madhusudan (the slayer of the demon Madhu): names of Vishnu; in Gurbani, names of God.
1135.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Lord, my Master, unite (me) with those Saadhs who have meditated (on you), (that) I may be liberated. Seeing the sight of them the mind blossoms; every moment I am a sacrifice to them. Repeat in (your) heart the Name of the Lord, Murari. Show grace, show grace, O Father of the world, my Master: make me the water-carrier of the slaves of (your) slaves. Excellent is their understanding, excellent their honour, in whose hearts Banwari dwells. Attach (me) to their service, O Lord, my Master; remembering them, may I be liberated. Those who have not found such a True Guru, the holy one, are beaten and driven out of the Lord's court. Those slanderers find no honour; the Creator has cut off their noses. The Lord himself makes (beings) speak, and himself speaks; the Lord himself is stainless, formless, needing no food. O Lord, he whom you unite (with yourself) will meet you; O servant Nanak, what (power) have these poor creatures? ॥4॥
1135.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). That alone is your Sat Sangat, O Lord, in which the Lord's praise is heard. Those who have heard the Lord's Name, and whose minds are drenched (in it): we ever serve their feet. Meditating on the Lord, the Life of the world, (one) crosses over. Many and countless are your Names, O Lord; with this tongue they cannot be counted. O Gursikhs, utter the Lord('s Name), sing of the Lord; taking the Guru's teaching, repeat (the Name of) the Lord. He who hears the Guru's teaching: that servant receives the Lord's abundant peace. Blessed is that lineage, blessed that father, blessed that mother, who gave birth to (such) servants. Those who have meditated on my Lord, Har Har, with every breath and every morsel, have become the Lord's servants in the true court. O Lord, Har Har, your Names are beyond reach; (you) have placed them within your devotees, O Lord. O Nanak, the servant who has received the understanding of the Guru's teaching crosses over, repeating (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
1136.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Setting all the (other) lunar days aside, (you say) Govind was born on the eighth lunar day. Men led astray by doubt talk nonsense; Narayan is beyond birth and death. Making panjiri, you feed it (to the idol) in secret; he is neither born nor does he die, O saakat, dull as cattle! You sing (the idol) lullabies, and in this lie all offences; burnt be the mouth with which (you) say the Master enters births. He is neither born nor dies, neither comes nor goes; Nanak's God pervades all. ॥4॥

The eighth lunar day (ashtami) of the dark half of Bhadon, Janmashtami, is kept as the birthday of Krishna; on it people make panjiri, a sweet, and offer it to the image, rock it in a cradle and sing it lullabies.
Saakat (Sanskrit shakta): a worshipper of Shakti (Maya); in Gurbani, one cut off from God and lost in Maya.
1136.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Rising, (one) is at peace; sitting, (one) is at peace; no fear touches (one), once (one) understands this: the One Master is our protector; he is the Knower of all hearts. (One) sleeps free of care, and wakes free of care: O God, you are present everywhere. (He) dwells in peace at home, and finds peace outside — Says Nanak, (the one in whom) the Guru has made the mantra (of the Name) firm. ॥3॥
1136.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I keep neither (Hindu) fasts nor (the fasts of) the month of Ramadan; I serve him who protects at the last. My (Lord) is the One, Gosain and Allah; (I) have settled my accounts with both Hindu and Turk. I go neither on Hajj to the Kaaba nor to worship at tiraths; I serve the One alone, and no other. I neither perform puja nor offer namaz; taking the One Formless Lord into (my) heart, I bow (to him). We are neither Hindu nor Muslim; (our) body and breath of life belong to Allah, to Ram. Says Kabir: this I have declared: meeting the Guru, the Pir, I have recognised my own Master. ॥5॥
Gosain (go-sain, master of the earth): a Hindu name of God.
This shabad is the Fifth Guru's, but its closing line names Kabir in place of Nanak: the Guru unfolds the thought of a shabad of Kabir's in this raag (ਹਮਰਾ ਝਗਰਾ ਰਹਾ ਨ ਕੋਊ).
1136.4: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In Sahaj (I) have bound and brought in the ten does; the five deer (I) have pierced with the arrows of the Word of Shiv, the Auspicious One. Taking the company of the Sants with me, I rode out to hunt; (I) caught the deer without horses or weapons. Bent on the hunt, (I) had come running outside; (but) I found the game in the village of (my own) home. Catching the deer, (I) brought them home, to the shop; (the Sants) shared them out and carried them off, bit by bit. This game has been given away as a gift; in Nanak's house is the Name alone. ॥4॥
The ten does: the ten senses, of perception and of action; the five deer: the five enemies, lust, anger and the rest.
1136.5: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Though (he) be fed (the Name) a hundred times with longing care, the Lord, Har Har, does not come into the saakat's mind. Take the counsel of the Sants; in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) attain the supreme state. Much water is poured over a stone, (yet) it is not soaked, and stays bone dry. The six Shastras are recited to a fool, as though the wind were blowing in the ten directions. As when a threshing floor without grain is threshed, so from the saakat no one gains anything. Each clings to that alone to which he has been attached; says Nanak, God has made this arrangement. ॥5॥
1137.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He who fashioned the soul, the life-breath and the body, he who created (beings) is the one who feels (their) pain. The Guru, Gobind, is the soul's help, whose shade (is over us) always, in this world and the next. To worship God in adoration is the pure way; in the Saadh Sangat the perverse bent is destroyed. Friends, well-wishers and wealth are no support (to the soul); blessed, blessed are you, my Narayan. Nanak speaks the Amrit Bani: know no other but the One. ॥4॥
1137.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ahead (of me) is the Merciful, behind (me) is Narayan; in the middle part is the Lord, the home of love's delights. God is, for us, the Shastra of omens; peace, Sahaj and bliss fill (our) house and home. Uttering the Naam with the tongue and hearing it with the ears, (they) have come alive; remembering, remembering God, (they) have become immortal and steadfast. (They) have dispelled the sorrows of birth after birth; the unstruck (Anhad) Shabad plays in (their inner) court. In his grace God has united with himself O Nanak, (those who) have come to God's refuge. ॥4॥
Anhad (anahata, unstruck): sound that rings without being struck, unbroken; in Gurbani, the Shabad of God's praise that resounds within without a break.
1137.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Millions of heart's desires come to hand; on the road of Jam, (the Name) is the traveller's companion. The Name of the Guru, of Gobind, is the (true) water of the Ganga. Whoever remembers it is liberated; drinking it, (one) wanders through births no more. (The Name is) worship, chanting, austerity and holy bathing; remembering the Name, (people) have become free of desire. (The Name is) kingdom, riches, mansions and royal courts; remembering the Name, (one's) conduct becomes perfect. Slave Nanak has reflected and found this: without the Lord's Name all is false, (mere) ashes. ॥4॥
1137.4: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Not a sesame seed's worth of stain has touched (the Lord's servant) at all; the wicked Brahmin has died in the agony of colic. The Supreme Lord himself has protected the Lord's servants; by the Guru's glory the sinner has died. The servant has himself meditated on his own Master; that foolish sinner (the Lord) himself has destroyed. God, mother and father (to him), is the protector of his own slave; the slanderer's brow is blackened, here and hereafter. The Supreme God has heard servant Nanak's prayer; the vile sinner has wasted away, his hopes dashed. ॥4॥
1137.5: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Good, good, good, good, good is your Name; false, false, false, false is the pride of the world. Beautiful are your servants; the sight of them is beyond measure; without the Name the whole world is ashes. Wondrous is your creation; your feet are worthy of praise; priceless is your praise, O true King. God (Khuda) is the support of the unsupported, (their) shelter; (he) raises up the poor; meditate (on him) day and night. On Nanak the Master himself is merciful; Allah does not slip from (his) heart, soul and breath. ॥4॥
1138.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through the Guru, obtain the true wealth; bear God's will, accepting it as true. Stay alive, alive, alive; rising each day, drink (the Name of) Ram, the home of all delights; say with the tongue: Har Har, Har Har. In Kalyug, deliverance comes through the Name alone; Nanak speaks (this) reflection on God (Brahm). ॥2॥
1138.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Serving the True Guru, (one) obtains all fruits; (and) wipes away the filth of birth after birth. O God, your Name purifies the fallen; the singing of (your) praises (comes to one) by the deeds written in the past. In the company of the Saadh deliverance comes; (one) gains honour at God's door. All good lies in the service of God's feet; all the angels, men and gods long for (that servant's) dust. Nanak has found the treasure of the Name; repeating, repeating (the Name of) the Lord, the whole world is saved. ॥4॥
1138.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The Lord) clasps his slave to his bosom; the slanderer he casts into the fire. Narayan protects (his slave) from the sinner; the sinner finds release nowhere; the sinner is consumed by his own deeds. The slave has come to love the dear Lord, Ram; the slanderer has taken the perverse bent. The Supreme Lord has made his innate nature manifest; the evil-doer has reaped what he did. (He) neither comes nor goes; he pervades all. Slave Nanak is in the Lord's refuge. ॥4॥
1138.4: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Sridhar, the Enchanter (Mohan), the Creator of all, the Formless One, the giver of peace: forsaking such a God you serve others: by what pleasures of poisonous Maya are you intoxicated? O my mind, meditate on Govind. I have looked at all other means; whatever (other) one devises, by it the task is spoiled. Forsaking the Master, the blind and ignorant manmukhs remember (his) handmaid (Maya); those who worship the Lord they slander, Guru-less, like beasts. Soul, frame, body and wealth: all is God's; the saakats say, (it is) mine. (Their) proud intellect is evil-minded and filthy; without the Guru (they) go round and round in the world-ocean. By burnt offerings, sacrifices, chanting, austerities and every discipline, at river-banks and tiraths, (God) is not found. Self-conceit was erased of those who took (his) refuge; O Nanak, through the Guru (he) has carried the world across. ॥4॥
Sridhar (he who holds Sri, Lakshmi): a name of Vishnu; in Gurbani, a name of God.
1139.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have seen (him) in the forest, seen (him) in the grass, seen (him) in the home and in the renunciate's life; I have seen (him) among the staff-bearers and the wearers of matted hair, in fasts, vows and tiraths. In the company of the Sants I have seen (him) within the mind; (he) fills the heavens, the netherworlds and all; with delight I have sung his joyful praises. I have seen (him) among yogis, all the garbs and sannyasis, among celibates, Jangams and wearers of patched coats; I have seen (him) among ascetics, great ascetics and sages, among actors, plays and dances. Within the four (Vedas) I have seen (him), within the six (Shastras) seen (him), in the eighteen (Puranas) and the Simritis; all together speak of the One, the One alone; then from whom shall I call him hidden? The Master is beyond grasp, beyond grasp, endless; his worth cannot be priced, cannot be priced. O servant Nanak, one should be a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those in whose hearts he has become manifest. ॥4॥
Jangams are Shaiva mendicants who go about ringing bells.
1139.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He who knows (God) to be near: why would he do evil? (He who) hoards poison (Maya) goes about ever afraid. (God) is near, yet (one) has not found (this) secret; without the True Guru, Maya has enticed all. Near, near (is he), everyone says; (but) some rare one, through the Guru, grasps the secret. (He who) does not see (him) near goes into another's house; he steals wealth, and lives by falsehood. the drug of the cheat has been cast upon him; he has not known the Lord to be with (him); without the Guru, he is led astray by doubt. (He who) does not know (him) near speaks falsehood; the fool is robbed by attachment to Maya. The treasure (of the Name) is within, (but) he goes off to other lands; without the Guru, he is led astray by doubt. He on whose forehead, on whose brow, (the Lord's) grace is written serves the True Guru, and (his) closed doors open. Within and without, that One is near (him); O servant Nanak, (for him) no one comes or goes. ॥4॥
1139.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Whom you protect, who can kill him? All, the whole world, is within you alone. The mortal devises millions of schemes, (but) that alone comes to pass which the Lord, who works wonders, does. Protect (me), protect (me), in your grace; (I have come) to your refuge, to your court. He who has served the Fearless One, the giver of peace, has cast off fear, and recognised the One. Whatever you do, that alone comes to pass; no other kills or protects. What are you thinking, in your human way? The all-pervading Being knows every heart, and is all-wise. The One is the prop, the One alone the support; the Creator knows everything. He on whom the Creator casts his glance of grace: all the affairs of that servant (he) brings to good. His protector is that One alone; O servant Nanak, no one can reach (him). ॥4॥
1140.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). One should fret if (God) were outside (anything); one should fret if Narhari were forgotten; one should fret if another (than he) were dear (to one); (but) why should one fret, when (he) pervades (all)? In attachment to Maya, (man) frets and frets and burns away; without the Name, wandering, wandering, wandering, he is worn out. One should fret if there were another Creator; one should fret if anyone died unjustly; one should fret if (God) knew nothing; (but) why should one fret, when (you) fill and pervade (all)? One should fret if anything happened by force (against his will); one should fret if (he) caused (anyone) pain by mistake. The Guru has said that whatever happens, all is from God; since then, leaving (all) fretting, we sleep free of care. O God, you alone are the Master; everyone is yours; as it pleases (you), so you decide. There is no second; (you,) the One, pervade (all); keep (my) honour: Nanak is in (your) refuge. ॥4॥
1140.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Without instruments, what is a dance? Without a throat, how can a singer (sing)? Without the string, how can the rabab sound? Without the Name, all deeds are in vain. Without the Name, say, who has crossed over? Without the True Guru, how has anyone got across? Without a tongue, where is a speaker? without ears, where is a hearer? without eyes, how does anyone see? Without the Name, man counts for nothing anywhere. Without learning, how can anyone be a pandit? Without authority to command, what is the splendour of a kingdom? Without understanding, how can the mind be still? Without the Name, the whole world has gone mad. Without detachment, how can one be a renunciant? Without renouncing Haumai, how can anyone be one who renounces? Without bringing the five enemies under control, how can the mind be subdued? Without the Name, (one) grieves for ever and ever. Without the Guru's teaching, how can there be wisdom? Without seeing (him), say, what meditation can there be? Without (God's) fear, all talk is vice; says Nanak, such is the understanding of (the Lord's) door. ॥5॥
1140.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God) has given man the sickness of Haumai; through the sickness of lust the elephant is held captive; through the sickness of sight the moths burn to death; through the sickness of sound the deer have perished. Whatever is seen, all of it is sick; free of sickness is my True Guru, the (true) yogi. Through the sickness of the tongue the fish is caught; through the sickness of scent the bumble-bee is destroyed; the whole world is (stricken with) the sickness of attachment; in the threefold sickness (of the three qualities) the vices have grown. In sickness (one) dies, in sickness (one) is born; in sickness (one) roams through births again and again. Bound by sickness, (one) finds not the least stillness; without the True Guru the sickness never goes. The one on whom the Supreme Lord has shown mercy, (God) has taken (him) by the arm and pulled (him) out of the sickness; (his) bonds were broken, (he) found the Saadh Sangat. Says Nanak, the Guru has cured (his) sickness. ॥4॥

Each of these creatures dies through one sense: the bumble-bee through smell, shut in the closing lotus; the moth through sight, in the flame; the elephant through touch, lured into a pit by a she-elephant; the fish through taste, on the bait; the deer through hearing, drawn by the hunter's music.
1141.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). When (God) comes to mind, there is supreme bliss; When (he) comes to mind, all sorrows are shattered; When (he) comes to mind, (one's) longing is fulfilled; When (he) comes to mind, (one) never grieves. Ram, the King, has come and become manifest within (me); the perfect Guru has dyed (me) in (his) love. When (he) comes to mind, (one) is king over all; When (he) comes to mind, (all) tasks are fulfilled; When (he) comes to mind, (one) is dyed the deep crimson (of love); When (he) comes to mind, (one) is ever in delight. When (he) comes to mind, (one) is wealthy forever; When (he) comes to mind, (one) is ever free of doubt; When (he) comes to mind, (one) enjoys all delights; When (he) comes to mind, dependence (on anyone) is ended. When (he) comes to mind, (one) finds the home of Sahaj; When (he) comes to mind, (one) is absorbed in Sunn; When (he) comes to mind, (one) sings Kirtan (songs of God's praise) forever; O Nanak, (his) mind is at one with the Lord. ॥4॥
Sunn: the stillness where no worldly thought stirs.
1141.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My Father (God) is ever-living; my brothers live for ever; my friends are imperishable for ever; my family dwells in its own (true) home. I have found peace, and so all are at ease; the perfect Guru has united (me) with the Father. My mansions are higher than all; my lands are boundless, beyond (anyone's) questioning; my rule is ever unshakeable; my wealth is inexhaustible and abiding. My glory (lives) through all the ages; my renown (rings out) in every place and every space between; my praise is (sung) in every home; my devotion (is known) among all people. My Father has become manifest within (me); Father and son, together, have formed a bond. Says Nanak, when the Father was pleased, Father and son were absorbed in the one love. ॥4॥
1141.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Being without enmity, O True Guru, O God the Giver, we are offenders, you are the forgiver. The sinner who finds shelter nowhere, if he comes to (your) refuge, becomes pure. Winning the True Guru over, (I) have obtained peace; meditating on the Guru, (I) have received all fruits. O Supreme Lord, O True Guru, (to you) my salutation. (My) mind and body are yours; all the land is yours. When the veil was removed, (you) came into sight: you are the Master, O King of all. When it pleased him, the dry wood turned green; when it pleased him, there was a lake on the dry land; when it pleased him, all fruits were obtained; anxiety left, by falling at the True Guru's feet. (God) has been gracious to the ungrateful, the one without virtue; mind and body are cooled, Amrit has rained into the mind. The Supreme Lord, the Guru, has become merciful; O Nanak, the servants, beholding (him), are in rapture. ॥4॥
1142.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My True Guru depends on no one; the way of my True Guru is true for ever; my True Guru is the one who gives to all; my True Guru is the all-pervading Being, the Creator. There is no deity like the Guru; he on whose forehead (good) fortune is (written) takes up (his) service. My True Guru cherishes all; my True Guru kills and brings to life. The glory of my True Guru is made manifest in every place. My True Guru is the strength of the strengthless; my True Guru is the support in (my) home. I am ever a sacrifice to the True Guru, who has made the path plain and shown it. He who has served the Guru: fear does not touch him; he who has served the Guru: pain does not torment him. Nanak has searched the Simritis and the Vedas: between the Supreme Lord and the Guru there is no difference. ॥4॥
1142.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Repeating the Naam, the mind has come to light; repeating the Naam, sin has left the body; repeating the Naam, all the holy days have been kept; repeating the Naam, (one) has bathed at the sixty-eight (tiraths). Our tirath is the Name of the Lord; the Guru has taught (this) essence of wisdom. Repeating the Naam, pain has fled far; repeating the Naam, the utter fool has become wise; repeating the Naam, light has shone forth; repeating the Naam, entanglements are undone. Repeating the Naam, Jam does not come near; repeating the Naam, (one) finds peace in the Lord's court; repeating the Naam, God says, Well done; the Naam is our true capital. The Guru has told (me) this teaching, the essence: the praise of the Lord and the Naam are the support of the mind. O Nanak, through the atonement of the Name (people) are saved; other rites are (only) to win people's trust. ॥4॥
1142.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Salutation to him a hundred thousand times; one should offer this mind to him as a sacrifice. In his remembrance, torments are erased; there is bliss, and no fevers afflict (one). Such a diamond is the immaculate Name by repeating which all tasks are fulfilled. He by whose glance the camp of sorrow is torn down, (and one) holds the cooling Amrit Naam in the mind; he whose feet countless devotees worship, (he) is the fulfiller of all desires. In an instant (he) has filled the empty to the brim; in an instant (he) has made the withered green; in an instant (he) has given the homeless a place; in an instant (he) has given honour to the dishonoured. The One fills and pervades all; (but) he alone repeats (his Name) whose True Guru is perfect; the Lord's Kirtan is the support of that one on whom, says Nanak, (God) himself is merciful. ॥4॥
1143.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Me, the forsaken bride, (the Lord) himself has adorned; giving (me) beauty and colour, (he) has embellished (me) with the Name. Sorrow and all torment are gone; the Guru has become my mother and father. O friends, O companions, there is bliss in my home; in (his) grace my Husband (the Lord) has met me. The burning (of craving) is quenched; all hopes are fulfilled; the darkness is gone, light has dawned; the Anhad Shabad (resounds), wondrous and amazing; perfect is the Guru, perfect (his) grace. He to whom Gopal has become manifest: by the sight of him (one) is ever in rapture; in him are all virtues and great treasures, to whom the True Guru has given the Naam. He whom his own Master has met: (his) mind and body are cooled, repeating Har Har. Says Nanak, those servants who are pleasing to God: the dust (of their feet) some rare one obtains. ॥4॥
1143.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In plotting sins, (he) feels no sloth; going to a prostitute, (he) feels no shame at all; all day long (he) toils for wages; (but) at the time to remember the Lord, a thunderbolt falls on (his) head. Clinging to Maya, the world has gone astray; the One who leads astray has himself led (it) astray; (it) is absorbed in empty dealings. Watching the pageants of Maya, (his life) passes away; in love with a cowrie shell, (he) deals crookedly; the mind runs in the bonds of blind dealings; (but) the Creator does not come into (his) heart. Doing thus, and doing, (he) has met with pain; the tasks of Maya are never completed; (his) mind is sunk in lust, anger and greed; (he) has died writhing, like a fish without water. He whose protector the Lord himself has become ever repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har; (he) has sung the Lord's praises in the Saadh Sangat; O Nanak, (he) has found the perfect True Guru. ॥4॥
1143.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (On whom God) shows his mercy, that one obtains (the Naam); (he) enshrines the Lord's Name in (his) mind. The true Shabad (abides) in (his) heart and mind; (his) sins of birth after birth depart. The Name of Ram is the support of the soul; by the Guru's grace, repeat it daily, O brothers; it carries (you) across the world-ocean. Those for whom the Lord has written this treasure (in their fate), those servants receive honour in the Lord's court. Sing (his) praises in peace, Sahaj and bliss; hereafter (even) the homeless find a place. Through age upon age this is the essence, the quintessence: remembrance of the Lord is the true reflection. He whom (God) attaches to (his) hem, he alone is attached; asleep for birth after birth, (he) awakens. (O God, they are) your devotees; you yourself are the devotees' own; you yourself chant your own glory. All beings and creatures are in your hands; O God of Nanak, (you are) ever with (all). ॥4॥
1144.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). For me the Naam is the inner Knower; for me the Naam is of use; the Lord's Name pervades (my) every pore; the perfect True Guru has given (this) gift. The jewel of the Naam is in my storehouse, beyond reach, priceless, infinite, boundless. For me the Naam is the unshakeable Master; the glory of the Name shines in all; for me the Naam is the perfect banker; for me the Naam is the carefree (Lord). For me the Naam is food and love; for me the Naam is the mind's aim; by the Sant's grace the Naam is not forgotten; repeating the Naam, the Anhad sounds ring out in full. By God's grace (I) have obtained the Naam, the nine treasures; by the Guru's grace (I) have come into accord with the Name. They alone are wealthy, (they) the eminent, O Nanak, who have the treasure of the Name. ॥4॥
The nine treasures (nidhis): by tradition, the nine treasures of Kuber, the god of wealth; that is, all the riches of the world.
1144.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord), you are my father, you are my mother; you are the giver of peace to my soul and breath of life; you are my Master, I am your servant; without you, I have no other. In your grace, O God, grant (this) gift: that I may praise you day and night. We are your instruments, you are the player; we are your beggars; give (us) alms, O Giver. By your grace (we) enjoy love and delight; within every heart it is you who pervade. (O God,) by your grace (your) Name is repeated; in the Saadh Sangat (may I) sing your praises; by your kindness, pain is destroyed; by your mercy, the lotus (of the heart) blossoms. I am a sacrifice to the divine Guru, whose sight bears fruit, whose service is pure. Be kind, O my Master, my God, that Nanak may sing your praises always. ॥4॥
1144.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He whose court stands highest of all: to him be salutation for ever and ever; he whose seat is higher than the high: through (that) Lord's Name millions of sins are erased. In his refuge there is peace for ever (for the one) whom he, in his grace, unites (with himself). He whose works cannot be fathomed, in whom every heart puts its trust, has become manifest in the company of the Saadh; the devotees worship (him) with love, night and day. Giving and giving, (his) storehouses never run short; in an instant (God) can set up and pull down; he whose Hukam no one can erase, that True One is over the heads of kings. In whose shelter (we are), in him alone is (our) hope; our pain and pleasure (rest) with him alone. (He) has preserved his servant's honour in full; Nanak sings his praise. ॥4॥
1145.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The mourning woman has made (her weeping) a daily rite; (for) the bond (with the dead) has come to (her) mind, for the sake of goods and their use. If anyone, understanding (this), turns detached, (he) grieves no more over birth and death. All this business and expanse is of poisonous Maya; some rare one has made the Name (his) support. Maya of the three qualities holds sway (over all); whoever clings (to it) meets pain and torment. There is no peace without meditating on the Name; the treasure of the Name (only) the very fortunate one obtains. He who gives (his) heart to a player in disguise regrets it once the disguise is taken off. As (it goes with) one who would take shelter in a cloud's shade, so (it goes with) this expanse of attachment and vice. If anyone obtains the One Thing, his task alone is fulfilled. He who, by the Guru's grace, has obtained the Naam: O Nanak, his coming (into the world) is approved. ॥4॥
1145.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Slander of a Sant (makes one) wander through births; slander of a Sant makes (one) sick; through slander of a Sant (one) suffers pain; Jam punishes the slanderer. Those who quarrel with a Sant: those slanderers taste no joy at all. Slander of a devotee gets (the slanderer's) body shattered; slander of a devotee makes (one) suffer hell; through slander of a devotee (one) rots in the womb; through slander of a devotee (one) falls from sovereignty. The slanderer finds release nowhere; what (slanderers) sow, they themselves eat. (The slanderer) is worse than a thief, an adulterer or a gambler; the slanderer has set a needless load upon his own head. The devotees of the Supreme Lord bear no enmity; he who worships (their) feet crosses over. The Primal Being (himself) has led the slanderer astray; O Nanak, (the record of his) past deeds cannot be erased. ॥4॥
1145.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). For me the Naam is the Vedas and the Naad (of the yogi's horn); for me the Naam is the fulfilment of (all) tasks; for me the Naam is the worship of the gods; for me the Naam is serving the Guru. The Perfect Guru has made the Name of the Lord firm (within me); the highest of all deeds is (repeating the Name of) the Lord, Har Har. For me the Naam is the dip and the bath (at the tiraths); for me the Naam is charity complete; repeating the Naam, they all become pure; those who repeat the Naam are my brothers and friends. For me the Naam is omen and auspicious hour; for me the Naam is contentment and choice delights; for me the Naam is all religious observance; for me the Naam is pure dealing. Each one in whose mind the One God has come to dwell: for all such servants, the Lord, Har Har, is the prop. O Nanak, the singing of the Lord's praises (dwells) in the mind and body (of him) to whom (God) gives the Name in the Saadh Sangat. ॥4॥
1146.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) to the poor you give wealth; countless sins depart, the mind becomes pure; all desires and tasks are fulfilled, (when) you give your devotee (your) Name. Fruitful is the service of Gopal, the King; (he is) the Master who does and causes all to be done; from him no one goes away empty-handed. O God, you destroy the sickness of the sick; you erase the grief of the sorrowful, O God; the homeless you seat in a place (of honour); your servant you attach to (your) devotion. To the dishonoured, O God, you give honour; the foolish dullard becomes clever and wise; the fear of all that is fearsome flees, (when) the Lord dwells in the mind of his servant. God, the Supreme Lord, is the treasure of peace; the knowledge of the essence is the Lord's Amrit Naam. (He whom God) in his grace attaches to the service of the Sants, O Nanak, (he) stays absorbed in the company of the Saadh. ॥4॥
1146.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the assembly of the Sants the Lord comes to dwell in the mind; in the assembly of the Sants all sin flees; in the assembly of the Sants the way of life is pure; in the company of the Sants love for the One arises. That place is called the assembly of the Sants (where) the praises of the Supreme Lord alone are sung. In the assembly of the Sants (the round of) birth and death ends; in the assembly of the Sants Jam says nothing (to one); in the company of the Sants the pure Bani (is uttered); in the assembly of the Sants the Naam is spoken. The seat of the assembly of the Sants is unshakeable; in the assembly of the Sants sins are destroyed; in the assembly of the Sants (God's) pure discourse goes on; in the company of the Sants the pain of Haumai flees. The assembly of the Sants is never destroyed; in the assembly of the Sants (dwells) the Lord, the treasure of virtues; the assembly of the Sants is the resting-place of the Master; O Nanak, (there) the Lord is woven (into the Sants), like warp and weft. ॥4॥
1146.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). What sickness (can touch one) when (God) himself protects? That servant suffers neither pain nor anguish. He on whom God shows mercy: from over him (God) drives away death. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is a companion forever; he in whose mind it comes is ever at peace; Jam does not come near him. When this (being) was not, who then created (him)? From what source, and in what form, has (he) brought (him) forth? He himself kills, and himself gives life; he ever cherishes his own devotee. Know that all things are in his hands; my God is the Lord of those who have no lord. his Name is the Destroyer of sorrow; sing his praises, and you will find peace. O Master, hear the prayer of the Sants: (our) soul, breath and wealth are in your keeping. This world is yours; all meditate on you alone; show mercy, that Nanak may find peace. ॥4॥
1147.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) on your support (I) live in Kalyug; on your support (all) sing your praises; on your support, death does not touch (one); on your support, the entanglement (of Maya) is destroyed. In faith and in the world, your support (is mine); the one Master pervades all. On your support (I) rejoice; on your support (I) repeat the Guru's mantra; on your support the ocean of fear is crossed; the Protector is perfect, an ocean of peace. On your support there is no fear at all; that True One knows every heart. on your support, your strength is in the mind; here and hereafter you are (our) support. (We have) your support and trust in you; all meditate on (you), O God, treasure of virtues; repeating (your Name) again and again, your servants rejoice; O Nanak, remember the True One, the treasure of virtues. ॥4॥
1147.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). First, (he) has given up slandering others; all the anxiety of (his) mind has gone; greed and attachment, all, (he) has cast far away; seeing God ever present, (he) is the supreme Vaishnav (the true devotee). Rare is such a renunciant; that servant repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har. (He) has forsaken the company of the proud intellect; the dye of lust and anger has faded (from him); (he) meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har Hare; (such people) have crossed over in the company of the holy. Enemy and friend have become alike (to him); the Lord fills all; accepting God's will, (he) has found peace. The Perfect Guru has made the Name of the Lord firm (within him). He whom (God) himself, in his grace, protects: that devotee alone chants the chant of the Name. (he who) has taken counsel from the Guru has light in (his) mind; says Nanak, his (labour) has come to fruition. ॥4॥
1147.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). No peace comes from earning great wealth; no peace comes from watching dances and plays; no peace comes from conquering many lands; all peace lies in singing the praises of the Lord, Har Har. Obtain peace, Sahaj and bliss; the Saadh Sangat is found by great good fortune; through the Guru, utter the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Mother, father, son and wife are bonds; bonds are the rites and pious deeds done with (the pride that) I am the doer; (when) the One who cuts the bonds dwells in the mind, then (one) finds peace and dwells in one's own home (within). All are beggars; God is the Giver, the treasure of virtues, endless and boundless. He on whom (his) own God bestows grace: that very servant will repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har. (My) prayer is before my own Guru: be gracious, O Being, treasure of virtues. Says Nanak, (I have come) to your refuge; keep (me) as it pleases (you), O Lord of the world. ॥4॥
1147.4: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (He who), meeting the Guru, has given up the love of another, (who) through the Guru has repeated the Lord's Name: (his) anxiety is forgotten, love for the Naam has taken hold (of him); (he), though asleep for birth after birth, has awoken. (He whom God) in his grace attaches to his own service finds every peace in the company of the Saadh. Through the Guru's Shabad (he) has rid (himself) of sickness and faults; (he) keeps the medicine of the Naam within (his) mind; meeting the Guru, bliss has come into (his) mind; the Name of the Lord holds all treasures. The terror of Jam, of birth and death, is gone; in the Saadh Sangat the inverted lotus (of the heart) has blossomed; singing (God's) praises, (he has found) an abiding rest; all (his) tasks have been fulfilled. (His) body, so hard to obtain, has been approved (at the Lord's door); it has borne fruit through repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Says Nanak, God has shown mercy (to me); with every breath and every morsel (I) repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Hari. ॥4॥
1148.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He whose Name is the highest of all: sing his praises for ever and ever; remembering him, all pain departs, and every comfort comes to dwell in the mind. O mind, remember that True One; in this world and the next you will attain release. The all-pervading Being, the Stainless One, is the Creator; (he) gives food to all beings and creatures; in an instant (he) forgives millions of sins; through loving devotion (he) ever carries (beings) across. True wealth and true glory (are his), (who) has received unwavering understanding from the perfect Guru. He whom the Protector, in his grace, (protects): all his darkness is dispelled. (My) attention is fixed on the Supreme Lord, who, free of all desire, wholly fills (all); erasing (my) doubt and fear, Gopal has met (me); the Guru has become merciful to Nanak. ॥4॥
1148.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He in whose remembrance there is light in the mind, torments are erased, and one dwells in peace and Sahaj: (his remembrance) comes to him alone to whom God (himself) gives (it); (he) is granted the service of the perfect Guru. O God, your Name is (the spring of) every peace; O my mind, sing (it) at all hours. (He) obtains whatever fruit he desires (who) enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind. Meditating on the Lord, (his) comings and goings cease, fixing (his) attention on God with loving devotion. Lust, anger and pride are destroyed; the attachments and loves of Maya are broken; (he) rests on God's support day and night, (he) to whom the Supreme Lord gives (this) gift. (O God, you are) the Master who does and causes all to be done; you know the inner being of every heart. In your grace, attach (me) to your service; Nanak, (your) servant, is in your refuge. ॥4॥
1148.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He who does not repeat the Naam dies of shame; lacking the Name, how can (he) sleep at ease? Forsaking the Lord's remembrance, (he) wants the supreme state; (but) without a root, how can there be branches? O my mind, meditate on the Guru, Govind; (he) washes off the filth of birth after birth, and cutting (your) bonds, unites (you) with the Lord. Bathing at a tirath, how can the stone (of the heart) be clean? the filth of Haumai clings to the mind. Millions of rites are the root of bondage; without the Lord's worship, (they are) a useless bundle (of straw). Without eating, hunger is not appeased; when the sickness goes, then the pains depart. (Man) is caught up in lust, anger, greed and attachment; (he) has not repeated (the Name of) the God who made (him). Blessed, blessed are the Saadhs; blessed is the Lord's Name; at all hours sing (his) Kirtan, (his) praises. Blessed is the Lord's devotion, blessed the Creator; Nanak (is) in the refuge of God, the infinite Being. ॥4॥
1149.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Guru has become fully pleased, (and all) fears have gone; the Name of the Stainless One has been taken into the mind. (God is) merciful to the meek, ever kind; all entanglements have been destroyed. (There are) peace, Sahaj and bliss in abundance; in the Saadh Sangat fears and doubts are erased; the tongue utters the Amrit (Name) of the Lord, Har Har. Love for the lotus feet (of the Lord) has taken hold; in an instant the great ghost has been destroyed. At all hours chant the chant of the Lord, Har Har; Govind, the Guru, is himself the Protector. (He) ever cherishes his own servant; he watches over the breaths of his devotees. Say, of what account is man? (God) gives (his) hand and saves (his devotee) from Jam (himself). Spotless is (his) glory, spotless (his) way of life, (in whose) mind and heart the Supreme Lord has come to dwell. In his grace the Guru has given (this) gift; Nanak has found the treasure of the Naam. ॥4॥
1149.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My Guru is the Cause of creation, all-powerful; (he) gives peace to soul and breath, (and is ever) near. (He is) the Destroyer of fear, the imperishable King; beholding the sight of him, all sorrow departs. (O God,) wherever I look, (I see) your refuge; I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the True Guru's feet. The divine Guru has met (me); (my) tasks are fulfilled; (his) spotless service bestows every fruit. Taking them by the hand, (he) has made his servants (his own), (and) has given the Name of Ram a dwelling in (their) hearts. (Theirs is) bliss forever, and no grief at all; no pain, no suffering, no sickness afflicts (them). (O God,) everything is yours; you are the Creator; O Supreme Lord, O Guru, unreachable and boundless. Spotless is the glory (of him to whom) the wondrous Bani, (the praise) of the perfect Supreme Lord, is pleasing in the mind. He pervades the water, the land and the sky; O Nanak, everything comes about from God. ॥4॥
1149.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (One whose) mind and body are dyed in love for Ram's feet: (God) fulfils all (his) desires; at all hours (he) sings (the praises of) the Lord; the True Guru has given (him) the perfect mantra. Most fortunate is he who loves the Naam; in his company the world crosses over. He alone is wise who remembers the One; he is wealthy whose intellect discerns; he is of noble family who remembers the Master; he is honourable who recognises his own self. By the Guru's grace he has attained the supreme state; (he) has meditated on the virtues of Gopal day and night. (His) bonds are broken, (his) hopes fulfilled; the Lord's feet dwell in (his) heart. Says Nanak, he whose fortune is perfect, that servant has come to God's refuge. (He is) pure himself, and has made all (others) pure; with (his) tongue (he) has savoured (the Name of) Ram, the home of all delights. ॥4॥
1150.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Repeating the Naam, no obstacle at all stands in the way; hearing the Naam, Jam runs off from afar; repeating the Naam, all sorrows are destroyed; repeating the Naam, (one) dwells at the Lord's feet. Meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har: (it is) devotion free of obstacles; sing the praises of the Lord with ever-growing delight. Remembering the Lord, no evil eye can fall on (one); remembering the Lord, neither demon nor god can touch (one); remembering the Lord, attachment and pride do not bind (one); remembering the Lord, (one) is not shut up in the wombs of births. Every hour is the hour for the Lord's remembrance; (yet) among many, only one remembers the Lord. Of high caste or low, whatever servant repeats (the Name): whoever repeats (it) attains release. One should repeat the Lord's Name in the Saadh Sangat; (there) the love of the Lord's Name is full. O God, show mercy to Nanak; O Lord, grant (me) to remember (you) with every breath. ॥4॥
1150.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God) himself is the Shastra, himself the Veda; he himself, (dwelling) in every heart, knows its secret. He to whom all things belong is Light itself; (he is) the Cause of creation, perfect, all-powerful. O my mind, take hold of God's support. Through the Guru, worship (his) lotus feet; no enemy and no sorrow comes near. He himself is the forest and the blade of grass, the essence of the three worlds; (he it is) on whose thread the world is strung. He himself joins Shiv and Shakti together; he himself is free of desire, and himself the enjoyer. Wherever I look, there he is; apart from him there is no other at all. Through love of the Naam the ocean (of the world) is crossed; Nanak sings (his) praises in the Saadh Sangat. He in whose power are release, (the world's) enjoyments and the way (of life): his servant lacks nothing at all. Those with whom (God), in his grace, is well pleased: O servant Nanak, those servants alone are blessed. ॥4॥
Shiv and Shakti: the conscious spirit and Maya; their union makes the world of the three qualities.
1150.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the minds of the devotees is the bliss of Gobind; (they) have become steady, and every anxiety has left (them). (Their) fears and doubts have been destroyed in an instant; the Supreme Lord has come to dwell in (their) minds. Ram, Ram is ever the helper of the Sants; at home and abroad, the Supreme God is with (them); (he) pervades every place in full. Gopal is (their) wealth, property, youth and way of life; (he) ever sustains (their) soul and breath in peace. Giving (him) his hand, (God) saves his servant, and does not leave (his) side for even a moment; (he is) with (him) always.
