There is no beloved like the Lord, no other at all; that True One looks after (his own) with care. Narayan is mother, father, son and kinsman; from the beginning, from the start of the ages, the devotees have sung (his) praises. In (their) minds is his support, the strength of God; apart from the One, (for them) there is no other at all. In Nanak's mind (too) is this strength: our God brings (our) purpose to fulfilment. ॥4॥
1151.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Remembering the Lord's Name, fear itself has been seized by fear; every sickness of the three qualities is gone, and the servant's tasks are fulfilled. The Lord's people ever sing (his) praises; they have found the abode of the Perfect One. Even Dharam Raj, the king of the Jams, longs day and night for the sight of the servant, (that he may) be made pure. Lust, anger, greed, intoxication, slander and pride are wiped out in the Saadh Sangat. Such Sants are met by great good fortune; I, Nanak, am ever a sacrifice to them. ॥2॥
1151.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He who harbours the five (enemies) is a worshipper of five pirs; each day he rises and speaks falsehood with (his) tongue; (he) paints (sacred) marks (on his body) and practises hypocrisy; (and) pines and wastes away within, like a widow. Without the Lord's Name all is false. Without the perfect Guru, release is not found; in the true court the Saakat is plundered. He alone is unclean who does not know (the Lord's) creative power. The Lord does not accept a plastered (cooking) place as purity. (He whose) inside is filthy, (though he) washes the outside every day, loses his honour in the true court. (He) strives for the sake of Maya, (but) never sets (his) foot on the straight (path). Him who made (him) he does not bring to mind; from (his) mouth he utters falsehood upon falsehood. He on whom the Creator bestows grace: his dealings are in the Saadh Sangat; love for the Lord's Name and for devotion has taken hold (of him); says Nanak, that servant suffers no break. ॥4॥
1151.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The whole world curses the slanderer; the slanderer's dealings are false; the slanderer's conduct is foul; (but the Lord) is the protector of his servant. The slanderer has died along with (his fellow) slanderer; the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, has protected (his) servants; over the slanderer's head death has thundered. No one believes what the slanderer says; slanderers tell lies and (then) regret it; (they) wring (their) hands and strike (their) heads on the ground; God does not let the slanderer go. The Lord's servant wishes no ill at all (on anyone); (yet) pain strikes the slanderer like a spear. Like a heron he keeps (his) wings spread; (but when he) spoke with (his) mouth, then, being weighed, (he) was cast out. The Creator himself knows every heart; he whom the Lord makes (his) servant becomes steadfast. The Lord's servant is (held) true in (his) court; having reflected, servant Nanak has spoken this essence. ॥4॥
1152.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). With both hands joined I offer (my) prayer; (my) soul, body and wealth are the capital (given) by him. He alone is my Master, the Creator; (to him) I am a sacrifice a million times. The dust (of the feet) of the Saadh has made (me) pure; remembering God, the mind's vices are wiped out, (and) the filth of birth after birth has been taken away. He in whose house are all treasures, by whose service honour is obtained, (he) is the fulfiller of all desires, (and) the support of the soul and breath of the devotees. Within each and every heart (he) gives light to all; repeating (the Name of) the treasure of virtues again and again, the devotees live. He whose service does not go in vain: meditate on that One within (your) mind and body. By the Guru's teaching (come) compassion and contentment, (and) the treasure of the Naam; this is a spotless thing. (O God,) in your grace, attach (me) to the hem (of your robe), (that) Nanak may ever meditate on (your) lotus feet. ॥4॥
1152.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My own True Guru has heard (my) prayer; (my) whole task has come to good. Within (my) mind and body (I) have meditated on God; the perfect Guru has taken away all fear. The divine Guru is the greatest of all, all-powerful; by his service (I) obtain every comfort. By whose doing all that happens comes about: his command no one can erase. The Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, is beyond compare; the Guru, whose form bears fruit, is his very image. He within whom the Lord's Name dwells: whatever he sees is (to him) the knowledge of God. He in whose mind the light is full, twenty parts in twenty: within that servant the Supreme Lord dwells. To that Guru (I) ever bow; to that Guru (I) am ever a sacrifice. Again and again (I) wash the True Guru's feet and drink (the water); repeating (the Name of) the Guru again and again, I, Nanak, live forever. ॥4॥
1153.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 3, Partal, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O God, cherisher of all, merciful One, which of (your) virtues can I count? Countless are (your) colours, many (your) waves; (you are) the Master of all. (For you) there are countless (paths of) wisdom, countless meditations, countless chants, recitations and austerities; countless reflect on (your) virtues and raise sweet strains; countless sages keep silence. Countless sounds, countless instruments, countless delights at every moment (are of your making); hearing (your) praise, countless faults and countless diseases are wiped out. O Nanak, in the service of the infinite divine Lord lie all the fruits and merits of (bathing at) the banks of tiraths, the six rites, fasts, worship, roaming the earth and making pilgrimages. ॥2॥
Partal: a setting in which the rhythm (taal) changes again and again as the hymn is sung.
The six rites (khat karam): the six duties of a Brahmin: studying and teaching, performing and officiating at sacrifice, giving and receiving gifts.
1153.2: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (One who) through reflection on the Guru's (word) recognises Ram in the self and the self in Ram, has come to know the Amrit Bani through the Shabad; (he) has killed (his) Haumai, and cuts away (his) sorrows. O Nanak, the diseases of Haumai are evil. Wherever I look, there is this one pain; the Primal Lord himself forgives through the Shabad. Those whom the Assayer himself has assayed are not pierced by the testing-needle again. Those on whom (his) gracious glance fell, the Guru has united (with the Lord); he who is pleasing to God, he alone is true. Air, water and fire are diseased; diseased is the earth with all its pleasures; mother, father, Maya and the body: these are diseased; diseased are those bound in family ties. Diseased are Brahma, Vishnu and Shiv; diseased is the whole world. Recognising the Lord's state, they were set free, (they who) reflected on the Guru's Shabad. Diseased are the seven seas with the rivers; the continents and the netherworlds are full of disease. The Lord's people are at ease in the True One; in every place (he) casts (his) gracious glance (on them). Diseased are those who wear the garbs of the six orders, and the countless men of hatha of every kind; what can the poor Vedas and Kateb do? (People) do not understand the One alone. He who eats sweet delicacies is filled with disease; in (living on) tubers and roots there is no peace (either). (Those who,) forgetting the Naam, walk another path repent at the last moment. (He who) wanders to tiraths is not rid of (his) disease; (what he) read has turned into dispute and wrangling. The disease of double-mindedness is greater still; (through it one) has become dependent on Maya. (He who), through the Guru, praises the True One by the Shabad, (with) the True One in (his) mind, is rid of (his) disease. O Nanak, the Lord's servants, on whom by (his) grace the seal (of the Name) is set, are spotless night and day. ॥9॥
Ashtapadi (ashta, eight; pad, stanza): a hymn of about eight stanzas.
The Kateb: the scriptures of the Semitic faiths (the Torah, the Psalms, the Gospel and the Quran).
1154.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. That Creator has brought forth a wondrous play; (he) has made the Anhad Bani, the Shabad, heard; the manmukhs have gone astray, the Gurmukhs (he) has made to understand; the Creator has ever been bringing about the cause (of it all). The Guru's Shabad is within me; (on it is my) attention; I will never give up the Lord's Name. (His) father sent Prahlad to study; taking (his) tablet, (Prahlad) came to the teacher. (He said:) I will not study any rites or ways other than the Naam; write (the Name of) Gobind, Murari, on my tablet. The mother said to her son Prahlad: Do not study what you are bent on; (so) she kept counselling (him). (Prahlad said:) The fearless Giver, the dear Lord, is with me; if (I) give up the Lord, then (my) family will be disgraced. (The teachers said:) Prahlad has led all the pupils astray; he does not listen to what we say, and sets his own affairs right; (he) has instilled devotion in the whole city. The assembly of the wicked has no power at all (over him). Sanda and Marka raised a complaint; all the demons strove in vain; he himself preserves the honour of his devotees; what can come of what a created being says? By the joining of past deeds, the demon held sway as king; (he) does not understand the Lord; he (the Creator) himself has led (him) astray. (He) picked a quarrel with his son Prahlad; the blind (demon) does not see that death has drawn near. (He) kept Prahlad (shut) in a room and put a lock on the door; (but) the fearless child is not afraid at all: within me is the Guru, Gopal. He who is a created being and vies (with the Creator) has taken a (great) name though he is nothing; what was written from the beginning came to pass: (he) picked a quarrel with the (Lord's) servant. The father raised a mace against Prahlad: Where is your Lord of the universe, your Gosain? (Prahlad said:) The Life of the world, the Giver, is the friend at the end; wherever I look, there (he) is pervading. Tearing the pillar open, the Lord revealed himself; (and) struck down the proud demon and destroyed him. In the minds of the devotees there was bliss; rejoicing rang out; (the Lord) gives glory to his servant. (The Creator) has brought forth birth, death and attachment; the Creator has written coming and going (into the lot of beings). For Prahlad's sake the Lord revealed himself; the devotees' word came to pass. The hosts of the gods hail Lakshmi: O mother, take away the form of Narsingh. Lakshmi is afraid, and cannot go (near him); Prahlad, the servant, came and clung to (the Lord's) feet. The True Guru has fixed the treasure of the Naam firm (in the mind); kingdom, wealth and all of Maya are false; (yet) greedy men stay clinging (to it); without the Lord's Name, punishment is met in the Lord's court. Says Nanak, everyone does as (the Lord) makes (him) do; they are accepted who have fixed (their) minds on the Lord. (The Lord) has ever taken the side of his devotees; the Creator has shown his own form. ॥13॥
Lakshmi: the goddess of wealth, in the Puranas the consort of Vishnu.
1155.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (He who) through the Guru's service obtained the fruit of Amrit has quenched Haumai and craving; the Lord's Name came to dwell in (his) heart and mind, (and his) desire merged in the mind itself. O my beloved, dear Lord, bestow your grace (on me): night and day (your) lowly servant begs for the Lord's virtues; through the Guru's Shabad (the Lord) saves (him). Jam cannot even cast an eye on the Sants; not a trace of the heat of sorrow touches (them). Those who (come to) your refuge cross over themselves, and carry all (their) families across. You yourself preserve the honour of the devotees; this is your greatness; (you) cut away (their) sins and sorrows of birth after birth; not a speck, not a mustard seed of double-mindedness (remains in them). We, foolish and ignorant, understand nothing; you yourself grant understanding. Whatever pleases you, that (a being) will do; nothing else can be done. Creating the world, you set (it) to worldly toil; (it) has done evil deeds; (it) has lost the treasure of this birth in a gamble, and has not gained awareness of the Shabad. The manmukhs die; they perceive nothing; (in them is) the darkness of evil-mindedness and ignorance. (they) never reach the far shore of the world-ocean; without the Guru, with the load (of sins) on (their) heads, (they) drowned and died. The servants dyed in the True Shabad are true; the Lord God himself has united (them with himself). Through the Shabad (they) have come to know the Guru's Bani, and stay with (their) minds fixed on the True One. You yourself are spotless; spotless (too) are your servants, who reflect (on you) through the Guru's Shabad. Nanak is ever a sacrifice to those who keep the Name of Ram enshrined in (their) hearts. ॥8॥
1155.2: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. He in whose heart is the Naam is the great king; he in whose heart is the Naam has (his) tasks fulfilled; he in whose heart is the Naam has gained millions in wealth; without the Naam, life goes in vain. (I) praise him whose capital is the wealth of the Lord; most fortunate is he on whose forehead is the Guru's hand. He in whose heart is the Naam has many forts and armies; he in whose heart is the Naam has the ease of Sahaj; he in whose heart is the Naam has become cool and calm; without the Naam, life is cursed, (no better than) death. He in whose heart is the Naam is liberated while living; he in whose heart is the Naam knows every way (of living); he in whose heart is the Naam has obtained the nine treasures; without the Naam, (one) comes and goes, wandering in doubt. He in whose heart is the Naam is free of all want; he in whose heart is the Naam ever has profit; he in whose heart is the Naam has a great family; without the Naam, the manmukh is a fool. He in whose heart is the Naam has a seat that never moves; he in whose heart is the Naam dwells on a throne; he in whose heart is the Naam is the true banker; he who lacks the Naam has neither honour nor credit. He in whose heart is the Naam is known among all; he in whose heart is the Naam is (the image of) the all-pervading Being, the Creator; he in whose heart is the Naam is the highest of all; without the Naam, (one) wanders through countless wombs. He in whose heart is the Naam has his work made known (everywhere); he in whose heart is the Naam has had (his) darkness dispelled; he in whose heart is the Naam is a man accepted (by the Lord); without the Naam, there is coming and going again and again. He has obtained the Naam on whom (God) has become merciful; in the Saadh Sangat (he) has beheld Gopal; (his) coming and going has ended; (he) has found peace; says Nanak, (his) essence has been merged in the Essence (of the Lord). ॥8॥
1156.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (He who) has made millions of Vishnus as (his) incarnations, whose places for dharma are millions of universes, (who) created millions of Maheshes and took (them) back into (himself), (and who) has set millions of Brahmas to fashioning the world: such is our Master, Govind; (I) cannot describe the expanse of (his) virtues. Millions of Mayas serve as handmaids in his (house), millions of beings are his couch; (O God,) millions of creations are within your being; millions of devotees dwell with the Lord. Millions of canopied kings bow down; millions of Indras stand at (his) door; millions of Baikunths lie within his sight; millions are the names of him whose worth is beyond reckoning. At whose (door) millions of sounds resound, millions (his) arenas, (where his) wondrous plays (go on); millions of Shaktis and Shivs obey (his) command; (he) gives support to millions of beings. Millions of tiraths are at his feet; millions are made pure by repeating (his) beautiful Name; millions of worshippers perform (his) worship; millions are (his) expanses; there is no other at all. Millions of spotless swans (sing) his glory; millions of the sons of Brahma sing his praise; in an instant (he brings) millions of dissolutions and creations; (O God,) your millions of virtues cannot be counted. Millions of the wise expound (your) wisdom; millions of meditators fix (their) meditation; millions of great ascetics practise nothing but austerities; millions of great sages abide in silence. The unseen Master, the Lord beyond the reach of the senses, pervades every heart; he knows every heart. (O God,) wherever I look, you dwell; the Guru has given Nanak this light. ॥8॥
Baikunth: in the Puranas, the heaven of Vishnu.
1157.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The True Guru has given me a gift; (he) has given the Lord's Name, a priceless jewel. (Now there are) endless delights and wonders of Sahaj; without a care, God has met Nanak. Says Nanak, the praise of the Lord is true; again and again keep (your) mind absorbed in it. Without a care, (God's) love has become my food; without a care, the Name is repeated within me; without a care, I am being saved through the Shabad; without a care, my storehouses are full. Without a care, my tasks are fulfilled; without a care, my sorrows have lifted; without a care, my enemies (have become) friends; without a care, (I) have brought this mind under control. The Carefree God has comforted me; without a care, my hope is fulfilled; without a care, the whole essence of truth (is) mine; the Guru has given me the mantra (of the Name) of the Carefree One. Without a care, my enmities have perished; without a care, my darkness is dispelled; without a care, Kirtan is sweet to the mind; without a care, (I) have seen God in every heart. Without a care, all (my) doubt is wiped out; without a care, (God,) the home of peace, has come to dwell in the mind; without a care, the Anhad (sound) plays within me; without a care, Gobind thunders within me. Without a care, my mind is content; (I) have recognised the eternal Master, the Carefree One; without a care, all discernment has welled up (in me); without a care, the Lord's support, Har Har, has come to (my) hand. The Carefree God wrote (my) destiny from the beginning; without a care, the one God, the Master, has met (me); all care has gone, without a care; Nanak, Nanak, Nanak has become one with God. ॥8॥
1157.2: Raag Bhairao, the hymns of the Bhagats: Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. This wealth I have is the Lord's Name; I neither tie it up in a knot nor sell it to live on. The Naam is my field, the Naam my garden; (O Lord,) I, your servant, practise devotion, (abiding) in your refuge. The Naam is my wealth, the Naam my stock-in-trade; leaving you aside, I know no other (stock). The Naam is my kin, the Naam my brother; at the end it is the Naam that stands by me as a friend. He whom (the Lord) keeps detached within Maya, says Kabir: I am his servant. ॥4॥
1157.3: Naked is the coming, naked the going; no one will remain, be he king or chief. For me, Ram the King is the nine treasures; (but) for you, (O man,) it is love of property, wife and wealth. (These) do not come along (at birth), nor go along (at death); what of it, then, if elephants are tethered at the door? The fortress of Lanka was of gold; (yet) what did foolish Ravan take with him? Says Kabir: give thought to some good (as well); gamblers go off shaking out both hands (empty). ॥4॥
1158.1: Brahma is soiled, Indra is soiled; the sun is soiled, and soiled is the moon. This world is soiled and foul; the one Lord alone is stainless, who has no end and no far shore. Soiled are the lords of the universes; soiled are night and day, and the thirty days (of the month). Soiled is the pearl, soiled the diamond; soiled are wind, fire and water. Soiled are Shiv, Shankar and Mahesh; soiled are the Siddhas, the seekers and the wearers of holy garbs. Soiled are the yogis and the Jangams, matted hair and all; soiled is the body, together with the soul (the swan). Says Kabir: those people are accepted (at the Lord's door), they alone are stainless, who know Ram. ॥6॥
1158.2: (O Mullah,) make your mind Mecca, and your body the qibla (the point one faces in prayer); the One who speaks (within you), he is the supreme Guru. Give the call to prayer, O Mullah, and say the namaz in the one mosque that has ten doors (the body). Make a sacrifice (bismil) of your dark nature (tamas), your doubt and the impurity of your mind; eat up the five (enemies), and contentment will come. the Hindu and the Turk (the Muslim) have one Master; what can a Mullah do, and what a Sheikh? Says Kabir: I have gone mad; little by little (my) mind has merged in Sahaj. ॥4॥
1158.3: Joining the Ganga, a stream is spoiled; (but) that stream becomes the Ganga, and its own self is gone. Kabir is spoiled, calling out the Name of Ram; he has become (one with) the True One, and goes nowhere else. Growing beside the sandalwood, a tree is spoiled; (but) that tree becomes sandalwood, and its own self is gone. Touching the paaras, copper is spoiled; (but) that copper becomes gold, and its own self is gone. In the company of the Sants Kabir is spoiled; (but) that Kabir has become one with Ram, and his own self is gone. ॥4॥
Paaras: the philosopher's stone, held to turn iron into gold at a touch; sandalwood is held to make the trees near it fragrant.
1158.4: (People put on) a mark on the forehead, a rosary in the hand, and a holy garb; people have taken Ram for a toy. If I am mad, then I am yours, O Ram; what does the world know of my secret? I pluck no leaves (as offerings), I worship no gods; without devotion to Ram, (all) worship bears no fruit. I worship the True Guru, and ever and always seek to please (him); with such service, in the Lord's court I am at peace. The world says Kabir has gone mad; Ram has recognised Kabir's secret. ॥4॥
1158.5: Turning back (from Maya), I have put out of mind both caste and lineage; my weaving is (now) in Sunn and Sahaj. No quarrel of mine is left; I have left both the Pandit and the Mullah. Weaving and weaving, I clothe my own self; where there is no self, there I stay and sing (the Lord's praises). What the Pandits and the Mullahs have written down, I have left behind and gone on; I have taken none of it. With true love (ikhlas) in the heart, behold the Mir (the Lord); O Kabir, (those who have met the Lord) have met (him) by searching and searching their own selves. ॥4॥
1159.1: No one gives the poor man respect; (the poor man) may try in a hundred thousand ways, (but) he (the rich man) gives (him) no thought. If a poor man goes to a rich man's (house), (the rich man,) sitting before him, turns his back. If a rich man goes to a poor man's (house), (the poor man) gives (him) respect and calls him in. Poor and rich are brothers, both of them; the working of God's power cannot be undone. Says Kabir: he alone is (truly) poor in whose heart the Naam is not. ॥4॥
1159.2: (If) devotion is earned through service of the Guru, then alone is this human body (counted as) gained. The gods (too) yearn for this body; with that body (now yours), take to the Lord's service. Worship Gobind, and do not forget (him); this alone is the gain of human birth. While old age, (that) disease, has not yet come, while death has not yet seized the body, while the voice has not yet faltered, worship Saringpani, O mind. If you do not worship (him) now, when will you, O brother? the end comes, and (then) worship cannot be done. Whatever you would do, carry it out now; (else) later you will repent, and not reach the far shore. That one is the servant whom (the Lord) has set to serve (him); he it is who has found the Stainless Lord. Meeting the Guru, the doors (of his mind) have opened; he does not come again on the road of births. This is your chance, this your turn; reflect and see within your own heart. Says Kabir: win (this game) or lose (it); I have told you in many ways, calling out again and again. ॥5॥
1159.3: In the city of Shiv (the auspicious Lord) dwells the finest understanding; there, (O yogis,) join (it) and reflect; (then) understanding of this world and the next comes; who, then, dies doing deeds of possessiveness? My attention has settled on my own true state (nij pad); the Name of Ram, the King, is my knowledge of God (Brahm Gyan). At the root door I have set the lock (bandh); above the sun I have held the moon fast; at the western door the sun burns; the Meru staff dwells above the head. There is a slab that screens the western door; above that slab is another window; above the window, the Tenth Gate; says Kabir: it has no end and no far shore. ॥3॥

Kabir speaks here in the yogis' terms: the root door (the chakra at the base of the spine), the sun and the moon (the right and left breath channels, pingala and ida), the western door (the way up the back, along the spine), the Meru staff (the spine). The Tenth Gate (dasam duar): the inner door beyond the body's nine openings, where the soul meets God.
1159.4: That one is a Mullah who fights his own mind, who, by the Guru's teaching, grapples with death, (and) crushes the pride of the Being of death (the Jam); to that Mullah, my salaam always. (God) is present here; why do you tell of him as far off? Bind the brawling (passions), and find the Beautiful One. That one is a Qazi who searches out his own body, who kindles Brahm, (the divine) fire within the body, who does not let his seed (bindu) fall, even in dreams: that Qazi knows neither old age nor death. That one is a Sultan who draws two arrows (to the bow), brings back within (the mind) that runs outside, (and) gathers his army in the Gagan Mandal (the Tenth Gate); that Sultan bears the royal canopy over his head. The yogi calls out, Gorakh, Gorakh; the Hindu utters the Name of Ram; the Muslim has his one Khuda; (but) Kabir's Master pervades all. ॥4॥
Gorakh (Gorakhnath): the teacher revered by the Nath yogis.
1160.1: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). They who call a stone God: their service goes for nothing. He who falls at a stone's feet: his toil is wasted. Our Master ever speaks; God gives his gifts to every being. God is within, (but) the blind one does not know (him); beguiled by doubt, he puts the noose (on himself). The stone neither speaks nor gives anything; (such) rites are empty, (such) service bears no fruit. If one rubs sandalwood on a corpse, say, what fruit does (the corpse) get from it? If one rolls a corpse in filth, what does the corpse lose by it? Says Kabir: I say it aloud: understand and see, O foolish Saakat: in the love of another, many a home has been brought to ruin; the devotees of Ram are ever at peace. ॥4॥
As at 1136.3, the Guru here unfolds the thought of the shabad of Kabir's just before (ਸੋ ਮੁਲਾਂ ਜੋ ਮਨ ਸਿਉ ਲਰੈ).
1160.2: The fish in the water are pierced by Maya; the moths at the lamp are run through by Maya; Maya, as lust, takes hold of the elephant; snakes and bumblebees are worn away in Maya. Such an enchantress is Maya, O brother, that as many beings as there are, so many she leads astray. Birds and the beasts of the wild are steeped in Maya; sugar torments the fly sorely; horses and camels are hemmed in by Maya; the eighty-four Siddhas are at play in Maya. The six celibates (jatis) are Maya's slaves; (so are) the nine Naths, the sun and the moon; ascetics and great rishis lie asleep in Maya; in Maya are death and the five enemies. Dogs and jackals are steeped in Maya; monkeys, leopards and lions, cats, sheep and foxes, trees and roots: (all) lie in Maya. The gods are soaked in Maya, (and those of) the ocean, of Indra's realm and of the earth. Says Kabir: whoever has a belly has Maya (upon him); (one) is freed only when (one) has found the Saadh. ॥5॥
The six celibates (jatis): by tradition Hanuman, Bhishma, Lakshman, Bhairav, Gorakh and Dattatreya.
1160.3: As long as (one) keeps saying mine, mine, so long not a single task (of his) comes to good. When this mine, mine is wiped away, then God comes and sets (his) task right. Reflect on such wisdom, O mind: why do you not remember the Lord, the destroyer of pain? As long as the lion (of pride) lives in the forest, so long the forest does not flower at all; but the moment the jackal (of humility) devours the lion, all the vegetation bursts into flower. He who has won drowns; he who has lost swims across; by the Guru's grace (he) crosses to the far shore. Kabir, the servant, says, to make (it) plain: keep your attention fixed on Ram alone. ॥3॥
1161.1: He who has seventy hundred commanders (salars), whose prophets number one and a quarter lakh, whose sheikhs are said to be eighty-eight crore, and fifty-six crore his close attendants: who will carry the plea of a poor man like me (to him)? (his) court is far off; who can reach (his) palace? The thirty-three crore (gods) are his household; the eighty-four lakh (kinds of beings) wander about crazed; (God) showed Baba Adam a little of his stern eye, (and) even he kept paradise only a little while. He in whose heart there is turmoil wears a yellow face; forsaking the Kateb, he does the devil's work; he finds fault with the world, (and) is angry at people, (but) he reaps what he himself has done. (O Lord,) you are the Giver, I am ever a beggar; were I to answer (you) back, it would be a sin. Kabir, your servant, has come into your shelter; O Rahman (the Merciful), keep (me) near (you): (that is my) paradise. ॥4॥
Baba Adam: in the Semitic faiths the first man, sent out of paradise for disobeying God.
1161.2: Everyone talks of going there (to Baikunth), (but) I do not know where Baikunth is. They have not known the secret of their own selves, (yet) they describe Baikunth by talk alone. As long as, O mind, (you) hope for Baikunth, there is no dwelling at (the Lord's) feet. (its) moat, fort, city and rampart (I do) not (know); I do not know the gate of Baikunth. Says Kabir: what more should one say now? The Saadh Sangat is Baikunth itself. ॥4॥
1161.3: How is this mighty fortress to be taken, O brother? (It has) a double wall and a triple moat. the five (enemies), the twenty-five (principles), attachment, pride and envy (stand ready), with mighty Maya as (their) cover; the strength of (your) poor servant does not reach (that far); what shall I do, O Raghurai? Lust is the keeper of the doors, pain and pleasure the sentries, sin and virtue the gates; anger, a mighty brawler, is the chief; and there the mind is king, in revolt. Relish (of the senses) is (his) armour, possessiveness (his) helmet; he has strung the bow of evil intellect; the arrows of craving stay (ready) within the heart: so the fortress cannot be taken. (But) I made love the fuse and attention the rocket, and fired the shell of wisdom; I lit the fire of Brahm in Sahaj, and with a single stroke (the fort) was won. With truth and contentment I took up the fight, and broke down both gates; through the Saadh Sangat and the Guru's grace I seized the king of the fort. With the host of the Lord's devotees and the strength of Simran, I have cut the noose of the fear of death; Kabir, the servant, has climbed atop the fort, and taken the kingdom that never perishes. ॥6॥
The twenty-five: the twenty-five principles (tattvas) of the Sankhya school.
1162.1: Into Mother Ganga, deep and unfathomed, (they) took Kabir, bound in chains. (When) the mind does not waver, why should the body be afraid? (my) mind remains absorbed in (the Lord's) lotus feet. By a wave of the Ganga my chain was broken; Kabir is seated on a deerskin. Says Kabir: (I have) no companion and no friend; in water and on land, Raghunath (the Lord) is the protector. ॥3॥
1162.2: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, an Ashtapadi of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (He who is attuned to the Name) makes his dwelling in a fortress unreachable, hard of approach, in which the Light (of God) shines; lightning flashes (there), and there is bliss, where God, Bal Gobind (the Lord ever young), lies at rest. (When) this soul is attuned to the Name of Ram, old age and death are left behind, and doubt takes flight. (Those) whose minds are fond of (the reckoning of) low caste and high go on singing the songs of Haumai. The Anhad Shabad rings out (there), where God, Sri Gopal, lies at rest. (He who) has fashioned the continents and the spheres, sphere upon sphere, (and) who breaks down the three worlds and the three (qualities): the Unreachable One, beyond the senses, dwells within the heart; no one finds the far shore of the secret of Dharnidhar (the Support of the earth). As fragrance shows itself in the plantain flower, (as) pollen has made its home in the lotus, (so) within the twelve-petalled heart (dwells) the mantra (of God), where Sri Kamla Kant (Lakshmi's Lord) lies at rest. Below and above, (God's) light meets the eye; (he) gives light in the realm of Sunn; there is no sun there, no moon; (there) the primal Stainless One is in bliss. The One who is in the universe, know that same One in the body; bathe in the Mansarovar (of the Name); he whose chant is Sohang, on him neither virtue nor sin leaves a stain. (For him) there is no low caste and no high, no sunshine and no shade; (this) is found nowhere else but in the Guru's refuge. (he) is not moved though one would move (him); he neither comes nor goes; he remains merged in Sunn and Sahaj. If anyone comes to know (God) within the mind, he who speaks (his praise) becomes (that One) himself; he who, through the mantra (of the Guru), makes the Light steady in the mind, says Kabir: that mortal swims across. ॥8॥
Sohang (Sanskrit so'ham, he am I): the recognition that one's own self is of the light of the one Lord.
1162.3: He at whose (door) millions of suns give light, millions of Mahadevs (Shivs) and (their) Kailash mountains, millions of Durgas massage his feet, (and) millions of Brahmas recite the Vedas: when I beg, (I beg) of Ram alone; with any other god I have nothing to do. Millions of moons light (his) lamps, the thirty-three (crore) gods, all of them, eat of (his) food, the nine planets, in their millions, stand in (his) court, millions of Dharam Rajs are his door-keepers. Millions of winds move about (his) upper chambers, millions of Basak serpents spread (his) bed, millions of oceans fetch his water, millions of the eighteen loads (of all vegetation) are the hair (of his body). Millions of Kamers (Kuber) fill (his) treasuries, millions of Lakshmis deck themselves out (for him), millions of sins and virtues keep looking to (him), millions of Indras do him service. Fifty-six crore (clouds) are his door-keepers, flashing beyond measure over town after town; the terrible one (Kali), her locks let loose, moves about (there); Gopal plays with millions of powers. Millions of sacrifices (are held) at his court, millions of Gandharbs (the singers of the gods) hail his victory, millions of branches of learning all tell of (his) virtues, yet (none) finds the end of the Supreme Lord. Millions of Bawans (Vaman, the dwarf incarnation) are the hair of his body, by whom Ravan's army was outdone; of whom thousands of crores of Puranas tell at length, (and who) crushed Duryodhan's pride. Millions of Kandarps (gods of love) cannot match (his beauty), they who steal the desires from deep within (all hearts). Says Kabir: hear (me), O Saringpani, grant (me) the state free of fear; this is the gift I beg. ॥8॥

Kabilas: Kailash, the Himalayan mountain held to be Shiva's abode. Basak (Vasuki): in the Puranas, the king of the serpents. Duryodhan: the eldest of the Kauravas in the Mahabharata, slain in the war with the Pandavas.
1163.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O tongue, I would cut you into a hundred pieces if you did not utter (the Name of) Sri Gobind. O tongue, be dyed in the Lord's Name; meditating on the Lord, Har Har, be dyed a lovely colour. Futile is the tongue (given) to other tasks; the Lord's Name alone is the nirban pad (the state free of desire). Worship offered to countless millions of other (gods) does not come up to the Name of the one Lord. Namdev humbly prays: this is (my) task: (to say,) your forms are endless, O Narayan. ॥4॥
1163.2: He who has given up others' wealth and others' wives: near him dwells Narhari. Those who do not worship Narayan: I do not (even) look upon them. Those within whom there is a gap (between them and the Lord): as beasts are, so are those men. Namdev humbly prays: without a nose (a man) does not look fine, (though he have all) thirty-two marks (of beauty). ॥3॥
1163.3: Milk in a bowl, water in a jug: Nama milked the kapila (brown) cow and brought (the milk). Drink the milk, O King Gobind; drink the milk, (that) my mind may be content; otherwise the father of the house will be angry (with me). The golden bowl, filled with Amrit, Nama took it and set it before the Lord. (The Lord said:) This one devotee dwells in my heart; seeing Nama, Narayan smiled. Having given (the Lord) the milk to drink, the devotee went home; (thus) Nama had the sight of the Lord. ॥4॥
1164.1: I am crazed (for him); Ram is my Husband; for him I adorn myself with care upon care. Let people slander (me) as they will, slander as they will, slander as they will; (my) body and mind are (given over) to (my) beloved Ram. One should not quarrel or wrangle with anyone; with the tongue one should drink (the Name of) Ram, the home of all delights. Now, knowing (him) in (my) soul, it has so come about that I meet Gopal to the beat of the drum. Whether a man praise (me) or slander (me), Nama has met Sri Rang (the Lord) himself. ॥4॥
1164.2: Sometimes (one) does not care even for kheer, sugar and ghee; sometimes (the Lord) has (him) beg for crusts from house to house; sometimes he has (him) pick gram out of the rubbish. As Ram keeps (us), so should one live, O brother; the Lord's glory cannot be told in any way. Sometimes he has (one) make fine steeds prance; sometimes (one) has not even shoes for the feet. Sometimes he lays (him) to sleep on a bed spread with white sheets; sometimes (he) has not so much as straw on the ground (to lie on). Says Namdev: the one Name alone saves; the one whom the Guru meets, (the Name) carries him across. ॥4॥
1164.3: (O Lord,) I came to your temple, laughing and playing; (but) as Nama worshipped, (they) seized (him) and made (him) rise. Low is my caste, O King of the Yadavs; why was I born into a calico printer's (home)? Taking up (my) blanket, I turned and went, and went and sat down behind the temple. As Nama utters the Lord's praises, the temple turns towards the Lord's humble devotee. ॥3॥
1164.4: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. As the hungry love grain, as the thirsty have need of water, as the fool is given over to his family, such is Nama's love for Narayan. Nama's love is fixed on Narayan; naturally, in Sahaj, he has become detached. As a woman is steeped in (love of) another man, (as) the greedy man is fond of wealth, (as) to the lustful man a woman is dear, such is Nama's love for Murari. That alone is (true) love which (the Lord) himself instils; by the Guru's grace double-mindedness goes; (that love) never breaks, (and one) stays merged (in him). Nama has fixed (his) mind on the True Name. As is the love of a child and (its) mother, so is (my) mind steeped in the Lord. Namdev humbly prays: (my) love has taken hold; Gobind dwells in my mind. ॥4॥
1164.5: The blind (man) forsakes the wife of his home, and carries on with another's woman. As the parrot is delighted at the sight of the simbal (silk-cotton) tree, (but) at the last dies clinging (to it). The sinner's home is in fire; it burns on and on, never quenched. He does not go to see the Lord's worship; leaving the road, he takes to the wrong way; strayed from the Root (of all), he comes and goes; throwing away Amrit, he loads up poison and eats it. As when a courtesan's dance is held, (the dancers) put on (fine) clothes and adorn themselves; she keeps the full beat and minds her breath; (yet) around her neck is the noose of Jam. He on whose forehead (the Lord's) grace is written runs to take the Guru's refuge. Says Namdev: this is (my) reflection: in this way, O Sants, cross over. ॥4॥
1165.1: Sanda and Marka went and complained: (Prahlad) will not study; we have worn ourselves out (on him); he says Ram and claps the beat with his hands; he has spoiled all the pupils. He keeps repeating the Name of Ram, and holds the remembrance of the dear Lord in his heart. The chief queen pleads: the king has brought the whole earth under his sway; (but) her son Prahlad does not heed her word; he has set his mind on something else. The council of the wicked met and laid a plan: we shall put an end to his days; (but) from the terrors of mountain, tree, water and fire Ram, the Sovereign Lord, kept (him), turning Maya's ways around. Drawing his sword of death, (Harnakhash), afraid (at heart), flew into a rage: tell me, who is there to save you? The Lord in yellow robes, the Master of the three worlds, speaks from within the pillar. He who tore Harnakhash apart with his claws, and gave gods and men a Master to shelter them, says Namdev: I meditate on (that) Narhari; Ram is the giver of the state free of fear. ॥5॥
1165.2: The Sultan asked: listen, you, Nama, let me see the works of your Ram. The Sultan had Nama bound (and said): let me see your Lord, (your) Bithal. Bring the slaughtered cow back to life, or else I will cut off (your) neck right here. (Nama said:) O king, how can such a thing be? no one slaughtered comes back to life. Nothing comes of my doing; what Ram does, that alone will be. The king rose up in his pride, and goaded a huge elephant on (at Nama). Nama's mother wept: (son,) why do you not leave Ram and worship Khuda? (Nama said:) I am not your child, nor are you my mother; even if the body falls, (Nama) will still sing the Lord's praises. The elephant struck with its trunk, (but) Nama was saved in the Lord's shelter. (The king said:) Qazis and Mullahs salute (me), (but) this Hindu has crushed my pride. (The people said:) O king, hear (our) plea: take gold to the weight of Nama. (The king said:) If I take the wealth, I shall fall into hell, leaving the faith to hoard (the goods of) the world. With fetters on (his) feet, keeping time with (his) hands, Nama sang the praises of Gopal. Even if the Ganga and the Jamuna flowed backwards, Nama would still keep on uttering Hari. When (Nama) heard that seven gharis had gone by, the Master of the three worlds had still not come. Then came the music of beating wings; Gobind came, riding on Garur (the king of birds). He took care of his own devotee; Gopal came, riding on Garur. (The Lord said:) If you say so, I will tilt the earth; if you say so, I will lift it and turn it over. If you say so, I will bring the dead cow to life, (that) all may see it and believe. Nama humbly asked: put the hobble (on the cow's legs); the calf was let to her, and the cow was milked. When the milking had filled the pitcher, (Nama) took it and laid it before the king. The king went off to his palace, and a hard hour came upon (him). Through the Qazis and Mullahs (the king) sent his plea: command (me); forgive (me), O Hindu; I am your cow. Nama said: hear, O king: give me some assurance of this. The measure of this assurance is this: walk in truth and gentleness, O Sultan. (Word of) Namdev spread everywhere; all the Hindus went together to Nama. (They said:) had the cow not come to life this time, the trust in Namdev would have been lost. Nama's fame endured in the world; (Nama) crossed over, taking the humble devotees with him. the slanderers had every grief and sorrow; between Nama and Narayan there is no difference. ॥28॥
Bithal (Vitthal): Namdev's name for God.
1166.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. If the divine Guru (is met), then Murari is met; If the divine Guru (is met), then one crosses over; If the divine Guru (is met), then one swims across to Baikunth; If the divine Guru (is met), then one dies while still living. True, true, true, true, true is the divine Guru; all other service is false, false, false, false. If the divine Guru (is met), then he makes the Naam firm (within); If the divine Guru (is met), (the mind) does not run in the ten directions; If the divine Guru (is met), (one stays) far from the five (enemies); If the divine Guru (is met), one does not die in grief. If the divine Guru (is met), then (one's) speech is Amrit; If the divine Guru (is met), then (one tells) the story of the Ineffable (Lord); If the divine Guru (is met), then the body (becomes as pure as) Amrit; If the divine Guru (is met), (people) repeat the Naam. If the divine Guru (is met), one has insight into the three worlds; If the divine Guru (is met), one comes to understand the high state; If the divine Guru (is met), then (one's) head is in the sky; If the divine Guru (is met), there is acclaim for ever. If the divine Guru (is met), one is ever detached; If the divine Guru (is met), slander of others is given up; If the divine Guru (is met), bad and good are one (to him); If the divine Guru (is met), (good) destiny (shows) on the forehead. If the divine Guru (is met), (no vice) plunders the body; If the divine Guru (is met), the temple turns (to face the devotee); If the divine Guru (is met), then the hut has been thatched; If the divine Guru (is met), the bed has been brought out (of the river). If the divine Guru (is met), then (one) has bathed at the sixty-eight (tiraths); If the divine Guru (is met), the marks of (Vishnu's) discus have been set upon the body; If the divine Guru (is met), then (one has done) the worship of the twelve (lingas of Shiv); If the divine Guru (is met), all poison (turns to sweet) fruit. If the divine Guru (is met), then doubt is broken; If the divine Guru (is met), then one is freed from Jam; If the divine Guru (is met), then one swims across the terrifying world-ocean; If the divine Guru (is met), then one is not born (again) to die. If the divine Guru (is met), (that is) the practice of the eighteen (Puranas); If the divine Guru (is met), (that is the offering of) the eighteen loads. Without the divine Guru there is no other place; Namdev (is) in the Guru's refuge. ॥9॥
By tradition, the Lord himself thatched Namdev's hut; and a bed a king had given Namdev, which Namdev had cast into the river, was brought back out of the water when the king asked for it.
1167.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Without seeing (him), no longing (for him) springs up; (and) whatever is seen perishes. He who repeats the Naam, along with (the Lord's) praise, is the yogi; he alone is free of desire. When anyone dwells on Ram, (his mind) is absorbed (in him); he touches the paaras, and double-mindedness is no more. He is a muni who devours the double-mindedness of the mind, and is merged in the One who pervades the three worlds, who has no doors (of a body). Everyone acts after the nature of his mind; (but he who) becomes (one with) the Creator abides free of fear. For the sake of fruit the plants come into flower; when the fruit sets, then the flower falls away. For the sake of knowledge deeds are practised; when knowledge has come, there deeds come to an end. For the sake of ghee the wise (woman) churns the curd; (so the one who knows is) liberated while alive, ever free of desire. Says Ravidas: (this is) the supreme detachment; why do you not repeat Ram in (your) heart, O luckless one? ॥4॥
1167.2: Raag Bhairao, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Come, O Kalandar, O Keshav (of the beautiful hair), (you) who have put on the garb of an Abdal. (You,) who have made the sky the cap on (your) head, and the seven netherworlds (your) sandals: (all) the skin-clad (beings) are your dwelling; thus are you arrayed, O Gopal. Fifty-six crore (clouds) are your robe, sixteen thousand (worlds) your trousers; the eighteen loads are your club, and the whole world your sahnak (a faqir's clay dish). (My) body is the mosque, the mind the Maulana, who offers the namaz of Sahaj; with Lady Kaula (Lakshmi) is your marriage, O Formless One, (Lord) of all that has form. As I worshipped, (you) had my cymbals snatched away; to whom shall I cry out? Nama's Master, the Inner-knower, roams through all the lands. ॥4॥
Kalandar: a wandering Muslim faqir; Abdal: a Muslim faqir.

1125.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Making (all things), you watch over them, and you yourself know their state.
What can one say? Nothing can be said.
Whatever there is, all is your will.
Whatever is to be done rests with you;
before whom (else) should a prayer be made?
(Our) speaking and hearing is your word (of praise) alone.
You yourself know (all), O Lord of every wonder.
(God) himself does, causes to be done, and knows;
O Nanak, setting up and pulling down, he watches over (all). ॥4॥
1125.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Through the Guru's Shabad (the Word) countless sages have crossed over; Indra and his like, Brahma and his like, have crossed over.
Sanak, Sanandan and countless ascetics have reached the far shore by the Guru's grace.
Without the Shabad, how can the world-ocean be crossed?
Without the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) the world is gripped by disease; in double-mindedness one drowns and drowns, and dies.
The Guru is the Divine; the Guru is the unseen, the unfathomable (Lord); in the Guru's service lies the understanding of the three worlds.
The Guru, the Giver, himself bestowed the gift, and the unseen, unfathomable (Lord) was found.
The mind is king: the mind has been won over by the mind itself, and desire has merged in the mind.
The mind is the yogi (joined to God); the mind, going to ruin, is the one separated (from him); the mind, when it understands, sings (his) praises.
Those who through the Guru have subdued the mind and reflected on the Shabad are rare in the world.
O Nanak, the Master pervades and fills (all); through the true Shabad comes deliverance. ॥4॥
1125.3: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
There is no sight in the eyes, the body is wasted; old age has conquered (you), and death (stands) over (your) head.
Beauty, colour and gladness do not last; how will the net of Jam (the messenger of Death) let (you) go?
O mortal, repeat (the Name of) the Lord: (your) life is slipping away.
Without the true Shabad you will never be released; (your) life has been in vain.
In the body are lust, anger, ego and possessiveness; (their) pain is hard and very heavy.
Through the Guru, repeat (the Name of) Ram (the Lord), and savour (its) taste with the tongue; in this way, swim, and cross over.
The ears are deaf, the intellect has grown shallow, (yet you) have not understood the Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) of the Shabad.
The manmukh (the self-willed) has gambled away the treasure of (human) life; without the Guru the blind one has not seen.
He who stays unattached, free of hope among hopes, a renunciant in the meditation of Sahaj,
Nanak humbly prays: (that one) is released through the Guru, his loving attention fixed on the Name of Ram. ॥4॥
1126.1: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(In old age) the gait is clumsy, the feet and hands give way, the skin of the body has withered;
the eyes are misted, the ears have gone deaf; (yet) the manmukh has not known the Naam.
O blind one, what have you gained by coming into the world?
Ram is not in (your) heart, nor the Guru's service; you are leaving, having lost (even your) capital.
The tongue is not dyed in the Lord's love; whenever it speaks, (its words are) insipid.
Caught up in slandering the Sants (saints), (such people) have become beasts; they never become good.
Only a rare one has tasted the Amrit (the nectar that gives spiritual life), (one whom the Lord) has brought into union with the True Guru.
As long as the secret of the Shabad has not come (to one), so long does death torment (him).
He who never knows another's door or house, (only) the one door of the True One,
by the Guru's grace he has attained the supreme state: so Nanak says, having reflected. ॥4॥
1126.2: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
All night you sleep, a noose around your neck; the day you have wasted in entanglements.
Not for an instant, a moment, a little while have you known God, who created this world.
O mind, how will you escape (this) heavy pain?
What did you bring, and what will you take away? Repeat (the Name of) Ram: (that alone) does good.
The manmukh's (heart-)lotus is upside down, (his) understanding shallow; because of the blind mind, worldly affairs (ride) on his head.
Death and birth hang ever over your head; without the Name the noose is around (your) neck.
The gait totters, and the eyes too are blind; (yet) attention to the Shabad has not pleased (you).
(Reading) the Shastras and the Vedas, (one) is still in Maya (the world's illusion and lure) of the three qualities; the blind one toils only at worldly affairs.
You have lost the capital: where will you find profit, O evil-minded one, empty of wisdom?
Those who, reflecting on the Shabad, have tasted the delight of Ram, O Nanak, are content in the True One. ॥4॥
1126.3: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(He who) stays with the Guru day and night, (keeps) Ram on (his) tongue, and is dyed in (his) love,
who knows no other, recognises the Shabad, and has known and recognised (the Lord) within —
such a servant is pleasing to my mind,
who, subduing his self, is dyed in the Infinite and does the work (the Guru gives him).
Within and without is the Being, Niranjan, free of the stain of Maya; to that primal Being, (my) salutation.
Within each and every heart, and in all without a break, the One whose form is true is pervading.
Those dyed in the True One have the true Amrit on (their) tongue, and not a mustard seed's worth of the filth of falsehood.
They have tasted the pure Naam, the delight of Amrit; dyed in the Shabad, they have won honour.
The virtuous, meeting the virtuous, earns the profit; through the Guru, in the Naam, (he finds) glory.
All sorrows are erased through the Guru's service; O Nanak, the Naam (becomes his) companion. ॥4॥
1127.1: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
To hold the Naam in the heart is all wealth and support; it is obtained by the Guru's grace.
Through this undying treasure one is fulfilled, and in the meditation of Sahaj one is attuned (to the Lord) in love.
O mind, one should fix one's thought on the devotion of Ram.
Through the Guru, repeat the Name of Ram in the heart: (so) one reaches (one's true) home in Sahaj.
Doubt, separation (from God) and fear are never shed; coming and going (in births), (one) does not understand.
Without the Lord's Name no one finds liberation; (such people) drown and die without water.
Busy with worldly affairs, you will lose all honour, O fool, and (your) doubt will not be erased.
Without the Guru's Shabad there is never liberation, O blind one; (there is only) the sprawl of worldly affairs.
(He whose) mind is at one with the Stainless One, who has no lineage, (his) mind has died through the mind itself;
within and without he has known the One alone; O Nanak, (for him) there is no other, no second. ॥4॥
1127.2: Raag Bhairao, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
With sacrifices, fire offerings, charity, austerities and worship, the body (still) suffers and ever endures pain;
without the Name of Ram (no one) finds liberation; through the Guru one obtains liberation in the Naam.
Without the Name of Ram, birth in the world is in vain.
(One) eats poison and speaks words of poison; without the Name (he) dies fruitless and wanders (in births).
(The pandit) expounds books, their recitation and grammar, and performs the sandhya rites at the three times of day;
(but) O mortal, where is liberation without the Guru's Shabad? Without the Name of Ram (he) dies entangled.
(Taking up) the staff and water-pot, the topknot, the sacred thread and the loincloth, (one) journeys to places of pilgrimage and wanders far and wide;
(but) without the Name of Ram peace does not come; he who repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har, crosses over.
(One) makes a crown of matted hair, smears ashes on the body, and leaving off clothes goes naked;
(but) without the Name of Ram there is no fulfilment; for one bound by his past deeds, (all this) is but a garb.
However many beings and creatures dwell in water, on land and in the sky, you, (O God), are everywhere, in every being.
By the Guru's grace, save your servant: Nanak has drunk the Lord's delight, savouring it. ॥5॥
1127.3: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Let no one take pride in (high) caste.
He who knows Brahm (God) is a Brahmin.
Do not take pride in caste, you foolish, ignorant one:
from this pride many evils spring.
Everyone speaks of the four varnas (castes);
(yet) all creation has come from the (one) seed of Brahm.
The whole world is one clay;
the Potter shapes (from it) vessels of many kinds.
The five elements join to make the form of the body;
who can reckon (them) less (in one) or more (in another)?
Says Nanak, this soul is bound by (its) deeds;
without meeting the True Guru, (it) is not set free. ॥5॥
1128.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Yogis, householders, pandits and the wearers of (religious) garbs:
these are asleep, (each) in his own pride.
Drunk with the wine of Maya, (the soul) lies asleep;
(he who) stays awake is robbed by no one.
He alone is awake who meets the True Guru;
he brings the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) under (his) control.
He alone is awake who reflects on the Essence;
he dies (to himself) and does not kill others.
He alone is awake who knows the One;
he leaves prakriti (the world of Maya) and recognises the Essence.
Whoever of the four varnas is awake
is released from Jam, from death.
Says Nanak, that servant is awake
in whose eyes is the collyrium of (divine) wisdom. ॥6॥
1128.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
He whom (God) keeps in his refuge
clings to the True One and obtains the true fruit.
O people, to whom (else) do you cry out?
By (his) Hukam (God's will and command) (all) came to be; by (his) Hukam (all) takes its course.
This (visible) form (of the world) is upheld by you, (O God);
in an instant it perishes, and (you) take no time to make (it).
(He to whom God) in his grace has shown (the world as) a play
has attained the supreme state by the Guru's grace.
Says Nanak, he (alone) kills and brings back to life;
understand (it) so, and let no one stray in doubt. ॥4॥
1128.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
I am the bride; the Creator is my Husband;
as he makes me do, so is the adornment I put on.
When it pleases him, he takes his delight (in me);
(my) body and mind are for the True Master (alone).
What praise or slander can anyone offer,
when he, the One, is himself at work (in all)?
By the Guru's grace, (I feel) the pull of love;
I shall meet the Merciful One, sounding the five Shabads (sounds).
Says Nanak, what can anyone do (against one)
1128.4: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
He alone is a muni (a silent sage) who kills the double-mindedness of the mind,
and, having killed double-mindedness, reflects on Brahm.
Let someone search out this mind, O brother:
searching the mind, the Naam, the nine treasures, is found.
Making attachment the root, the Creator brought forth the world;
attaching (it) to possessiveness, he led (it) astray in doubt.
From this mind (come) all bodies and breath;
through the mind's reflection, understanding the Hukam, (one) merges (in God).
(When God's) grace comes, the Guru shows mercy;
(then) this mind awakens, and the double-mindedness of this mind dies.
The mind's (true) nature is (that of) the ever-detached One,
who dwells in all, beyond (Maya), without attachment.
Says Nanak, he who knows this secret
(becomes one with) the primal Being, the Stainless, the Divine. ॥6॥
1129.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Name of Ram is the deliverance of the world;
it carries (one) over the world-ocean to the far shore.
By the Guru's grace, cherish the Lord's Name (in your heart);
it keeps faith with you for ever.
The foolish manmukhs do not keep the Naam in mind;
without the Name, how will they reach the far shore?
The Giver himself bestows the gift;
all praise to the One who gives.
(On whom God) casts his glance of grace, (him) he unites with the True Guru;
O Nanak, (and) he makes the Naam dwell in (his) heart. ॥4॥
1129.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
As many as there are in the worlds, all have been saved through the Naam alone —
those who receive it through the Guru.
(On whom) the dear Lord bestows his grace,
(him) he gives, through the Guru, the glory of the Naam.
Those who hold the Name of Ram in love and affection
are saved themselves, and (each) becomes the saviour of all (his) families.
Without the Name the manmukhs go to the city of Jam;
they are in torment and suffer blows.
O Nanak, (then) the Naam is received. ॥4॥
1129.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Love of Govind carried Sanak and his brothers across;
through the Shabad they reflected on the Name of Ram.
O dear Lord, bestow your grace (on me),
(that) through the Guru love for the Naam alone may take hold (of me).
When there is love within, and true devotion,
(then) union (with God) comes through the perfect Guru.
(Such a one) dwells in his own home, in Sahaj and in love;
through the Guru, the Naam comes to dwell in the mind.
O Nanak, keep the Naam enshrined in (your) heart. ॥4॥
1129.4: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Kalyug, enshrine the Name of Ram in (your) heart;
without the Name, (one) only puts ashes on (one's own) forehead.
The Name of Ram is hard to obtain, O brother;
it comes to dwell in the mind by the Guru's grace.
The servants who seek that Name of Ram
receive it from the perfect Guru.
The servants who accept the Lord's will are approved;
through the Guru's Shabad (they bear) the mark of the Naam.
Serve him who upholds (all) by his power;
O Nanak, through the Guru, love the Naam. ॥4॥
1129.5: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(but) it is not their season, nor are the rites accepted.
In Kalyug the Name of Ram is the essence (of all);
through the Guru, true love (for it) takes hold.
Searching body and mind, he has found (God) in (his own) house,
who through the Guru has fixed (his) thought on the Name of Ram.
The collyrium of (divine) wisdom comes from the True Guru;
(then) the Name of Ram (is seen) pervading the three worlds.
In Kalyug (it is the season of) the one dear Lord alone; there is no other season.
O Nanak, through the Guru, make the Name of Ram take root in (your) heart. ॥4॥
1130.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The manmukhs are gripped by the disease of double-mindedness; they burn greatly in craving.
Dying again and again they are born, and find no resting place; (they have) wasted (their) life in vain.
O my Beloved, be merciful and grant (me) understanding.
The world has been made sick with Haumai (ego); without the Shabad the sickness does not go.
Countless sages read the Simritis and the Shastras, (but) without the Shabad (true) awareness is not gained.
All who live in the three qualities are gripped by the disease; possessiveness has robbed (them of) awareness.
Some God himself has drawn out (of it); God himself has set (them) to the Guru's service.
They have found the treasure of the Lord's Name, and peace has come to dwell in (their) minds.
The Gurmukhs (those who follow the Guru) live in the fourth state; they have found a dwelling in their own home.
The perfect True Guru has shown (them) mercy, and (they) have rid themselves of self from within.
Over every head is the command of the One alone, who created Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra (Shiv);
O Nanak, the One alone is unmoving and true; he neither dies nor is born. ॥5॥
1130.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh, in double-mindedness, is ever sick; the whole world is sick.
The Gurmukhs understand (this), and rid themselves of the sickness by reflecting on the Guru's Shabad.
O dear Lord, unite (me) with the Sat Sangat (the company of the true).
O Nanak, (the Lord) gives glory to him who fixes (his) thought on the Name of Ram.
Through possessiveness all are gripped by the disease of death; Jam's rule is over their heads.
Jam does not come near the Gurmukh mortals who keep the Lord enshrined in their hearts.
Those who have not known the Lord's Name through the Guru, why did they come into the world?
They never did the Guru's service; they wasted (their) life in vain.
O Nanak, those whom (the Lord) has set to the True Guru's service are perfect and greatly fortunate;
whatever they wish, that fruit they obtain; through Gurbani (one) finds peace. ॥4॥
1130.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(The manmukh) is born in pain, dies in pain, and in pain goes about (his) work;
he never escapes the womb and the cycle of births; he stays sunk in filth.
Cursed, cursed is the manmukh: he has squandered (his) life;
he did not serve the perfect Guru, nor was the Lord's Name pleasing (to him).
The Guru's Shabad takes away every disease of the one whom the dear Lord joins (to it).
Through the Naam, in the Naam alone, glory comes to the one in whose mind (the Lord) makes (it) dwell.
When the True Guru is met, then (one) obtains the fruit: true living, the essence of peace.
Pure are the servants who cling to the Lord and set (their) love on the Lord's Name.
Should I find the dust (of the feet) of those who have meditated on the perfect True Guru, I would put it on (my) forehead.
O Nanak, the dust of those who have fixed (their) thought on the Name of Ram is found by perfect fortune. ॥4॥
1131.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The servant who reflects on the Shabad is true; those in whose hearts that True One (dwells)
(and who) practise true devotion day and night — then no pain (touches their) body.
Everyone talks of the devotee, the devotee;
(but) without serving the True Guru, devotion is not found; that God is met by perfect fortune.
The manmukhs lose (their) capital and ask for gain; where can any gain or profit come from?
Jam, Death, stands ever over (their) heads; in the love of another, (they) have lost (their) honour.
In many garbs (people) roam day and night, (but) the disease of Haumai does not go.
Reading and reading, they wrangle and dispute; joined to Maya, (they) have lost (their) awareness.
Those who serve the True Guru attain the supreme state; through the Naam (they) receive glory.
O Nanak, those in whose minds the Naam has come to dwell have won honour at the True One's door. ॥4॥
1131.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh's hope never leaves (him); in the love of another (he) comes to ruin.
Like a river, (his) belly is never filled; the fire of craving burns him away.
Those dyed in the delight of Ram are ever in bliss.
The Naam is in (their) hearts, double-mindedness has fled from (their) minds; drinking the Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, (they) are satisfied.
The Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), who fashioned the creation, himself sets each and every one to (his) task;
he who himself made attachment to Maya himself sets (beings) on (the love of) another.
If there were a second, something could be said to that one; (O God,) all are merged in you.
(He who) through the Guru has reflected on the essence of (divine) wisdom, (God) merges (his) light in the Light.
That God is true, true for ever; true is the whole of (his) visible form.
O Nanak, the True Guru has given (this) understanding: through the True Name comes deliverance. ॥4॥
1131.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Kalyug those who have not recognised Ram are ghosts; in Satjug those who reflected (on him) were Param Hans (supreme swans);
in Duapar and Treta (too such) humans live; a rare one has subdued Haumai.
In Kalyug, glory (comes) through the Name of Ram.
In every age the Gurmukh has known the One; without the Name, liberation is not found.
The true servant perceives the Naam in (his) heart; through the Guru, he enshrines it in (his) mind.
Those who are attuned in love to the Name of Ram have crossed over, and carried across all (their) families too.
My God is the giver of virtue; through the Shabad he burns away faults.
The servants in whose minds (he) has come to dwell are beautiful; (they) have enshrined the Naam in (their) hearts.
(He to whom) the True Guru has shown (the Lord's) home, door and mansion delights in (his) love;
whatever (the Guru) says, he accepts as good; O Nanak, he utters the Naam. ॥4॥
1132.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Merge the mind's desire back into the mind, by reflecting on the Guru's Shabad.
(He who) gains understanding from the perfect Guru does not die again and again.
O my mind, the Name of Ram is (your) support;
(he who takes it), by the Guru's grace, has attained the supreme state; (the Lord) is the fulfiller of every wish.
The One alone pervades all; without the Guru, this is not understood.
(He in whom) my Lord God has been revealed through the Guru sings the Lord's praises night and day.
The Lord alone is the giver of peace; elsewhere (people) find no peace.
Those who have not served the True Guru, the Giver, go at the last, repenting.
(He who), serving the True Guru, has found lasting peace: pain does not rush upon (him) again.
O Nanak, (he) has received the Lord's devotion; (his) light merges in the Light. ॥4॥
1132.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without the Guru the world has gone mad; gone astray, it suffers blows.
Dying again and again it is born, ever in pain; it finds no word of (the Lord's) door.
O my mind, ever remain in the True Guru's refuge.
(so) the Lord's Name feels ever sweet in the heart, and by the Guru's Shabad the world-ocean is crossed.
(One) puts on many garbs, (but his) mind wavers; within are lust, anger and pride.
Within is thirst and very great hunger; he goes barking from door to door.
Those who die through the Guru's Shabad and then live find liberation at (the Lord's) door.
Within (them) is calm, and lasting peace, (for they) keep the Lord enshrined in (their) hearts.
As it pleases him, so he makes (beings) walk; nothing (else) can be done.
O Nanak, through the Guru (one) cherishes the Shabad, (and finds) glory in the Name of Ram. ॥4॥
1132.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Haumai and attachment to Maya have led (the manmukh) astray; he earns pain and eats pain.
Within is greed, (like) rabies, a heavy affliction; without discernment he wanders.
Cursed is the manmukh's life in the world;
not even in a dream has he called the Name of Ram to mind; never does he come to love the Lord.
He does the deeds of beasts and does not understand; he practises falsehood and becomes false.
If the True Guru is met, (his mind) is turned around; some rare servant searches and finds (the Lord).
(He in whose) heart the Name of the Lord, Har Har, ever dwells has found the treasure of virtues;
by the Guru's grace he has found the Perfect One, and the pride of (his) mind is ended.
The Creator himself does and causes (all) to be done; he himself sets (one) on the path;
he himself gives glory through the Guru; O Nanak, (such a one) merges in the Naam. ॥4॥
1133.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Write on my tablet (the Name of) Hari, Govind, Gopal.
In the love of another, (people) are caught in Jam's net.
The True Guru cherishes and keeps me;
the Lord, the giver of peace, is with me.
By the Guru's teaching Prahlad utters (the Name of) the Lord;
the child does not worry over punishment.
His mother counsels (him): O dear Prahlad,
son, give up the Name of Ram, and save your life.
Prahlad says: Listen, O my mother,
I will not give up the Name of Ram; the Guru has made me understand (it).
Sanda, Marka and all the rest went and complained:
Prahlad has gone astray himself, and has led all the pupils astray.
In the assembly of the wicked a plot was settled;
(but) the Lord, Raghurai, becomes Prahlad's protector.
(Harnakhash) rushed (at him), sword in hand, in great pride:
Where is your Lord, who would save you?
In an instant a fearsome form came forth, tearing the pillar open;
(the Lord) tore Harnakhash apart with his claws, and saved Prahlad.
The dear Lord brings the tasks of the Sants to good;
he saved twenty-one generations of his servant Prahlad.
Through the Guru's Shabad (he) kills the poison of Haumai;
O Nanak, through the Name of Ram (he) carries the Sants across. ॥5॥
1133.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(God) himself sets demons upon the Sants, and he himself is (their) protector.
(O God,) those who are ever in your refuge have no pain in their minds.
In every age (the Lord) has kept (the honour) of his devotees.
The demon's son Prahlad knows nothing of the Gayatri or of tarpan; through the Shabad (the Lord) has united him in union with himself.
(The devotees) practise devotion at all hours, day and night; through the Shabad (they) have shed double-mindedness.
Ever pure are those who are dyed in the True One; that True One dwells in (their) minds.
The fools read (the lore of) double-mindedness and do not recognise the Root (of all); they have wasted their life in vain.
They slander the Sants; (they) stirred up the wicked demon.
Prahlad does not read (the lore of) double-mindedness, does not give up the Lord's Name, and is not frightened by anyone's threats.
The dear Lord is the protector of the Sants; the demon's death drew near.
(The Lord) himself keeps his own honour, and gives glory to the devotees.
O Nanak, (the Lord) tore Harnakhash apart with his claws; the blind (demon) found no word of (the Lord's) door. ॥5॥
1133.3: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(The Lord) in his grace attaches (one) to the feet of the Sants, the Lord's servants;
through the Guru's Shabad meditate on the Lord, and let (your) awareness merge (in him).
O my mind, meditate on the Name of the Lord, Narayan.
(He on whom) the Lord, Har Har, the giver of peace, shows his grace, (him) he carries across the world-ocean through the Guru, by the Lord's Name.
Joining the company of the Saadh (the holy one), sing of the Lord;
through the Guru's teaching take (the Name of) Ram, the home of all delights.
Bathe in the pool of the Amrit wisdom of the Guru, the holy one;
(so) all misdeeds and sins are destroyed.
(O God,) you yourself are the Creator, and the universe rests on you;
unite servant Nanak, the slave of your slaves, (with yourself). ॥4॥
1134.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Utter the Lord's Name; fruitful is that moment (when it is uttered);
by the Guru's teaching all pains are dispelled.
O my mind, meditate on the Name of the Lord, Narhari.
(O God,) in your grace unite (me) with the perfect Guru, (that) in the company of the Sat Sangat (I) may cross the world-ocean.
Meditate on the Life of the world, and in (your) mind remember the Lord;
(he) dispels your sins, millions upon millions.
(He on whose) face the dust (of the feet) of the Saadhs of the Sat Sangat has fallen
has bathed at the sixty-eight (tiraths) and in the Sursari (the Ganga).
The Lord has shown his grace to me, a fool;
the Lord who carries across has carried servant Nanak across. ॥4॥
1134.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Doing good deeds is the best (of all things), (and it is) the rosary;
turn it in (your) heart, and it will go along with you.
Repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Banwali.
(O God,) in your grace unite (us) with the Sat Sangat, (where) the noose of Maya, the noose of Jam, is broken.
He who has given himself to the toil of service, through the Guru:
for him the Shabad is fashioned in the true mint.
The Lord is beyond reach, beyond the senses; the Guru has shown (him) the One beyond reach;
searching within the city of the body, (he) has found the Lord.
We are children, the Lord is the father who cherishes (us);
with your glance of grace carry servant Nanak across. ॥4॥
1134.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
All bodies are yours, and you are within them all;
there is no one outside you.
O my mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, the giver of peace.
(O God,) I praise you; you are my Lord God, my father.
Wherever I look, there is that Lord God;
all is in your power; there is no other at all.
He whom it pleases you to protect, O Lord:
(O God,) you fill the water, the land and the sky; you are in all.
O servant Nanak, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, ever present, right before (you). ॥4॥
1134.4: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Lord's Sant, in whose heart is the Name of the Lord, Murari, is the Lord's own image.
He on whose forehead (such) destiny is written cherishes the Lord's Name in his heart, through the Guru's teaching.
One should repeat (the Name of) Madhusudan, enshrining (him) in the heart.
In the city of the body are five restless thieves; the Lord, through the Guru's Shabad, has struck (them) down and driven (them) out.
Those whose minds are at one with the Lord: the Lord himself brings their tasks to good.
Their dependence on people is ended; the Lord, the Creator, has taken their side.
Counsel and planning could be held only if anything were outside the Lord.
Whatever (he) does, that alone will be good; meditate night and day on the Name of the Lord, Murari.
Whatever the Lord does, he does it himself, by himself alone; he asks no one, and takes no one's counsel.
O Nanak, one should ever meditate on that God who in his grace has brought (us) to the True Guru. ॥4॥
1135.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Lord, my Master, unite (me) with those Saadhs who have meditated (on you), (that) I may be liberated.
