Seeing the sight of them the mind blossoms; every moment I am a sacrifice to them.
Repeat in (your) heart the Name of the Lord, Murari.
Show grace, show grace, O Father of the world, my Master: make me the water-carrier of the slaves of (your) slaves.
Excellent is their understanding, excellent their honour, in whose hearts Banwari dwells.
Attach (me) to their service, O Lord, my Master; remembering them, may I be liberated.
Those who have not found such a True Guru, the holy one, are beaten and driven out of the Lord's court.
Those slanderers find no honour; the Creator has cut off their noses.
The Lord himself makes (beings) speak, and himself speaks; the Lord himself is stainless, formless, needing no food.
O Lord, he whom you unite (with yourself) will meet you; O servant Nanak, what (power) have these poor creatures? ॥4॥
1135.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
That alone is your Sat Sangat, O Lord, in which the Lord's praise is heard.
Those who have heard the Lord's Name, and whose minds are drenched (in it): we ever serve their feet.
Meditating on the Lord, the Life of the world, (one) crosses over.
Many and countless are your Names, O Lord; with this tongue they cannot be counted.
O Gursikhs, utter the Lord('s Name), sing of the Lord; taking the Guru's teaching, repeat (the Name of) the Lord.
He who hears the Guru's teaching: that servant receives the Lord's abundant peace.
Blessed is that lineage, blessed that father, blessed that mother, who gave birth to (such) servants.
Those who have meditated on my Lord, Har Har, with every breath and every morsel, have become the Lord's servants in the true court.
O Lord, Har Har, your Names are beyond reach; (you) have placed them within your devotees, O Lord.
O Nanak, the servant who has received the understanding of the Guru's teaching crosses over, repeating (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
1136.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Setting all the (other) lunar days aside,
(you say) Govind was born on the eighth lunar day.
Men led astray by doubt talk nonsense;
Narayan is beyond birth and death.
Making panjiri, you feed it (to the idol) in secret;
he is neither born nor does he die, O saakat, dull as cattle!
You sing (the idol) lullabies, and in this lie all offences;
burnt be the mouth with which (you) say the Master enters births.
He is neither born nor dies, neither comes nor goes;
1136.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Rising, (one) is at peace; sitting, (one) is at peace;
no fear touches (one), once (one) understands this:
the One Master is our protector;
he is the Knower of all hearts.
(One) sleeps free of care, and wakes free of care:
O God, you are present everywhere.
(He) dwells in peace at home, and finds peace outside —
Says Nanak, (the one in whom) the Guru has made the mantra (of the Name) firm. ॥3॥
1136.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I keep neither (Hindu) fasts nor (the fasts of) the month of Ramadan;
I serve him who protects at the last.
My (Lord) is the One, Gosain and Allah;
(I) have settled my accounts with both Hindu and Turk.
I go neither on Hajj to the Kaaba nor to worship at tiraths;
I serve the One alone, and no other.
I neither perform puja nor offer namaz;
taking the One Formless Lord into (my) heart, I bow (to him).
We are neither Hindu nor Muslim;
(our) body and breath of life belong to Allah, to Ram.
Says Kabir: this I have declared:
meeting the Guru, the Pir, I have recognised my own Master. ॥5॥
1136.4: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In Sahaj (I) have bound and brought in the ten does;
the five deer (I) have pierced with the arrows of the Word of Shiv, the Auspicious One.
Taking the company of the Sants with me, I rode out to hunt;
(I) caught the deer without horses or weapons.
Bent on the hunt, (I) had come running outside;
(but) I found the game in the village of (my own) home.
Catching the deer, (I) brought them home, to the shop;
(the Sants) shared them out and carried them off, bit by bit.
This game has been given away as a gift;
in Nanak's house is the Name alone. ॥4॥
1136.5: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Though (he) be fed (the Name) a hundred times with longing care,
the Lord, Har Har, does not come into the saakat's mind.
Take the counsel of the Sants;
in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) attain the supreme state.
Much water is poured over a stone,
(yet) it is not soaked, and stays bone dry.
The six Shastras are recited to a fool,
as though the wind were blowing in the ten directions.
As when a threshing floor without grain is threshed,
so from the saakat no one gains anything.
Each clings to that alone to which he has been attached;
says Nanak, God has made this arrangement. ॥5॥
1137.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He who fashioned the soul, the life-breath and the body,
he who created (beings) is the one who feels (their) pain.
The Guru, Gobind, is the soul's help,
whose shade (is over us) always, in this world and the next.
To worship God in adoration is the pure way;
in the Saadh Sangat the perverse bent is destroyed.
Friends, well-wishers and wealth are no support (to the soul);
blessed, blessed are you, my Narayan.
know no other but the One. ॥4॥
1137.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ahead (of me) is the Merciful, behind (me) is Narayan;
in the middle part is the Lord, the home of love's delights.
God is, for us, the Shastra of omens;
peace, Sahaj and bliss fill (our) house and home.
Uttering the Naam with the tongue and hearing it with the ears, (they) have come alive;
remembering, remembering God, (they) have become immortal and steadfast.
(They) have dispelled the sorrows of birth after birth;
the unstruck (Anhad) Shabad plays in (their inner) court.
In his grace God has united with himself
O Nanak, (those who) have come to God's refuge. ॥4॥
1137.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Millions of heart's desires come to hand;
on the road of Jam, (the Name) is the traveller's companion.
The Name of the Guru, of Gobind, is the (true) water of the Ganga.
Whoever remembers it is liberated; drinking it, (one) wanders through births no more.
(The Name is) worship, chanting, austerity and holy bathing;
remembering the Name, (people) have become free of desire.
(The Name is) kingdom, riches, mansions and royal courts;
remembering the Name, (one's) conduct becomes perfect.
Slave Nanak has reflected and found this:
without the Lord's Name all is false, (mere) ashes. ॥4॥
1137.4: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Not a sesame seed's worth of stain has touched (the Lord's servant) at all;
the wicked Brahmin has died in the agony of colic.
The Supreme Lord himself has protected the Lord's servants;
by the Guru's glory the sinner has died.
The servant has himself meditated on his own Master;
that foolish sinner (the Lord) himself has destroyed.
God, mother and father (to him), is the protector of his own slave;
the slanderer's brow is blackened, here and hereafter.
The Supreme God has heard servant Nanak's prayer;
the vile sinner has wasted away, his hopes dashed. ॥4॥
1137.5: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Good, good, good, good, good is your Name;
false, false, false, false is the pride of the world.
Beautiful are your servants; the sight of them is beyond measure;
without the Name the whole world is ashes.
Wondrous is your creation; your feet are worthy of praise;
priceless is your praise, O true King.
God (Khuda) is the support of the unsupported, (their) shelter;
(he) raises up the poor; meditate (on him) day and night.
On Nanak the Master himself is merciful;
Allah does not slip from (his) heart, soul and breath. ॥4॥
1138.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through the Guru, obtain the true wealth;
bear God's will, accepting it as true.
rising each day, drink (the Name of) Ram, the home of all delights;
say with the tongue: Har Har, Har Har.
In Kalyug, deliverance comes through the Name alone;
1138.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Serving the True Guru, (one) obtains all fruits;
(and) wipes away the filth of birth after birth.
O God, your Name purifies the fallen;
the singing of (your) praises (comes to one) by the deeds written in the past.
In the company of the Saadh deliverance comes;
All good lies in the service of God's feet;
all the angels, men and gods long for (that servant's) dust.
Nanak has found the treasure of the Name;
repeating, repeating (the Name of) the Lord, the whole world is saved. ॥4॥
1138.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Lord) clasps his slave to his bosom;
the slanderer he casts into the fire.
Narayan protects (his slave) from the sinner;
the sinner finds release nowhere; the sinner is consumed by his own deeds.
The slave has come to love the dear Lord, Ram;
the slanderer has taken the perverse bent.
The Supreme Lord has made his innate nature manifest;
the evil-doer has reaped what he did.
(He) neither comes nor goes; he pervades all.
Slave Nanak is in the Lord's refuge. ॥4॥
1138.4: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Sridhar, the Enchanter (Mohan), the Creator of all, the Formless One, the giver of peace:
forsaking such a God you serve others: by what pleasures of poisonous Maya are you intoxicated?
O my mind, meditate on Govind.
I have looked at all other means; whatever (other) one devises, by it the task is spoiled.
Forsaking the Master, the blind and ignorant manmukhs remember (his) handmaid (Maya);
those who worship the Lord they slander, Guru-less, like beasts.
Soul, frame, body and wealth: all is God's; the saakats say, (it is) mine.
(Their) proud intellect is evil-minded and filthy; without the Guru (they) go round and round in the world-ocean.
By burnt offerings, sacrifices, chanting, austerities and every discipline, at river-banks and tiraths, (God) is not found.
Self-conceit was erased of those who took (his) refuge; O Nanak, through the Guru (he) has carried the world across. ॥4॥
1139.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have seen (him) in the forest, seen (him) in the grass, seen (him) in the home and in the renunciate's life;
I have seen (him) among the staff-bearers and the wearers of matted hair, in fasts, vows and tiraths.
In the company of the Sants I have seen (him) within the mind;
(he) fills the heavens, the netherworlds and all; with delight I have sung his joyful praises.
I have seen (him) among yogis, all the garbs and sannyasis, among celibates, Jangams and wearers of patched coats;
I have seen (him) among ascetics, great ascetics and sages, among actors, plays and dances.
Within the four (Vedas) I have seen (him), within the six (Shastras) seen (him), in the eighteen (Puranas) and the Simritis;
all together speak of the One, the One alone; then from whom shall I call him hidden?
The Master is beyond grasp, beyond grasp, endless; his worth cannot be priced, cannot be priced.
O servant Nanak, one should be a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those in whose hearts he has become manifest. ॥4॥
1139.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He who knows (God) to be near: why would he do evil?
(He who) hoards poison (Maya) goes about ever afraid.
(God) is near, yet (one) has not found (this) secret;
without the True Guru, Maya has enticed all.
Near, near (is he), everyone says;
(but) some rare one, through the Guru, grasps the secret.
(He who) does not see (him) near goes into another's house;
he steals wealth, and lives by falsehood.
the drug of the cheat has been cast upon him; he has not known the Lord to be with (him);
without the Guru, he is led astray by doubt.
(He who) does not know (him) near speaks falsehood;
the fool is robbed by attachment to Maya.
The treasure (of the Name) is within, (but) he goes off to other lands;
without the Guru, he is led astray by doubt.
He on whose forehead, on whose brow, (the Lord's) grace is written
serves the True Guru, and (his) closed doors open.
Within and without, that One is near (him);
O servant Nanak, (for him) no one comes or goes. ॥4॥
1139.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Whom you protect, who can kill him?
All, the whole world, is within you alone.
The mortal devises millions of schemes,
(but) that alone comes to pass which the Lord, who works wonders, does.
Protect (me), protect (me), in your grace;
(I have come) to your refuge, to your court.
He who has served the Fearless One, the giver of peace,
has cast off fear, and recognised the One.
Whatever you do, that alone comes to pass;
no other kills or protects.
What are you thinking, in your human way?
The all-pervading Being knows every heart, and is all-wise.
The One is the prop, the One alone the support;
the Creator knows everything.
He on whom the Creator casts his glance of grace:
all the affairs of that servant (he) brings to good.
His protector is that One alone;
O servant Nanak, no one can reach (him). ॥4॥
1140.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One should fret if (God) were outside (anything);
one should fret if Narhari were forgotten;
one should fret if another (than he) were dear (to one);
(but) why should one fret, when (he) pervades (all)?
In attachment to Maya, (man) frets and frets and burns away;
without the Name, wandering, wandering, wandering, he is worn out.
One should fret if there were another Creator;
one should fret if anyone died unjustly;
one should fret if (God) knew nothing;
(but) why should one fret, when (you) fill and pervade (all)?
One should fret if anything happened by force (against his will);
one should fret if (he) caused (anyone) pain by mistake.
The Guru has said that whatever happens, all is from God;
since then, leaving (all) fretting, we sleep free of care.
O God, you alone are the Master; everyone is yours;
as it pleases (you), so you decide.
There is no second; (you,) the One, pervade (all);
keep (my) honour: Nanak is in (your) refuge. ॥4॥
1140.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Without instruments, what is a dance?
Without a throat, how can a singer (sing)?
Without the string, how can the rabab sound?
Without the Name, all deeds are in vain.
Without the Name, say, who has crossed over?
Without the True Guru, how has anyone got across?
Without a tongue, where is a speaker?
without ears, where is a hearer?
without eyes, how does anyone see?
Without the Name, man counts for nothing anywhere.
Without learning, how can anyone be a pandit?
Without authority to command, what is the splendour of a kingdom?
Without understanding, how can the mind be still?
Without the Name, the whole world has gone mad.
Without detachment, how can one be a renunciant?
Without renouncing Haumai, how can anyone be one who renounces?
Without bringing the five enemies under control, how can the mind be subdued?
Without the Name, (one) grieves for ever and ever.
Without the Guru's teaching, how can there be wisdom?
Without seeing (him), say, what meditation can there be?
Without (God's) fear, all talk is vice;
says Nanak, such is the understanding of (the Lord's) door. ॥5॥
1140.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) has given man the sickness of Haumai;
through the sickness of lust the elephant is held captive;
through the sickness of sight the moths burn to death;
through the sickness of sound the deer have perished.
Whatever is seen, all of it is sick;
free of sickness is my True Guru, the (true) yogi.
Through the sickness of the tongue the fish is caught;
through the sickness of scent the bumble-bee is destroyed;
the whole world is (stricken with) the sickness of attachment;
in the threefold sickness (of the three qualities) the vices have grown.
In sickness (one) dies, in sickness (one) is born;
in sickness (one) roams through births again and again.
Bound by sickness, (one) finds not the least stillness;
without the True Guru the sickness never goes.
The one on whom the Supreme Lord has shown mercy,
(God) has taken (him) by the arm and pulled (him) out of the sickness;
(his) bonds were broken, (he) found the Saadh Sangat.
Says Nanak, the Guru has cured (his) sickness. ॥4॥
1141.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When (God) comes to mind, there is supreme bliss;
When (he) comes to mind, all sorrows are shattered;
When (he) comes to mind, (one's) longing is fulfilled;
When (he) comes to mind, (one) never grieves.
Ram, the King, has come and become manifest within (me);
the perfect Guru has dyed (me) in (his) love.
When (he) comes to mind, (one) is king over all;
When (he) comes to mind, (all) tasks are fulfilled;
When (he) comes to mind, (one) is dyed the deep crimson (of love);
When (he) comes to mind, (one) is ever in delight.
When (he) comes to mind, (one) is wealthy forever;
When (he) comes to mind, (one) is ever free of doubt;
When (he) comes to mind, (one) enjoys all delights;
When (he) comes to mind, dependence (on anyone) is ended.
When (he) comes to mind, (one) finds the home of Sahaj;
When (he) comes to mind, (one) is absorbed in Sunn;
When (he) comes to mind, (one) sings Kirtan (songs of God's praise) forever;
O Nanak, (his) mind is at one with the Lord. ॥4॥
1141.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My Father (God) is ever-living;
my brothers live for ever;
my friends are imperishable for ever;
my family dwells in its own (true) home.
I have found peace, and so all are at ease;
the perfect Guru has united (me) with the Father.
My mansions are higher than all;
my lands are boundless, beyond (anyone's) questioning;
my rule is ever unshakeable;
my wealth is inexhaustible and abiding.
My glory (lives) through all the ages;
my renown (rings out) in every place and every space between;
my praise is (sung) in every home;
my devotion (is known) among all people.
My Father has become manifest within (me);
Father and son, together, have formed a bond.
Says Nanak, when the Father was pleased,
Father and son were absorbed in the one love. ॥4॥
1141.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Being without enmity, O True Guru, O God the Giver,
we are offenders, you are the forgiver.
The sinner who finds shelter nowhere,
if he comes to (your) refuge, becomes pure.
Winning the True Guru over, (I) have obtained peace;
meditating on the Guru, (I) have received all fruits.
O Supreme Lord, O True Guru, (to you) my salutation.
(My) mind and body are yours; all the land is yours.
When the veil was removed, (you) came into sight:
you are the Master, O King of all.
When it pleased him, the dry wood turned green;
when it pleased him, there was a lake on the dry land;
when it pleased him, all fruits were obtained;
anxiety left, by falling at the True Guru's feet.
(God) has been gracious to the ungrateful, the one without virtue;
mind and body are cooled, Amrit has rained into the mind.
The Supreme Lord, the Guru, has become merciful;
O Nanak, the servants, beholding (him), are in rapture. ॥4॥
1142.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My True Guru depends on no one;
the way of my True Guru is true for ever;
my True Guru is the one who gives to all;
my True Guru is the all-pervading Being, the Creator.
There is no deity like the Guru;
he on whose forehead (good) fortune is (written) takes up (his) service.
My True Guru cherishes all;
my True Guru kills and brings to life.
The glory of my True Guru
is made manifest in every place.
My True Guru is the strength of the strengthless;
my True Guru is the support in (my) home.
I am ever a sacrifice to the True Guru,
who has made the path plain and shown it.
He who has served the Guru: fear does not touch him;
he who has served the Guru: pain does not torment him.
Nanak has searched the Simritis and the Vedas:
between the Supreme Lord and the Guru there is no difference. ॥4॥
1142.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeating the Naam, the mind has come to light;
repeating the Naam, sin has left the body;
repeating the Naam, all the holy days have been kept;
repeating the Naam, (one) has bathed at the sixty-eight (tiraths).
Our tirath is the Name of the Lord;
the Guru has taught (this) essence of wisdom.
Repeating the Naam, pain has fled far;
repeating the Naam, the utter fool has become wise;
repeating the Naam, light has shone forth;
repeating the Naam, entanglements are undone.
Repeating the Naam, Jam does not come near;
repeating the Naam, (one) finds peace in the Lord's court;
repeating the Naam, God says, Well done;
the Naam is our true capital.
The Guru has told (me) this teaching, the essence:
the praise of the Lord and the Naam are the support of the mind.
O Nanak, through the atonement of the Name (people) are saved;
other rites are (only) to win people's trust. ॥4॥
1142.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Salutation to him a hundred thousand times;
one should offer this mind to him as a sacrifice.
In his remembrance, torments are erased;
there is bliss, and no fevers afflict (one).
Such a diamond is the immaculate Name
by repeating which all tasks are fulfilled.
He by whose glance the camp of sorrow is torn down,
(and one) holds the cooling Amrit Naam in the mind;
he whose feet countless devotees worship,
(he) is the fulfiller of all desires.
In an instant (he) has filled the empty to the brim;
in an instant (he) has made the withered green;
in an instant (he) has given the homeless a place;
in an instant (he) has given honour to the dishonoured.
The One fills and pervades all;
(but) he alone repeats (his Name) whose True Guru is perfect;
the Lord's Kirtan is the support of that one
on whom, says Nanak, (God) himself is merciful. ॥4॥
1143.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Me, the forsaken bride, (the Lord) himself has adorned;
giving (me) beauty and colour, (he) has embellished (me) with the Name.
Sorrow and all torment are gone;
the Guru has become my mother and father.
O friends, O companions, there is bliss in my home;
in (his) grace my Husband (the Lord) has met me.
The burning (of craving) is quenched; all hopes are fulfilled;
the darkness is gone, light has dawned;
the Anhad Shabad (resounds), wondrous and amazing;
perfect is the Guru, perfect (his) grace.
He to whom Gopal has become manifest:
by the sight of him (one) is ever in rapture;
in him are all virtues and great treasures,
to whom the True Guru has given the Naam.
He whom his own Master has met:
(his) mind and body are cooled, repeating Har Har.
Says Nanak, those servants who are pleasing to God:
the dust (of their feet) some rare one obtains. ॥4॥
1143.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In plotting sins, (he) feels no sloth;
going to a prostitute, (he) feels no shame at all;
all day long (he) toils for wages;
(but) at the time to remember the Lord, a thunderbolt falls on (his) head.
Clinging to Maya, the world has gone astray;
the One who leads astray has himself led (it) astray; (it) is absorbed in empty dealings.
Watching the pageants of Maya, (his life) passes away;
in love with a cowrie shell, (he) deals crookedly;
the mind runs in the bonds of blind dealings;
(but) the Creator does not come into (his) heart.
Doing thus, and doing, (he) has met with pain;
the tasks of Maya are never completed;
(his) mind is sunk in lust, anger and greed;
(he) has died writhing, like a fish without water.
He whose protector the Lord himself has become
ever repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har;
(he) has sung the Lord's praises in the Saadh Sangat;
O Nanak, (he) has found the perfect True Guru. ॥4॥
1143.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(On whom God) shows his mercy, that one obtains (the Naam);
(he) enshrines the Lord's Name in (his) mind.
The true Shabad (abides) in (his) heart and mind;
(his) sins of birth after birth depart.
The Name of Ram is the support of the soul;
by the Guru's grace, repeat it daily, O brothers; it carries (you) across the world-ocean.
Those for whom the Lord has written this treasure (in their fate),
those servants receive honour in the Lord's court.
Sing (his) praises in peace, Sahaj and bliss;
hereafter (even) the homeless find a place.
Through age upon age this is the essence, the quintessence:
remembrance of the Lord is the true reflection.
He whom (God) attaches to (his) hem, he alone is attached;
asleep for birth after birth, (he) awakens.
(O God, they are) your devotees; you yourself are the devotees' own;
you yourself chant your own glory.
All beings and creatures are in your hands;
O God of Nanak, (you are) ever with (all). ॥4॥
1144.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
For me the Naam is the inner Knower;
for me the Naam is of use;
the Lord's Name pervades (my) every pore;
the perfect True Guru has given (this) gift.
The jewel of the Naam is in my storehouse,
beyond reach, priceless, infinite, boundless.
For me the Naam is the unshakeable Master;
the glory of the Name shines in all;
for me the Naam is the perfect banker;
for me the Naam is the carefree (Lord).
For me the Naam is food and love;
for me the Naam is the mind's aim;
by the Sant's grace the Naam is not forgotten;
repeating the Naam, the Anhad sounds ring out in full.
By God's grace (I) have obtained the Naam, the nine treasures;
by the Guru's grace (I) have come into accord with the Name.
They alone are wealthy, (they) the eminent,
O Nanak, who have the treasure of the Name. ॥4॥
1144.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord), you are my father, you are my mother;
you are the giver of peace to my soul and breath of life;
you are my Master, I am your servant;
without you, I have no other.
In your grace, O God, grant (this) gift:
that I may praise you day and night.
We are your instruments, you are the player;
we are your beggars; give (us) alms, O Giver.
By your grace (we) enjoy love and delight;
within every heart it is you who pervade.
(O God,) by your grace (your) Name is repeated;
in the Saadh Sangat (may I) sing your praises;
by your kindness, pain is destroyed;
by your mercy, the lotus (of the heart) blossoms.
I am a sacrifice to the divine Guru,
whose sight bears fruit, whose service is pure.
Be kind, O my Master, my God,
that Nanak may sing your praises always. ॥4॥
1144.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He whose court stands highest of all:
to him be salutation for ever and ever;
he whose seat is higher than the high:
through (that) Lord's Name millions of sins are erased.
In his refuge there is peace for ever
(for the one) whom he, in his grace, unites (with himself).
He whose works cannot be fathomed,
in whom every heart puts its trust,
has become manifest in the company of the Saadh;
the devotees worship (him) with love, night and day.
Giving and giving, (his) storehouses never run short;
in an instant (God) can set up and pull down;
he whose Hukam no one can erase,
that True One is over the heads of kings.
In whose shelter (we are), in him alone is (our) hope;
our pain and pleasure (rest) with him alone.
(He) has preserved his servant's honour in full;
Nanak sings his praise. ॥4॥
1145.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The mourning woman has made (her weeping) a daily rite;
(for) the bond (with the dead) has come to (her) mind, for the sake of goods and their use.
If anyone, understanding (this), turns detached,
(he) grieves no more over birth and death.
All this business and expanse is of poisonous Maya;
some rare one has made the Name (his) support.
Maya of the three qualities holds sway (over all);
whoever clings (to it) meets pain and torment.
There is no peace without meditating on the Name;
the treasure of the Name (only) the very fortunate one obtains.
He who gives (his) heart to a player in disguise
regrets it once the disguise is taken off.
As (it goes with) one who would take shelter in a cloud's shade,
so (it goes with) this expanse of attachment and vice.
If anyone obtains the One Thing,
his task alone is fulfilled.
He who, by the Guru's grace, has obtained the Naam:
O Nanak, his coming (into the world) is approved. ॥4॥
1145.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Slander of a Sant (makes one) wander through births;
slander of a Sant makes (one) sick;
through slander of a Sant (one) suffers pain;
Jam punishes the slanderer.
Those who quarrel with a Sant:
those slanderers taste no joy at all.
Slander of a devotee gets (the slanderer's) body shattered;
slander of a devotee makes (one) suffer hell;
through slander of a devotee (one) rots in the womb;
through slander of a devotee (one) falls from sovereignty.
The slanderer finds release nowhere;
what (slanderers) sow, they themselves eat.
(The slanderer) is worse than a thief, an adulterer or a gambler;
the slanderer has set a needless load upon his own head.
The devotees of the Supreme Lord bear no enmity;
he who worships (their) feet crosses over.
The Primal Being (himself) has led the slanderer astray;
O Nanak, (the record of his) past deeds cannot be erased. ॥4॥
1145.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
For me the Naam is the Vedas and the Naad (of the yogi's horn);
for me the Naam is the fulfilment of (all) tasks;
for me the Naam is the worship of the gods;
for me the Naam is serving the Guru.
The Perfect Guru has made the Name of the Lord firm (within me);
the highest of all deeds is (repeating the Name of) the Lord, Har Har.
For me the Naam is the dip and the bath (at the tiraths);
for me the Naam is charity complete;
repeating the Naam, they all become pure;
those who repeat the Naam are my brothers and friends.
For me the Naam is omen and auspicious hour;
for me the Naam is contentment and choice delights;
for me the Naam is all religious observance;
for me the Naam is pure dealing.
Each one in whose mind the One God has come to dwell:
for all such servants, the Lord, Har Har, is the prop.
O Nanak, the singing of the Lord's praises (dwells) in the mind and body (of him)
to whom (God) gives the Name in the Saadh Sangat. ॥4॥
1146.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) to the poor you give wealth;
countless sins depart, the mind becomes pure;
all desires and tasks are fulfilled,
(when) you give your devotee (your) Name.
Fruitful is the service of Gopal, the King;
(he is) the Master who does and causes all to be done; from him no one goes away empty-handed.
O God, you destroy the sickness of the sick;
you erase the grief of the sorrowful, O God;
the homeless you seat in a place (of honour);
your servant you attach to (your) devotion.
To the dishonoured, O God, you give honour;
the foolish dullard becomes clever and wise;
the fear of all that is fearsome flees,
(when) the Lord dwells in the mind of his servant.
God, the Supreme Lord, is the treasure of peace;
the knowledge of the essence is the Lord's Amrit Naam.
(He whom God) in his grace attaches to the service of the Sants,
O Nanak, (he) stays absorbed in the company of the Saadh. ॥4॥
1146.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the assembly of the Sants the Lord comes to dwell in the mind;
in the assembly of the Sants all sin flees;
in the assembly of the Sants the way of life is pure;
in the company of the Sants love for the One arises.
That place is called the assembly of the Sants
(where) the praises of the Supreme Lord alone are sung.
In the assembly of the Sants (the round of) birth and death ends;
in the assembly of the Sants Jam says nothing (to one);
in the company of the Sants the pure Bani (is uttered);
in the assembly of the Sants the Naam is spoken.
The seat of the assembly of the Sants is unshakeable;
in the assembly of the Sants sins are destroyed;
in the assembly of the Sants (God's) pure discourse goes on;
in the company of the Sants the pain of Haumai flees.
The assembly of the Sants is never destroyed;
in the assembly of the Sants (dwells) the Lord, the treasure of virtues;
the assembly of the Sants is the resting-place of the Master;
O Nanak, (there) the Lord is woven (into the Sants), like warp and weft. ॥4॥
1146.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
What sickness (can touch one) when (God) himself protects?
That servant suffers neither pain nor anguish.
He on whom God shows mercy:
from over him (God) drives away death.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is a companion forever;
he in whose mind it comes is ever at peace; Jam does not come near him.
When this (being) was not, who then created (him)?
From what source, and in what form, has (he) brought (him) forth?
He himself kills, and himself gives life;
he ever cherishes his own devotee.
Know that all things are in his hands;
my God is the Lord of those who have no lord.
his Name is the Destroyer of sorrow;
sing his praises, and you will find peace.
O Master, hear the prayer of the Sants:
(our) soul, breath and wealth are in your keeping.
This world is yours; all meditate on you alone;
show mercy, that Nanak may find peace. ॥4॥
1147.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) on your support (I) live in Kalyug;
on your support (all) sing your praises;
on your support, death does not touch (one);
on your support, the entanglement (of Maya) is destroyed.
In faith and in the world, your support (is mine);
the one Master pervades all.
On your support (I) rejoice;
on your support (I) repeat the Guru's mantra;
on your support the ocean of fear is crossed;
the Protector is perfect, an ocean of peace.
On your support there is no fear at all;
that True One knows every heart.
on your support, your strength is in the mind;
here and hereafter you are (our) support.
(We have) your support and trust in you;
all meditate on (you), O God, treasure of virtues;
repeating (your Name) again and again, your servants rejoice;
O Nanak, remember the True One, the treasure of virtues. ॥4॥
1147.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
First, (he) has given up slandering others;
all the anxiety of (his) mind has gone;
greed and attachment, all, (he) has cast far away;
seeing God ever present, (he) is the supreme Vaishnav (the true devotee).
Rare is such a renunciant;
that servant repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
(He) has forsaken the company of the proud intellect;
the dye of lust and anger has faded (from him);
(he) meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har Hare;
(such people) have crossed over in the company of the holy.
Enemy and friend have become alike (to him);
the Lord fills all;
accepting God's will, (he) has found peace.
The Perfect Guru has made the Name of the Lord firm (within him).
He whom (God) himself, in his grace, protects:
that devotee alone chants the chant of the Name.
(he who) has taken counsel from the Guru has light in (his) mind;
says Nanak, his (labour) has come to fruition. ॥4॥
1147.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
No peace comes from earning great wealth;
no peace comes from watching dances and plays;
no peace comes from conquering many lands;
all peace lies in singing the praises of the Lord, Har Har.
Obtain peace, Sahaj and bliss;
the Saadh Sangat is found by great good fortune; through the Guru, utter the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Mother, father, son and wife are bonds;
bonds are the rites and pious deeds done with (the pride that) I am the doer;
(when) the One who cuts the bonds dwells in the mind,
then (one) finds peace and dwells in one's own home (within).
All are beggars; God is the Giver,
the treasure of virtues, endless and boundless.
He on whom (his) own God bestows grace:
that very servant will repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
(My) prayer is before my own Guru:
be gracious, O Being, treasure of virtues.
Says Nanak, (I have come) to your refuge;
keep (me) as it pleases (you), O Lord of the world. ॥4॥
1147.4: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(He who), meeting the Guru, has given up the love of another,
(who) through the Guru has repeated the Lord's Name:
(his) anxiety is forgotten, love for the Naam has taken hold (of him);
(he), though asleep for birth after birth, has awoken.
(He whom God) in his grace attaches to his own service
finds every peace in the company of the Saadh.
Through the Guru's Shabad (he) has rid (himself) of sickness and faults;
(he) keeps the medicine of the Naam within (his) mind;
meeting the Guru, bliss has come into (his) mind;
the Name of the Lord holds all treasures.
The terror of Jam, of birth and death, is gone;
in the Saadh Sangat the inverted lotus (of the heart) has blossomed;
singing (God's) praises, (he has found) an abiding rest;
all (his) tasks have been fulfilled.
(His) body, so hard to obtain, has been approved (at the Lord's door);
it has borne fruit through repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Says Nanak, God has shown mercy (to me);
with every breath and every morsel (I) repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Hari. ॥4॥
1148.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He whose Name is the highest of all:
sing his praises for ever and ever;
remembering him, all pain departs,
and every comfort comes to dwell in the mind.
O mind, remember that True One;
in this world and the next you will attain release.
The all-pervading Being, the Stainless One, is the Creator;
(he) gives food to all beings and creatures;
in an instant (he) forgives millions of sins;
through loving devotion (he) ever carries (beings) across.
True wealth and true glory (are his),
(who) has received unwavering understanding from the perfect Guru.
He whom the Protector, in his grace, (protects):
all his darkness is dispelled.
(My) attention is fixed on the Supreme Lord,
who, free of all desire, wholly fills (all);
erasing (my) doubt and fear, Gopal has met (me);
the Guru has become merciful to Nanak. ॥4॥
1148.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He in whose remembrance there is light in the mind,
torments are erased, and one dwells in peace and Sahaj:
(his remembrance) comes to him alone to whom God (himself) gives (it);
(he) is granted the service of the perfect Guru.
O God, your Name is (the spring of) every peace;
O my mind, sing (it) at all hours.
(He) obtains whatever fruit he desires
(who) enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind.
Meditating on the Lord, (his) comings and goings cease,
fixing (his) attention on God with loving devotion.
Lust, anger and pride are destroyed;
the attachments and loves of Maya are broken;
(he) rests on God's support day and night,
(he) to whom the Supreme Lord gives (this) gift.
(O God, you are) the Master who does and causes all to be done;
you know the inner being of every heart.
In your grace, attach (me) to your service;
Nanak, (your) servant, is in your refuge. ॥4॥
1148.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He who does not repeat the Naam dies of shame;
lacking the Name, how can (he) sleep at ease?
Forsaking the Lord's remembrance, (he) wants the supreme state;
(but) without a root, how can there be branches?
O my mind, meditate on the Guru, Govind;
(he) washes off the filth of birth after birth, and cutting (your) bonds, unites (you) with the Lord.
Bathing at a tirath, how can the stone (of the heart) be clean?
the filth of Haumai clings to the mind.
Millions of rites are the root of bondage;
without the Lord's worship, (they are) a useless bundle (of straw).
Without eating, hunger is not appeased;
when the sickness goes, then the pains depart.
(Man) is caught up in lust, anger, greed and attachment;
(he) has not repeated (the Name of) the God who made (him).
Blessed, blessed are the Saadhs; blessed is the Lord's Name;
at all hours sing (his) Kirtan, (his) praises.
Blessed is the Lord's devotion, blessed the Creator;
Nanak (is) in the refuge of God, the infinite Being. ॥4॥
1149.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Guru has become fully pleased, (and all) fears have gone;
the Name of the Stainless One has been taken into the mind.
(God is) merciful to the meek, ever kind;
all entanglements have been destroyed.
(There are) peace, Sahaj and bliss in abundance;
in the Saadh Sangat fears and doubts are erased; the tongue utters the Amrit (Name) of the Lord, Har Har.
Love for the lotus feet (of the Lord) has taken hold;
in an instant the great ghost has been destroyed.
At all hours chant the chant of the Lord, Har Har;
Govind, the Guru, is himself the Protector.
(He) ever cherishes his own servant;
he watches over the breaths of his devotees.
Say, of what account is man?
(God) gives (his) hand and saves (his devotee) from Jam (himself).
Spotless is (his) glory, spotless (his) way of life,
(in whose) mind and heart the Supreme Lord has come to dwell.
In his grace the Guru has given (this) gift;
Nanak has found the treasure of the Naam. ॥4॥
1149.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My Guru is the Cause of creation, all-powerful;
(he) gives peace to soul and breath, (and is ever) near.
(He is) the Destroyer of fear, the imperishable King;
beholding the sight of him, all sorrow departs.
(O God,) wherever I look, (I see) your refuge;
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the True Guru's feet.
The divine Guru has met (me); (my) tasks are fulfilled;
(his) spotless service bestows every fruit.
Taking them by the hand, (he) has made his servants (his own),
(and) has given the Name of Ram a dwelling in (their) hearts.
(Theirs is) bliss forever, and no grief at all;
no pain, no suffering, no sickness afflicts (them).
(O God,) everything is yours; you are the Creator;
O Supreme Lord, O Guru, unreachable and boundless.
Spotless is the glory (of him to whom) the wondrous Bani,
(the praise) of the perfect Supreme Lord, is pleasing in the mind.
He pervades the water, the land and the sky;
O Nanak, everything comes about from God. ॥4॥
1149.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One whose) mind and body are dyed in love for Ram's feet:
(God) fulfils all (his) desires;
at all hours (he) sings (the praises of) the Lord;
the True Guru has given (him) the perfect mantra.
Most fortunate is he who loves the Naam;
in his company the world crosses over.
He alone is wise who remembers the One;
he is wealthy whose intellect discerns;
he is of noble family who remembers the Master;
he is honourable who recognises his own self.
By the Guru's grace he has attained the supreme state;
(he) has meditated on the virtues of Gopal day and night.
(His) bonds are broken, (his) hopes fulfilled;
the Lord's feet dwell in (his) heart.
Says Nanak, he whose fortune is perfect,
that servant has come to God's refuge.
(He is) pure himself, and has made all (others) pure;
with (his) tongue (he) has savoured (the Name of) Ram, the home of all delights. ॥4॥
1150.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeating the Naam, no obstacle at all stands in the way;
hearing the Naam, Jam runs off from afar;
repeating the Naam, all sorrows are destroyed;
repeating the Naam, (one) dwells at the Lord's feet.
Meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har: (it is) devotion free of obstacles;
sing the praises of the Lord with ever-growing delight.
Remembering the Lord, no evil eye can fall on (one);
remembering the Lord, neither demon nor god can touch (one);
remembering the Lord, attachment and pride do not bind (one);
remembering the Lord, (one) is not shut up in the wombs of births.
Every hour is the hour for the Lord's remembrance;
(yet) among many, only one remembers the Lord.
Of high caste or low, whatever servant repeats (the Name):
whoever repeats (it) attains release.
One should repeat the Lord's Name in the Saadh Sangat;
(there) the love of the Lord's Name is full.
O God, show mercy to Nanak;
O Lord, grant (me) to remember (you) with every breath. ॥4॥
1150.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) himself is the Shastra, himself the Veda;
he himself, (dwelling) in every heart, knows its secret.
He to whom all things belong is Light itself;
(he is) the Cause of creation, perfect, all-powerful.
O my mind, take hold of God's support.
Through the Guru, worship (his) lotus feet; no enemy and no sorrow comes near.
He himself is the forest and the blade of grass, the essence of the three worlds;
(he it is) on whose thread the world is strung.
He himself joins Shiv and Shakti together;
he himself is free of desire, and himself the enjoyer.
Wherever I look, there he is;
apart from him there is no other at all.
Through love of the Naam the ocean (of the world) is crossed;
Nanak sings (his) praises in the Saadh Sangat.
He in whose power are release, (the world's) enjoyments and the way (of life):
his servant lacks nothing at all.
Those with whom (God), in his grace, is well pleased:
O servant Nanak, those servants alone are blessed. ॥4॥
1150.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the minds of the devotees is the bliss of Gobind;
(they) have become steady, and every anxiety has left (them).
(Their) fears and doubts have been destroyed in an instant;
the Supreme Lord has come to dwell in (their) minds.
Ram, Ram is ever the helper of the Sants;
at home and abroad, the Supreme God is with (them); (he) pervades every place in full.
Gopal is (their) wealth, property, youth and way of life;
(he) ever sustains (their) soul and breath in peace.
Giving (him) his hand, (God) saves his servant,
and does not leave (his) side for even a moment; (he is) with (him) always.
There is no beloved like the Lord, no other at all;
that True One looks after (his own) with care.
Narayan is mother, father, son and kinsman;
from the beginning, from the start of the ages, the devotees have sung (his) praises.
In (their) minds is his support, the strength of God;
apart from the One, (for them) there is no other at all.
In Nanak's mind (too) is this strength:
our God brings (our) purpose to fulfilment. ॥4॥
1151.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering the Lord's Name, fear itself has been seized by fear;
every sickness of the three qualities is gone, and the servant's tasks are fulfilled.
The Lord's people ever sing (his) praises; they have found the abode of the Perfect One.
Even Dharam Raj, the king of the Jams, longs day and night for the sight of the servant, (that he may) be made pure.
Lust, anger, greed, intoxication, slander and pride are wiped out in the Saadh Sangat.
Such Sants are met by great good fortune; I, Nanak, am ever a sacrifice to them. ॥2॥
1151.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He who harbours the five (enemies) is a worshipper of five pirs;
each day he rises and speaks falsehood with (his) tongue;
(he) paints (sacred) marks (on his body) and practises hypocrisy;
(and) pines and wastes away within, like a widow.
Without the Lord's Name all is false.
Without the perfect Guru, release is not found; in the true court the Saakat is plundered.
He alone is unclean who does not know (the Lord's) creative power.
The Lord does not accept a plastered (cooking) place as purity.
(He whose) inside is filthy, (though he) washes the outside every day,
loses his honour in the true court.
(He) strives for the sake of Maya,
(but) never sets (his) foot on the straight (path).
Him who made (him) he does not bring to mind;
from (his) mouth he utters falsehood upon falsehood.
He on whom the Creator bestows grace:
his dealings are in the Saadh Sangat;
love for the Lord's Name and for devotion has taken hold (of him);
says Nanak, that servant suffers no break. ॥4॥
1151.3: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The whole world curses the slanderer;
the slanderer's dealings are false;
the slanderer's conduct is foul;
(but the Lord) is the protector of his servant.
The slanderer has died along with (his fellow) slanderer;
the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, has protected (his) servants; over the slanderer's head death has thundered.
No one believes what the slanderer says;
slanderers tell lies and (then) regret it;
(they) wring (their) hands and strike (their) heads on the ground;
God does not let the slanderer go.
The Lord's servant wishes no ill at all (on anyone);
(yet) pain strikes the slanderer like a spear.
Like a heron he keeps (his) wings spread;
(but when he) spoke with (his) mouth, then, being weighed, (he) was cast out.
The Creator himself knows every heart;
he whom the Lord makes (his) servant becomes steadfast.
The Lord's servant is (held) true in (his) court;
having reflected, servant Nanak has spoken this essence. ॥4॥
1152.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
With both hands joined I offer (my) prayer;
(my) soul, body and wealth are the capital (given) by him.
He alone is my Master, the Creator;
(to him) I am a sacrifice a million times.
The dust (of the feet) of the Saadh has made (me) pure;
remembering God, the mind's vices are wiped out, (and) the filth of birth after birth has been taken away.
He in whose house are all treasures,
by whose service honour is obtained,
(he) is the fulfiller of all desires,
(and) the support of the soul and breath of the devotees.
Within each and every heart (he) gives light to all;
repeating (the Name of) the treasure of virtues again and again, the devotees live.
He whose service does not go in vain:
meditate on that One within (your) mind and body.
By the Guru's teaching (come) compassion and contentment,
(and) the treasure of the Naam; this is a spotless thing.
(O God,) in your grace, attach (me) to the hem (of your robe),
(that) Nanak may ever meditate on (your) lotus feet. ॥4॥
1152.2: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My own True Guru has heard (my) prayer;
(my) whole task has come to good.
Within (my) mind and body (I) have meditated on God;
the perfect Guru has taken away all fear.
The divine Guru is the greatest of all, all-powerful;
by his service (I) obtain every comfort.
By whose doing all that happens comes about:
his command no one can erase.
The Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, is beyond compare;
the Guru, whose form bears fruit, is his very image.
He within whom the Lord's Name dwells:
whatever he sees is (to him) the knowledge of God.
He in whose mind the light is full, twenty parts in twenty:
within that servant the Supreme Lord dwells.
To that Guru (I) ever bow;
to that Guru (I) am ever a sacrifice.
Again and again (I) wash the True Guru's feet and drink (the water);
repeating (the Name of) the Guru again and again, I, Nanak, live forever. ॥4॥
1153.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 3, Partal, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O God, cherisher of all, merciful One, which of (your) virtues can I count?
Countless are (your) colours, many (your) waves; (you are) the Master of all.
(For you) there are countless (paths of) wisdom, countless meditations, countless chants, recitations and austerities;
countless reflect on (your) virtues and raise sweet strains; countless sages keep silence.
Countless sounds, countless instruments, countless delights at every moment (are of your making); hearing (your) praise, countless faults and countless diseases are wiped out.
O Nanak, in the service of the infinite divine Lord lie all the fruits and merits of (bathing at) the banks of tiraths, the six rites, fasts, worship, roaming the earth and making pilgrimages. ॥2॥
1153.2: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(One who) through reflection on the Guru's (word) recognises Ram in the self and the self in Ram,
has come to know the Amrit Bani through the Shabad; (he) has killed (his) Haumai, and cuts away (his) sorrows.
O Nanak, the diseases of Haumai are evil.
Wherever I look, there is this one pain; the Primal Lord himself forgives through the Shabad.
Those whom the Assayer himself has assayed are not pierced by the testing-needle again.
Those on whom (his) gracious glance fell, the Guru has united (with the Lord); he who is pleasing to God, he alone is true.
Air, water and fire are diseased; diseased is the earth with all its pleasures;
mother, father, Maya and the body: these are diseased; diseased are those bound in family ties.
Diseased are Brahma, Vishnu and Shiv; diseased is the whole world.
Recognising the Lord's state, they were set free, (they who) reflected on the Guru's Shabad.
Diseased are the seven seas with the rivers; the continents and the netherworlds are full of disease.
The Lord's people are at ease in the True One; in every place (he) casts (his) gracious glance (on them).
Diseased are those who wear the garbs of the six orders, and the countless men of hatha of every kind;
what can the poor Vedas and Kateb do? (People) do not understand the One alone.
He who eats sweet delicacies is filled with disease; in (living on) tubers and roots there is no peace (either).
(Those who,) forgetting the Naam, walk another path repent at the last moment.
(He who) wanders to tiraths is not rid of (his) disease; (what he) read has turned into dispute and wrangling.
The disease of double-mindedness is greater still; (through it one) has become dependent on Maya.
(He who), through the Guru, praises the True One by the Shabad, (with) the True One in (his) mind, is rid of (his) disease.
O Nanak, the Lord's servants, on whom by (his) grace the seal (of the Name) is set, are spotless night and day. ॥9॥
1154.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
That Creator has brought forth a wondrous play;
(he) has made the Anhad Bani, the Shabad, heard;
the manmukhs have gone astray, the Gurmukhs (he) has made to understand;
the Creator has ever been bringing about the cause (of it all).
The Guru's Shabad is within me; (on it is my) attention;
I will never give up the Lord's Name.
(His) father sent Prahlad to study;
taking (his) tablet, (Prahlad) came to the teacher.
(He said:) I will not study any rites or ways other than the Naam;
write (the Name of) Gobind, Murari, on my tablet.
The mother said to her son Prahlad:
Do not study what you are bent on; (so) she kept counselling (him).
(Prahlad said:) The fearless Giver, the dear Lord, is with me;
if (I) give up the Lord, then (my) family will be disgraced.
(The teachers said:) Prahlad has led all the pupils astray;
he does not listen to what we say, and sets his own affairs right;
(he) has instilled devotion in the whole city.
The assembly of the wicked has no power at all (over him).
Sanda and Marka raised a complaint;
all the demons strove in vain;
he himself preserves the honour of his devotees;
what can come of what a created being says?
By the joining of past deeds, the demon held sway as king;
(he) does not understand the Lord; he (the Creator) himself has led (him) astray.
(He) picked a quarrel with his son Prahlad;
the blind (demon) does not see that death has drawn near.
(He) kept Prahlad (shut) in a room and put a lock on the door;
(but) the fearless child is not afraid at all: within me is the Guru, Gopal.
He who is a created being and vies (with the Creator) has taken a (great) name though he is nothing;
what was written from the beginning came to pass: (he) picked a quarrel with the (Lord's) servant.
The father raised a mace against Prahlad:
Where is your Lord of the universe, your Gosain?
(Prahlad said:) The Life of the world, the Giver, is the friend at the end;
wherever I look, there (he) is pervading.
Tearing the pillar open, the Lord revealed himself;
(and) struck down the proud demon and destroyed him.
In the minds of the devotees there was bliss; rejoicing rang out;
(the Lord) gives glory to his servant.
(The Creator) has brought forth birth, death and attachment;
the Creator has written coming and going (into the lot of beings).
For Prahlad's sake the Lord revealed himself;
the devotees' word came to pass.
The hosts of the gods hail Lakshmi:
O mother, take away the form of Narsingh.
Lakshmi is afraid, and cannot go (near him);
Prahlad, the servant, came and clung to (the Lord's) feet.
The True Guru has fixed the treasure of the Naam firm (in the mind);
kingdom, wealth and all of Maya are false;
(yet) greedy men stay clinging (to it);
without the Lord's Name, punishment is met in the Lord's court.
Says Nanak, everyone does as (the Lord) makes (him) do;
they are accepted who have fixed (their) minds on the Lord.
(The Lord) has ever taken the side of his devotees;
the Creator has shown his own form. ॥13॥
1155.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(He who) through the Guru's service obtained the fruit of Amrit has quenched Haumai and craving;
the Lord's Name came to dwell in (his) heart and mind, (and his) desire merged in the mind itself.
O my beloved, dear Lord, bestow your grace (on me):
night and day (your) lowly servant begs for the Lord's virtues; through the Guru's Shabad (the Lord) saves (him).
Jam cannot even cast an eye on the Sants; not a trace of the heat of sorrow touches (them).
Those who (come to) your refuge cross over themselves, and carry all (their) families across.
You yourself preserve the honour of the devotees; this is your greatness;
(you) cut away (their) sins and sorrows of birth after birth; not a speck, not a mustard seed of double-mindedness (remains in them).
We, foolish and ignorant, understand nothing; you yourself grant understanding.
Whatever pleases you, that (a being) will do; nothing else can be done.
Creating the world, you set (it) to worldly toil; (it) has done evil deeds;
(it) has lost the treasure of this birth in a gamble, and has not gained awareness of the Shabad.
The manmukhs die; they perceive nothing; (in them is) the darkness of evil-mindedness and ignorance.
(they) never reach the far shore of the world-ocean; without the Guru, with the load (of sins) on (their) heads, (they) drowned and died.
The servants dyed in the True Shabad are true; the Lord God himself has united (them with himself).
Through the Shabad (they) have come to know the Guru's Bani, and stay with (their) minds fixed on the True One.
You yourself are spotless; spotless (too) are your servants, who reflect (on you) through the Guru's Shabad.
Nanak is ever a sacrifice to those who keep the Name of Ram enshrined in (their) hearts. ॥8॥
1155.2: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
He in whose heart is the Naam is the great king;
he in whose heart is the Naam has (his) tasks fulfilled;
he in whose heart is the Naam has gained millions in wealth;
without the Naam, life goes in vain.
(I) praise him whose capital is the wealth of the Lord;
most fortunate is he on whose forehead is the Guru's hand.
He in whose heart is the Naam has many forts and armies;
he in whose heart is the Naam has the ease of Sahaj;
he in whose heart is the Naam has become cool and calm;
without the Naam, life is cursed, (no better than) death.
He in whose heart is the Naam is liberated while living;
he in whose heart is the Naam knows every way (of living);
he in whose heart is the Naam has obtained the nine treasures;
without the Naam, (one) comes and goes, wandering in doubt.
He in whose heart is the Naam is free of all want;
he in whose heart is the Naam ever has profit;
he in whose heart is the Naam has a great family;
without the Naam, the manmukh is a fool.
He in whose heart is the Naam has a seat that never moves;
he in whose heart is the Naam dwells on a throne;
he in whose heart is the Naam is the true banker;
he who lacks the Naam has neither honour nor credit.
He in whose heart is the Naam is known among all;
he in whose heart is the Naam is (the image of) the all-pervading Being, the Creator;
he in whose heart is the Naam is the highest of all;
without the Naam, (one) wanders through countless wombs.
He in whose heart is the Naam has his work made known (everywhere);
he in whose heart is the Naam has had (his) darkness dispelled;
he in whose heart is the Naam is a man accepted (by the Lord);
without the Naam, there is coming and going again and again.
He has obtained the Naam on whom (God) has become merciful;
in the Saadh Sangat (he) has beheld Gopal;
(his) coming and going has ended; (he) has found peace;
says Nanak, (his) essence has been merged in the Essence (of the Lord). ॥8॥
1156.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(He who) has made millions of Vishnus as (his) incarnations,
whose places for dharma are millions of universes,
(who) created millions of Maheshes and took (them) back into (himself),
(and who) has set millions of Brahmas to fashioning the world:
such is our Master, Govind;
(I) cannot describe the expanse of (his) virtues.
Millions of Mayas serve as handmaids in his (house),
millions of beings are his couch;
(O God,) millions of creations are within your being;
millions of devotees dwell with the Lord.
Millions of canopied kings bow down;
millions of Indras stand at (his) door;
millions of Baikunths lie within his sight;
millions are the names of him whose worth is beyond reckoning.
At whose (door) millions of sounds resound,
millions (his) arenas, (where his) wondrous plays (go on);
millions of Shaktis and Shivs obey (his) command;
(he) gives support to millions of beings.
Millions of tiraths are at his feet;
millions are made pure by repeating (his) beautiful Name;
millions of worshippers perform (his) worship;
millions are (his) expanses; there is no other at all.
Millions of spotless swans (sing) his glory;
millions of the sons of Brahma sing his praise;
in an instant (he brings) millions of dissolutions and creations;
(O God,) your millions of virtues cannot be counted.
Millions of the wise expound (your) wisdom;
millions of meditators fix (their) meditation;
millions of great ascetics practise nothing but austerities;
millions of great sages abide in silence.
The unseen Master, the Lord beyond the reach of the senses,
pervades every heart; he knows every heart.
(O God,) wherever I look, you dwell;
the Guru has given Nanak this light. ॥8॥
1157.1: Raag Bhairao, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The True Guru has given me a gift;
(he) has given the Lord's Name, a priceless jewel.
(Now there are) endless delights and wonders of Sahaj;
without a care, God has met Nanak.
Says Nanak, the praise of the Lord is true;
again and again keep (your) mind absorbed in it.
Without a care, (God's) love has become my food;
without a care, the Name is repeated within me;
without a care, I am being saved through the Shabad;
without a care, my storehouses are full.
Without a care, my tasks are fulfilled;
without a care, my sorrows have lifted;
without a care, my enemies (have become) friends;
without a care, (I) have brought this mind under control.
The Carefree God has comforted me;
without a care, my hope is fulfilled;
without a care, the whole essence of truth (is) mine;
the Guru has given me the mantra (of the Name) of the Carefree One.
Without a care, my enmities have perished;
without a care, my darkness is dispelled;
without a care, Kirtan is sweet to the mind;
without a care, (I) have seen God in every heart.
Without a care, all (my) doubt is wiped out;
without a care, (God,) the home of peace, has come to dwell in the mind;
without a care, the Anhad (sound) plays within me;
without a care, Gobind thunders within me.
Without a care, my mind is content;
(I) have recognised the eternal Master, the Carefree One;
without a care, all discernment has welled up (in me);
without a care, the Lord's support, Har Har, has come to (my) hand.
The Carefree God wrote (my) destiny from the beginning;
without a care, the one God, the Master, has met (me);
all care has gone, without a care;
Nanak, Nanak, Nanak has become one with God. ॥8॥
1157.2: Raag Bhairao, the hymns of the Bhagats: Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
This wealth I have is the Lord's Name;
I neither tie it up in a knot nor sell it to live on.
The Naam is my field, the Naam my garden;
(O Lord,) I, your servant, practise devotion, (abiding) in your refuge.
The Naam is my wealth, the Naam my stock-in-trade;
leaving you aside, I know no other (stock).
The Naam is my kin, the Naam my brother;
at the end it is the Naam that stands by me as a friend.
He whom (the Lord) keeps detached within Maya,
says Kabir: I am his servant. ॥4॥
1157.3: Naked is the coming, naked the going;
no one will remain, be he king or chief.
For me, Ram the King is the nine treasures;
(but) for you, (O man,) it is love of property, wife and wealth.
(These) do not come along (at birth), nor go along (at death);
what of it, then, if elephants are tethered at the door?
The fortress of Lanka was of gold;
(yet) what did foolish Ravan take with him?
Says Kabir: give thought to some good (as well);
gamblers go off shaking out both hands (empty). ॥4॥
1158.1: Brahma is soiled, Indra is soiled;
the sun is soiled, and soiled is the moon.
This world is soiled and foul;
the one Lord alone is stainless, who has no end and no far shore.
Soiled are the lords of the universes;
soiled are night and day, and the thirty days (of the month).
Soiled is the pearl, soiled the diamond;
soiled are wind, fire and water.
Soiled are Shiv, Shankar and Mahesh;
soiled are the Siddhas, the seekers and the wearers of holy garbs.
Soiled are the yogis and the Jangams, matted hair and all;
soiled is the body, together with the soul (the swan).
Says Kabir: those people are accepted (at the Lord's door),
they alone are stainless, who know Ram. ॥6॥
1158.2: (O Mullah,) make your mind Mecca, and your body the qibla (the point one faces in prayer);
the One who speaks (within you), he is the supreme Guru.
Give the call to prayer, O Mullah, and say the namaz
in the one mosque that has ten doors (the body).
Make a sacrifice (bismil) of your dark nature (tamas), your doubt and the impurity of your mind;
eat up the five (enemies), and contentment will come.
the Hindu and the Turk (the Muslim) have one Master;
what can a Mullah do, and what a Sheikh?
Says Kabir: I have gone mad;
little by little (my) mind has merged in Sahaj. ॥4॥
1158.3: Joining the Ganga, a stream is spoiled;
(but) that stream becomes the Ganga, and its own self is gone.
Kabir is spoiled, calling out the Name of Ram;
he has become (one with) the True One, and goes nowhere else.
Growing beside the sandalwood, a tree is spoiled;
(but) that tree becomes sandalwood, and its own self is gone.
Touching the paaras, copper is spoiled;
(but) that copper becomes gold, and its own self is gone.
In the company of the Sants Kabir is spoiled;
(but) that Kabir has become one with Ram, and his own self is gone. ॥4॥
1158.4: (People put on) a mark on the forehead, a rosary in the hand, and a holy garb;
people have taken Ram for a toy.
If I am mad, then I am yours, O Ram;
what does the world know of my secret?
I pluck no leaves (as offerings), I worship no gods;
without devotion to Ram, (all) worship bears no fruit.
I worship the True Guru, and ever and always seek to please (him);
with such service, in the Lord's court I am at peace.
The world says Kabir has gone mad;
1158.5: Turning back (from Maya), I have put out of mind both caste and lineage;
my weaving is (now) in Sunn and Sahaj.
No quarrel of mine is left;
I have left both the Pandit and the Mullah.
Weaving and weaving, I clothe my own self;
where there is no self, there I stay and sing (the Lord's praises).
What the Pandits and the Mullahs have written down,
I have left behind and gone on; I have taken none of it.
With true love (ikhlas) in the heart, behold the Mir (the Lord);
O Kabir, (those who have met the Lord) have met (him) by searching and searching their own selves. ॥4॥
1159.1: No one gives the poor man respect;
(the poor man) may try in a hundred thousand ways, (but) he (the rich man) gives (him) no thought.
If a poor man goes to a rich man's (house),
(the rich man,) sitting before him, turns his back.
If a rich man goes to a poor man's (house),
(the poor man) gives (him) respect and calls him in.
Poor and rich are brothers, both of them;
the working of God's power cannot be undone.
Says Kabir: he alone is (truly) poor
in whose heart the Naam is not. ॥4॥
1159.2: (If) devotion is earned through service of the Guru,
then alone is this human body (counted as) gained.
The gods (too) yearn for this body;
with that body (now yours), take to the Lord's service.
Worship Gobind, and do not forget (him);
this alone is the gain of human birth.
While old age, (that) disease, has not yet come,
while death has not yet seized the body,
while the voice has not yet faltered,
worship Saringpani, O mind.
If you do not worship (him) now, when will you, O brother?
the end comes, and (then) worship cannot be done.
Whatever you would do, carry it out now;
(else) later you will repent, and not reach the far shore.
That one is the servant whom (the Lord) has set to serve (him);
he it is who has found the Stainless Lord.
Meeting the Guru, the doors (of his mind) have opened;
he does not come again on the road of births.
This is your chance, this your turn;
reflect and see within your own heart.
Says Kabir: win (this game) or lose (it);
I have told you in many ways, calling out again and again. ॥5॥
1159.3: In the city of Shiv (the auspicious Lord) dwells the finest understanding;
(then) understanding of this world and the next comes;
who, then, dies doing deeds of possessiveness?
My attention has settled on my own true state (nij pad);
the Name of Ram, the King, is my knowledge of God (Brahm Gyan).
At the root door I have set the lock (bandh);
above the sun I have held the moon fast;
at the western door the sun burns;
the Meru staff dwells above the head.
There is a slab that screens the western door;
above that slab is another window;
above the window, the Tenth Gate;
says Kabir: it has no end and no far shore. ॥3॥
1159.4: That one is a Mullah who fights his own mind,
who, by the Guru's teaching, grapples with death,
(and) crushes the pride of the Being of death (the Jam);
to that Mullah, my salaam always.
(God) is present here; why do you tell of him as far off?
Bind the brawling (passions), and find the Beautiful One.
That one is a Qazi who searches out his own body,
who kindles Brahm, (the divine) fire within the body,
who does not let his seed (bindu) fall, even in dreams:
that Qazi knows neither old age nor death.
That one is a Sultan who draws two arrows (to the bow),
brings back within (the mind) that runs outside,
(and) gathers his army in the Gagan Mandal (the Tenth Gate);
that Sultan bears the royal canopy over his head.
The yogi calls out, Gorakh, Gorakh;
the Hindu utters the Name of Ram;
the Muslim has his one Khuda;
(but) Kabir's Master pervades all. ॥4॥
1160.1: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
They who call a stone God:
their service goes for nothing.
He who falls at a stone's feet:
his toil is wasted.
Our Master ever speaks;
God gives his gifts to every being.
God is within, (but) the blind one does not know (him);
beguiled by doubt, he puts the noose (on himself).
The stone neither speaks nor gives anything;
(such) rites are empty, (such) service bears no fruit.
If one rubs sandalwood on a corpse,
say, what fruit does (the corpse) get from it?
If one rolls a corpse in filth,
what does the corpse lose by it?
Says Kabir: I say it aloud:
understand and see, O foolish Saakat:
in the love of another, many a home has been brought to ruin;
the devotees of Ram are ever at peace. ॥4॥
1160.2: The fish in the water are pierced by Maya;
the moths at the lamp are run through by Maya;
Maya, as lust, takes hold of the elephant;
snakes and bumblebees are worn away in Maya.
Such an enchantress is Maya, O brother,
that as many beings as there are, so many she leads astray.
Birds and the beasts of the wild are steeped in Maya;
sugar torments the fly sorely;
horses and camels are hemmed in by Maya;
the eighty-four Siddhas are at play in Maya.
The six celibates (jatis) are Maya's slaves;
(so are) the nine Naths, the sun and the moon;
ascetics and great rishis lie asleep in Maya;
in Maya are death and the five enemies.
Dogs and jackals are steeped in Maya;
monkeys, leopards and lions,
cats, sheep and foxes,
trees and roots: (all) lie in Maya.
The gods are soaked in Maya,
(and those of) the ocean, of Indra's realm and of the earth.
Says Kabir: whoever has a belly has Maya (upon him);
(one) is freed only when (one) has found the Saadh. ॥5॥
1160.3: As long as (one) keeps saying mine, mine,
so long not a single task (of his) comes to good.
When this mine, mine is wiped away,
then God comes and sets (his) task right.
Reflect on such wisdom, O mind:
why do you not remember the Lord, the destroyer of pain?
As long as the lion (of pride) lives in the forest,
so long the forest does not flower at all;
but the moment the jackal (of humility) devours the lion,
all the vegetation bursts into flower.
He who has won drowns; he who has lost swims across;
by the Guru's grace (he) crosses to the far shore.
Kabir, the servant, says, to make (it) plain:
keep your attention fixed on Ram alone. ॥3॥
1161.1: He who has seventy hundred commanders (salars),
whose prophets number one and a quarter lakh,
whose sheikhs are said to be eighty-eight crore,
and fifty-six crore his close attendants:
who will carry the plea of a poor man like me (to him)?
(his) court is far off; who can reach (his) palace?
The thirty-three crore (gods) are his household;
the eighty-four lakh (kinds of beings) wander about crazed;
(God) showed Baba Adam a little of his stern eye,
(and) even he kept paradise only a little while.
He in whose heart there is turmoil wears a yellow face;
forsaking the Kateb, he does the devil's work;
he finds fault with the world, (and) is angry at people,
(but) he reaps what he himself has done.
(O Lord,) you are the Giver, I am ever a beggar;
were I to answer (you) back, it would be a sin.
Kabir, your servant, has come into your shelter;
O Rahman (the Merciful), keep (me) near (you): (that is my) paradise. ॥4॥
1161.2: Everyone talks of going there (to Baikunth),
(but) I do not know where Baikunth is.
They have not known the secret of their own selves,
(yet) they describe Baikunth by talk alone.
As long as, O mind, (you) hope for Baikunth,
there is no dwelling at (the Lord's) feet.
(its) moat, fort, city and rampart (I do) not (know);
I do not know the gate of Baikunth.
Says Kabir: what more should one say now?
The Saadh Sangat is Baikunth itself. ॥4॥
1161.3: How is this mighty fortress to be taken, O brother?
(It has) a double wall and a triple moat.
the five (enemies), the twenty-five (principles), attachment, pride and envy (stand ready), with mighty Maya as (their) cover;
the strength of (your) poor servant does not reach (that far); what shall I do, O Raghurai?
Lust is the keeper of the doors, pain and pleasure the sentries, sin and virtue the gates;
anger, a mighty brawler, is the chief; and there the mind is king, in revolt.
Relish (of the senses) is (his) armour, possessiveness (his) helmet; he has strung the bow of evil intellect;
the arrows of craving stay (ready) within the heart: so the fortress cannot be taken.
(But) I made love the fuse and attention the rocket, and fired the shell of wisdom;
I lit the fire of Brahm in Sahaj, and with a single stroke (the fort) was won.
With truth and contentment I took up the fight, and broke down both gates;
through the Saadh Sangat and the Guru's grace I seized the king of the fort.
With the host of the Lord's devotees and the strength of Simran, I have cut the noose of the fear of death;
Kabir, the servant, has climbed atop the fort, and taken the kingdom that never perishes. ॥6॥
1162.1: Into Mother Ganga, deep and unfathomed,
(When) the mind does not waver, why should the body be afraid?
(my) mind remains absorbed in (the Lord's) lotus feet.
By a wave of the Ganga my chain was broken;
Kabir is seated on a deerskin.
Says Kabir: (I have) no companion and no friend;
in water and on land, Raghunath (the Lord) is the protector. ॥3॥
1162.2: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, an Ashtapadi of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(He who is attuned to the Name) makes his dwelling in a fortress unreachable, hard of approach,
in which the Light (of God) shines;
lightning flashes (there), and there is bliss,
where God, Bal Gobind (the Lord ever young), lies at rest.
(When) this soul is attuned to the Name of Ram,
old age and death are left behind, and doubt takes flight.
(Those) whose minds are fond of (the reckoning of) low caste and high
go on singing the songs of Haumai.
The Anhad Shabad rings out (there),
where God, Sri Gopal, lies at rest.
(He who) has fashioned the continents and the spheres, sphere upon sphere,
(and) who breaks down the three worlds and the three (qualities):
the Unreachable One, beyond the senses, dwells within the heart;
no one finds the far shore of the secret of Dharnidhar (the Support of the earth).
As fragrance shows itself in the plantain flower,
(as) pollen has made its home in the lotus,
(so) within the twelve-petalled heart (dwells) the mantra (of God),
where Sri Kamla Kant (Lakshmi's Lord) lies at rest.
Below and above, (God's) light meets the eye;
(he) gives light in the realm of Sunn;
there is no sun there, no moon;
(there) the primal Stainless One is in bliss.
The One who is in the universe, know that same One in the body;
bathe in the Mansarovar (of the Name);
he whose chant is Sohang,
on him neither virtue nor sin leaves a stain.
(For him) there is no low caste and no high, no sunshine and no shade;
(this) is found nowhere else but in the Guru's refuge.
(he) is not moved though one would move (him); he neither comes nor goes;
he remains merged in Sunn and Sahaj.
If anyone comes to know (God) within the mind,
he who speaks (his praise) becomes (that One) himself;
he who, through the mantra (of the Guru), makes the Light steady in the mind,
says Kabir: that mortal swims across. ॥8॥
1162.3: He at whose (door) millions of suns give light,
millions of Mahadevs (Shivs) and (their) Kailash mountains,
millions of Durgas massage his feet,
(and) millions of Brahmas recite the Vedas:
when I beg, (I beg) of Ram alone;
with any other god I have nothing to do.
Millions of moons light (his) lamps,
the thirty-three (crore) gods, all of them, eat of (his) food,
the nine planets, in their millions, stand in (his) court,
millions of Dharam Rajs are his door-keepers.
Millions of winds move about (his) upper chambers,
millions of Basak serpents spread (his) bed,
millions of oceans fetch his water,
millions of the eighteen loads (of all vegetation) are the hair (of his body).
Millions of Kamers (Kuber) fill (his) treasuries,
millions of Lakshmis deck themselves out (for him),
millions of sins and virtues keep looking to (him),
millions of Indras do him service.
Fifty-six crore (clouds) are his door-keepers,
flashing beyond measure over town after town;
the terrible one (Kali), her locks let loose, moves about (there);
Gopal plays with millions of powers.
Millions of sacrifices (are held) at his court,
millions of Gandharbs (the singers of the gods) hail his victory,
millions of branches of learning all tell of (his) virtues,
yet (none) finds the end of the Supreme Lord.
Millions of Bawans (Vaman, the dwarf incarnation) are the hair of his body,
by whom Ravan's army was outdone;
of whom thousands of crores of Puranas tell at length,
(and who) crushed Duryodhan's pride.
