Millions of Kandarps (gods of love) cannot match (his beauty),
they who steal the desires from deep within (all hearts).
Says Kabir: hear (me), O Saringpani,
grant (me) the state free of fear; this is the gift I beg. ॥8॥
1163.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O tongue, I would cut you into a hundred pieces
if you did not utter (the Name of) Sri Gobind.
O tongue, be dyed in the Lord's Name;
meditating on the Lord, Har Har, be dyed a lovely colour.
Futile is the tongue (given) to other tasks;
the Lord's Name alone is the nirban pad (the state free of desire).
Worship offered to countless millions of other (gods)
does not come up to the Name of the one Lord.
Namdev humbly prays: this is (my) task:
(to say,) your forms are endless, O Narayan. ॥4॥
1163.2: He who has given up others' wealth and others' wives:
Those who do not worship Narayan:
I do not (even) look upon them.
Those within whom there is a gap (between them and the Lord):
as beasts are, so are those men.
Namdev humbly prays: without a nose
(a man) does not look fine, (though he have all) thirty-two marks (of beauty). ॥3॥
1163.3: Milk in a bowl, water in a jug:
Nama milked the kapila (brown) cow and brought (the milk).
Drink the milk, O King Gobind;
drink the milk, (that) my mind may be content;
otherwise the father of the house will be angry (with me).
The golden bowl, filled with Amrit,
Nama took it and set it before the Lord.
(The Lord said:) This one devotee dwells in my heart;
Having given (the Lord) the milk to drink, the devotee went home;
(thus) Nama had the sight of the Lord. ॥4॥
1164.1: I am crazed (for him); Ram is my Husband;
for him I adorn myself with care upon care.
Let people slander (me) as they will, slander as they will, slander as they will;
(my) body and mind are (given over) to (my) beloved Ram.
One should not quarrel or wrangle with anyone;
with the tongue one should drink (the Name of) Ram, the home of all delights.
Now, knowing (him) in (my) soul, it has so come about
that I meet Gopal to the beat of the drum.
Whether a man praise (me) or slander (me),
Nama has met Sri Rang (the Lord) himself. ॥4॥
1164.2: Sometimes (one) does not care even for kheer, sugar and ghee;
sometimes (the Lord) has (him) beg for crusts from house to house;
sometimes he has (him) pick gram out of the rubbish.
As Ram keeps (us), so should one live, O brother;
the Lord's glory cannot be told in any way.
Sometimes he has (one) make fine steeds prance;
sometimes (one) has not even shoes for the feet.
Sometimes he lays (him) to sleep on a bed spread with white sheets;
sometimes (he) has not so much as straw on the ground (to lie on).
Says Namdev: the one Name alone saves;
the one whom the Guru meets, (the Name) carries him across. ॥4॥
1164.3: (O Lord,) I came to your temple, laughing and playing;
(but) as Nama worshipped, (they) seized (him) and made (him) rise.
Low is my caste, O King of the Yadavs;
why was I born into a calico printer's (home)?
Taking up (my) blanket, I turned and went,
and went and sat down behind the temple.
As Nama utters the Lord's praises,
the temple turns towards the Lord's humble devotee. ॥3॥
1164.4: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
As the hungry love grain,
as the thirsty have need of water,
as the fool is given over to his family,
such is Nama's love for Narayan.
Nama's love is fixed on Narayan;
naturally, in Sahaj, he has become detached.
As a woman is steeped in (love of) another man,
(as) the greedy man is fond of wealth,
(as) to the lustful man a woman is dear,
such is Nama's love for Murari.
That alone is (true) love which (the Lord) himself instils;
by the Guru's grace double-mindedness goes;
(that love) never breaks, (and one) stays merged (in him).
Nama has fixed (his) mind on the True Name.
As is the love of a child and (its) mother,
so is (my) mind steeped in the Lord.
Namdev humbly prays: (my) love has taken hold;
Gobind dwells in my mind. ॥4॥
1164.5: The blind (man) forsakes the wife of his home,
and carries on with another's woman.
As the parrot is delighted at the sight of the simbal (silk-cotton) tree,
(but) at the last dies clinging (to it).
The sinner's home is in fire;
it burns on and on, never quenched.
He does not go to see the Lord's worship;
leaving the road, he takes to the wrong way;
strayed from the Root (of all), he comes and goes;
throwing away Amrit, he loads up poison and eats it.
As when a courtesan's dance is held,
(the dancers) put on (fine) clothes and adorn themselves;
she keeps the full beat and minds her breath;
(yet) around her neck is the noose of Jam.
He on whose forehead (the Lord's) grace is written
runs to take the Guru's refuge.
in this way, O Sants, cross over. ॥4॥
1165.1: Sanda and Marka went and complained: (Prahlad) will not study; we have worn ourselves out (on him);
he says Ram and claps the beat with his hands; he has spoiled all the pupils.
He keeps repeating the Name of Ram,
and holds the remembrance of the dear Lord in his heart.
The chief queen pleads: the king has brought the whole earth under his sway;
(but) her son Prahlad does not heed her word; he has set his mind on something else.
The council of the wicked met and laid a plan: we shall put an end to his days;
(but) from the terrors of mountain, tree, water and fire Ram, the Sovereign Lord, kept (him), turning Maya's ways around.
Drawing his sword of death, (Harnakhash), afraid (at heart), flew into a rage: tell me, who is there to save you?
The Lord in yellow robes, the Master of the three worlds, speaks from within the pillar.
He who tore Harnakhash apart with his claws, and gave gods and men a Master to shelter them,
says Namdev: I meditate on (that) Narhari; Ram is the giver of the state free of fear. ॥5॥
1165.2: The Sultan asked: listen, you, Nama,
let me see the works of your Ram.
The Sultan had Nama bound (and said):
let me see your Lord, (your) Bithal.
Bring the slaughtered cow back to life,
or else I will cut off (your) neck right here.
(Nama said:) O king, how can such a thing be?
no one slaughtered comes back to life.
Nothing comes of my doing;
what Ram does, that alone will be.
The king rose up in his pride,
and goaded a huge elephant on (at Nama).
Nama's mother wept:
(son,) why do you not leave Ram and worship Khuda?
(Nama said:) I am not your child, nor are you my mother;
even if the body falls, (Nama) will still sing the Lord's praises.
The elephant struck with its trunk,
(but) Nama was saved in the Lord's shelter.
(The king said:) Qazis and Mullahs salute (me),
(but) this Hindu has crushed my pride.
(The people said:) O king, hear (our) plea:
take gold to the weight of Nama.
(The king said:) If I take the wealth, I shall fall into hell,
leaving the faith to hoard (the goods of) the world.
With fetters on (his) feet, keeping time with (his) hands,
Nama sang the praises of Gopal.
Even if the Ganga and the Jamuna flowed backwards,
Nama would still keep on uttering Hari.
When (Nama) heard that seven gharis had gone by,
the Master of the three worlds had still not come.
Then came the music of beating wings;
Gobind came, riding on Garur (the king of birds).
He took care of his own devotee;
Gopal came, riding on Garur.
(The Lord said:) If you say so, I will tilt the earth;
if you say so, I will lift it and turn it over.
If you say so, I will bring the dead cow to life,
(that) all may see it and believe.
Nama humbly asked: put the hobble (on the cow's legs);
the calf was let to her, and the cow was milked.
When the milking had filled the pitcher,
(Nama) took it and laid it before the king.
The king went off to his palace,
and a hard hour came upon (him).
Through the Qazis and Mullahs (the king) sent his plea: command (me);
forgive (me), O Hindu; I am your cow.
Nama said: hear, O king:
give me some assurance of this.
The measure of this assurance is this:
walk in truth and gentleness, O Sultan.
(Word of) Namdev spread everywhere;
all the Hindus went together to Nama.
(They said:) had the cow not come to life this time,
the trust in Namdev would have been lost.
Nama's fame endured in the world;
(Nama) crossed over, taking the humble devotees with him.
the slanderers had every grief and sorrow;
between Nama and Narayan there is no difference. ॥28॥
1166.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
If the divine Guru (is met), then Murari is met;
If the divine Guru (is met), then one crosses over;
If the divine Guru (is met), then one swims across to Baikunth;
If the divine Guru (is met), then one dies while still living.
True, true, true, true, true is the divine Guru;
all other service is false, false, false, false.
If the divine Guru (is met), then he makes the Naam firm (within);
If the divine Guru (is met), (the mind) does not run in the ten directions;
If the divine Guru (is met), (one stays) far from the five (enemies);
If the divine Guru (is met), one does not die in grief.
If the divine Guru (is met), then (one's) speech is Amrit;
If the divine Guru (is met), then (one tells) the story of the Ineffable (Lord);
If the divine Guru (is met), then the body (becomes as pure as) Amrit;
If the divine Guru (is met), (people) repeat the Naam.
If the divine Guru (is met), one has insight into the three worlds;
If the divine Guru (is met), one comes to understand the high state;
If the divine Guru (is met), then (one's) head is in the sky;
If the divine Guru (is met), there is acclaim for ever.
If the divine Guru (is met), one is ever detached;
If the divine Guru (is met), slander of others is given up;
If the divine Guru (is met), bad and good are one (to him);
If the divine Guru (is met), (good) destiny (shows) on the forehead.
If the divine Guru (is met), (no vice) plunders the body;
If the divine Guru (is met), the temple turns (to face the devotee);
If the divine Guru (is met), then the hut has been thatched;
If the divine Guru (is met), the bed has been brought out (of the river).
If the divine Guru (is met), then (one) has bathed at the sixty-eight (tiraths);
If the divine Guru (is met), the marks of (Vishnu's) discus have been set upon the body;
If the divine Guru (is met), then (one has done) the worship of the twelve (lingas of Shiv);
If the divine Guru (is met), all poison (turns to sweet) fruit.
If the divine Guru (is met), then doubt is broken;
If the divine Guru (is met), then one is freed from Jam;
If the divine Guru (is met), then one swims across the terrifying world-ocean;
If the divine Guru (is met), then one is not born (again) to die.
If the divine Guru (is met), (that is) the practice of the eighteen (Puranas);
If the divine Guru (is met), (that is the offering of) the eighteen loads.
Without the divine Guru there is no other place;
Namdev (is) in the Guru's refuge. ॥9॥
1167.1: Raag Bhairao, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Without seeing (him), no longing (for him) springs up;
(and) whatever is seen perishes.
He who repeats the Naam, along with (the Lord's) praise,
is the yogi; he alone is free of desire.
When anyone dwells on Ram, (his mind) is absorbed (in him);
he touches the paaras, and double-mindedness is no more.
He is a muni who devours the double-mindedness of the mind,
and is merged in the One who pervades the three worlds, who has no doors (of a body).
Everyone acts after the nature of his mind;
(but he who) becomes (one with) the Creator abides free of fear.
For the sake of fruit the plants come into flower;
when the fruit sets, then the flower falls away.
For the sake of knowledge deeds are practised;
when knowledge has come, there deeds come to an end.
For the sake of ghee the wise (woman) churns the curd;
(so the one who knows is) liberated while alive, ever free of desire.
Says Ravidas: (this is) the supreme detachment;
why do you not repeat Ram in (your) heart, O luckless one? ॥4॥
1167.2: Raag Bhairao, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Come, O Kalandar, O Keshav (of the beautiful hair),
(you) who have put on the garb of an Abdal.
(You,) who have made the sky the cap on (your) head, and the seven netherworlds (your) sandals:
(all) the skin-clad (beings) are your dwelling; thus are you arrayed, O Gopal.
Fifty-six crore (clouds) are your robe, sixteen thousand (worlds) your trousers;
the eighteen loads are your club, and the whole world your sahnak (a faqir's clay dish).
(My) body is the mosque, the mind the Maulana, who offers the namaz of Sahaj;
with Lady Kaula (Lakshmi) is your marriage, O Formless One, (Lord) of all that has form.
As I worshipped, (you) had my cymbals snatched away; to whom shall I cry out?
Nama's Master, the Inner-knower, roams through all the lands. ॥4॥
